A San Jose man accused of killing two people in separate attacks may be a serial killer, authorities warned, saying there could be more victims.

Marcelino Castro, 28, has been charged with two counts of murder after he allegedly confessed to killing two men and led police to their bodies in different locations along the Guadalupe River.

“Although there’s only two victims, it looks like the start of a possible serial killer case, and I’m grateful he turned himself in before he continued,” Deputy Santa Clara County District Attorney Michael Gadeberg told SFGATE Thursday.

Castro “flagged down” a San Jose police officer on September 19 and told authorities he had killed someone near Lelong Street and West Alma Avenue, police said in a news release. He then led officers to a body buried near the Guadalupe River by Tamien Station, according to a police report obtained by the outlet.

After officers found the first victim, Castro confessed to a second killing and led investigators to another body near the Guadalupe River Trail by Coleman Avenue and Autumn Parkway. The victim had been wrapped in a red tent and left in tall grass near the river, according to a police report obtained by SFGate.

Marcelino Castro, 28, allegedly admitted to police that he killed two people, and authorities believe there may be even more victims ( San Jose Police Department )

Authorities believe the first killing occurred September 13, while the second happened either September 15 or 16, Gadeberg said.

Neither victim has been publicly identified.

According to the police report, Castro told officers he knew the first victim and had gone with him to an area near Tamien Station to smoke methamphetamine. Castro allegedly attacked the man “without provocation,” strangling him and slitting his throat before digging a shallow grave and burying him.

Days later, Castro allegedly targeted a second man. He “lured” the man to an area near the Guadalupe River Trail by offering to smoke with him, prosecutors allege.

Castro allegedly strangled the man and hit him with a rock before wrapping his body in the red tent and leaving it in the tall grass.

“It appears that this man may have just had a compulsion to kill and he started with someone he knew and then progressed to a random stranger,” Gadeberg said.

Gadeberg said the second victim was found in an area frequented by runners, families visiting a nearby playground and people living in homeless encampments. He said the victims may have been unhoused, but that has not been confirmed.

“Those areas are frequented by homeless people, but our understanding is that the defendant lured them to those locations,” he said.

A motive for the killings has not been identified. Gadeberg said the case is unlike anything he has previously encountered.

“I’ve never seen anything like this. I’ve had a spree killer case and a number of double homicides, but I have never had something like this where there is no apparent connection or motive,” Gadeberg said.

The two killings are San Jose’s 20th and 21st homicides of 2026, police said in the news release.

News.title: Manchester City found guilty of 114 charges
News.content:
How did we get here?

How many rules were City alleged to have broken?

The Premier League statement in February 2023 said that “a number of alleged breaches” had been referred to an independent commission. It then detailed each specific rule against each season in which the alleged breach took place. The precise number was not clear from the statement and led to varying reports between 115 and 130. Friday’s news suggested the figure was 115.

How far does it all go back?

All the way to 2009-10, the first full season following the club’s takeover by Sheikh Mansour, who is a member of the Abu Dhabi Royal family and the vice president of the United Arab Emirates. There were charges relating to all 14 seasons until the Premier League completed their investigation during the 2022-23 campaign. In that time, City won seven Premier League titles, six League Cups, three FA Cups and the Champions League. They have since also won another league title – the first club to do so four times in a row – as well as the Uefa Super Cup, the Fifa Club World Cup and the FA Cup and League double last season.

Which rules were they accused of breaking?

They can be split into five groups. The biggest relates to the seasons from 2009-10 until 2017-18 and the requirement for clubs to provide accurate financial information and act in the utmost good faith.

The next set of rules concern the full disclosure of manager and player payments. The alleged manager breaches related to the period between 2009-10 and 2012-13, when Roberto Mancini was leading the team. The alleged breaches with respect to player payments relate to all of the seasons between 2010-11 and 2015-16.

As well as providing financial detail, clubs were required to meet Uefa and Premier League rules which were designed to bring a club’s spending broadly in line with its income by placing set limits on losses. City were charged with breaches of Uefa’s licencing and financial fair play rules from 2013-14 until 2017-18, and the Premier League’s profit and sustainability rules from 2015-16 until 2017-18.

The final set of charges spanned the five seasons during which Manchester City were being investigated by the Premier League and rules that require members to cooperate in the utmost good faith by providing information and documents.

Do we know exactly how they were accused of breaking these rules?

A full picture will only emerge when the commission publishes its findings but we know that the Premier League investigation began in December 2018 following allegations in the German newspaper Der Spiegel based on the Football Leaks documents. These included alleged payments to former manager Roberto Mancini for consultancy work at an Abu Dhabi-based club that was separate to his regular contract at Manchester City.

We also know that City were alleged to have breached rules over setting out image rights payments to players in their club contract. Der Spiegel reported that the Premier League investigation also focused on payments to underage players, as well as whether club sponsors were paying for commercial deals themselves or a significant proportion was in fact effectively coming from owner Sheikh Mansour.

What have Manchester City said?

Manchester City have always denied breaking any rules. In response to the Premier League statement about the alleged breaches, they said that they have “irrefutable evidence” to support their position and “look forward to this matter being put to rest once and for all.”

At the start of the hearing in September 2024, City manager Pep Guardiola also said: “Wait for the independent panel. We believe we have not done anything wrong.”

Of the Football Leaks documents, Manchester City said: “We will not be providing any comment on out-of-context materials. The attempt to damage the club’s reputation is organised and clear.”

News.title: This quiet Dyson fan proved itself during a heatwave
News.content:
What is the Dyson Purifier Cool PC1?

The Dyson Purifier Cool PC1 is one of the brand’s more straightforward fans. There’s no humidifying or heating here, just a focus on cooling and air purification.

True to Dyson’s design ethos, the Purifier Cool PC1 is bladeless, which makes it safe around kids and pets, and easy to clean. The tower fan uses the company’s renowned technology to project a smooth stream of air, with 10 speed settings and a 350-degree oscillation range that circulates air evenly throughout the room. It’s relatively compact and lightweight, too.

The remote control magnetically attaches to the top of the fan but you can also control the device using the MyDyson companion app.

While it doesn’t offer all the extras of Dyson’s more expensive air purifiers, it’s a solid option if you want reliable cooling without any fuss, which is why it’s our Best Buy Dyson fan.

JUMP TO:

I’ve been testing the Dyson Purifier Cool PC1 in my home office, a small-to-medium-sized room that felt more like a sauna than a workplace during the recent heatwaves. While I wasn’t precisely measuring its air purification qualities (you can find that review on our best Dyson fan round-up), the windows open onto a main road so I was able to test out its ability to handle a steady stream of traffic fumes, dust and general pollution drifting in.

I used the fan over several weeks to see how it performs on a day-to-day basis, assessing all of the usual metrics: how well it cools the room, how quiet it is during use, how intuitive the controls are and whether the design fits into a regular living or working space. And finally, as Dyson is known for its premium pricing, is the Purifier Cool PC1 worth the outlay?

News.title: Britain sends team to South Sudan as country braces for Ebola
News.content:
British Ebola specialists have been deployed to South Sudan because of fears the haemorrhagic fever will spread from neighbouring Congo.

A rare form of Ebola, known as the Bundibugyo species, is spreading rapidly in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), where more than 7,800 people have caught the virus since May, 3,700 of whom have died.

To prepare for the threat of imported cases, Britain has positioned three experts in and around the South Sudanese capital, Juba. They will assist and train local authorities on infection control, set up awareness campaigns for local communities, and test people crossing the border for the virus.

The team is employed by the UK Health Security Agency’s (UKHSA) Public Health Rapid Support Team (PHRST), which is regularly sent to the epicentre of disease outbreaks overseas – for instant the cruise ship at the centre of a deadly hantavirus in the South Atlantic earlier this year.

The current Ebola outbreak is the fastest-growing ever recorded and is on course to become the largest in history, overtaking the 2014-16 West Africa Ebola outbreak, in which around 30,000 people contracted the haemorrhagic fever and roughly a third died.

Experts fear it is only a matter of time before the virus spreads to South Sudan, which shares a 500-mile border with the DRC. Thousands of people cross the frontier each day to work, attend school and trade goods, mostly fish, in lucrative markets between the two countries.

If the virus gained a foothold in South Sudan, which became the newest country on earth after severing ties with Khartoum in 2011, experts fear the consequences would be catastrophic and worsen an already dire humanitarian situation.

“It’s so variable as to where the outbreak is spreading at the moment, there are cases from some of the border towns [with South Sudan],” Ed Newman, director of the PHRST, told The Telegraph.

“There’s a feeling [Ebola could spread] any day. Maybe you could say we’ve been lucky so far,” Mr Newman said, on the sidelines of a UKHSA conference in Manchester.

News.title: Russell capitalises on Antonelli error to take Azerbaijan GP pole
News.content:
Russell – who begins the weekend 81 points behind the Italian – simply has to capitalise. And he really should do. Even if Antonelli hadn’t crashed out, he has looked on a different level this weekend, dominating practice and qualifying. Russell topped Q1, Q3 and Q3, securing the 12th pole of his career with a lap which was nine tenths quicker than his best lap in Q2 and eight tenths quicker than Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc, the next fastest driver. He could hardly believe it himself.

“That was a pretty decent lap,” he told his team over the radio on his cooldown lap. “How much was [the gap]?”

“Just over eight tenths to Leclerc.” came the response. “Woah!”

This has not been the easiest season for Russell, who began the year the overwhelming favourite for the title, having dominated his younger team-mate over the course of last season. So he could be forgiven for feeling proud of having done such a good job.

“It’s been a while so it definitely feels good,” he admitted. “This was probably the biggest pole margin of my whole career, including my F2 and F3 days.

“The lap felt really sweet, car’s been feeling really great this weekend. On a track like this where you can hug it, it feels amazing.”

News.title: Buttler injury derails England chase and sends Sri Lanka series to decider
News.content:
Enter Buttler to play a wonderful counter-attack, whacking Wellalage for four and six and dumping leg-spinner Sachindu Colombage over the rope twice as he raced to 41 off 22 balls.

Buttler was at a crossroads after the T20 World Cup in February. Despite England making the semi-finals, he averaged just 10 in the tournament to complete a third poor World Cup in a row. A break with his family, and a very good Indian Premier League, where he made a crucial technical correction, changed his fortunes.

Matthew Hayden, the batting coach at the Gujarat Titans, asked him whether he was watching the ball closely enough. Buttler discovered that, now 36, he is a right-eye dominant batsman, so with Hayden’s help he opened up his stance to give himself a better view of the ball. A summer rich in runs has followed with an average of 51 for England and a strut back in his body language. The injury has surely ended Buttler’s summer and there are worries that he could be out of the Pakistan ODI triangular tournament next month as well, just to add to the night’s woes.

This was not a vintage England performance. Atkinson made a crucial error on the boundary, dropping a straightforward chance off Kusal Mendis on 17. It kickstarted Mendis, who went on the charge smashing 51 in 24 balls. He put on 137 in 120 balls with Kuminda Mendis. Josh Tongue had an off day going at seven an over and Jofra Archer was given similar treatment, although he bowled better than figures suggest, as anything wayward with pace on the ball was hit away.

Overton was more effective with his cutters and slower balls, while Ahmed did at least bag a couple of wickets, credit for keeping his head after some early rough treatment. Kusal Mendis was given out leg before on 99 but overturned the decision and stroked a four next ball for a deserved hundred.

News.title: Oil jumps after Saudi thwarts missile attack
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. A global rout in bond markets deepened overnight as traders expect the US to keep raising interest rates.

Japan’s 10-year bond yield surged to 3.08pc on Thursday, its highest level since 1996, as markets responded to stronger than expected US economic data and higher oil prices.

It followed sharp rises in the US on Wednesday, when the yield on 10-year Treasuries – a benchmark of global borrowing costs – surged as high as 5.12pc, up from 4.96pc. It was the biggest jump since the “liberation day” tariff turmoil in April last year.

Bonds were sent into turmoil as traders bet that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates three times by April next year in an effort to bring down inflation. Money markets suggest there is a 70pc chance of the Fed following this month’s first rate rise in three years with a second in October.

This followed closely watched industry data on Wednesday, known as PMIs, showed US private sector activity jumped unexpectedly to a five-year high in September.

Meanwhile, oil prices spiked 3.9pc on Wednesday to move back above $100 a barrel, risking an inflationary spiral in the world economy.

Jim Reid, an analyst at Deutsche Bank, said: “The main driver was a strong batch of PMIs, along with a rebound in oil prices, which both led to mounting speculation about faster rate hikes.” Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) US borrowing costs hit highest since 2007 on fears economy overheating | Yield on 10-year Treasuries soars amid inflation concerns as oil prices rise

2) Diesel prices surge as Trump mulls 90-day US export ban | Pump prices could exceed £3 per litre in Britain if Washington imposes ‘catastrophic’ block on exports

3) England’s first new reservoir in 30 years delayed despite drought warnings | Havant Thicket, in Hampshire, will now be completed in 2034, five years after initially planned

4) Timpson customers ask for extra belt holes after weight-loss jabs | Boss of key cutting chain credits Ozempic and Mounjaro after surge in requests

5) Chinese carmaker’s new EV battery will charge in under five minutes | Geely says its latest system is fastest in industry as brands approach ‘physical limit’

What happened overnight

Debt markets were in turmoil after Japanese bond yields hit 30-year highs.

As Tokyo markets reopened after a three-day holiday, the benchmark 10-year Japanese government bond yield jumped to its highest level since 1996.

This came after a steep sell-off in the US market overnight. Oil prices remained around $103 a barrel and the dollar held gains after Tehran’s leader vowed to never surrender following a warning by Donald Trump that he could “annihilate” Iran.

Japan’s benchmark stock market, the Nikkei 225 rose 1pc to 65,645.10, as some chipmakers got a boost from the recent interest in AI. Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 fell 0.7pc to 8,702.00.

Hong Kong’s Hang Seng lost 0.3pc to 24,762.39, while the Shanghai Composite dipped 0.9pc to 4,545.09. Trading was closed in South Korea for the Chuseok autumn harvest holiday.

News.title: Zelensky lashes out at EU
News.content:
Volodymyr Zelensky lashed out at the European Union over its moves to weaken sanctions on Russian oligarchs.

In his address to the UN General Assembly, the Ukrainian leader warned that beyond making life “more comfortable” for Russians, “it also gives the war more time for Putin to send poor people into the kill zone. So Russia’s revenues must remain a target.”

His criticism came after France and Luxembourg successfully pushed for sanctions exemptions for Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman, Russian oligarchs, on Tuesday.

Kyiv branded the decision “shameful and unjustifiable”. The men are known to share close ties to Vladimir Putin and have net worths of $14bn and $16bn, respectively.

In his fourth address to the UN as a wartime leader, Mr Zelensky said it was paramount that the international community increased pressure on the Kremlin to stop “the madness” of the war spreading.

Under pressure from Donald Trump to halt attacks on Russian energy targets, Mr Zelensky defended his country’s aerial offensive for successfully depriving Putin of revenue for his war.

“When someone gives Russia more money through trade, they give this war more time. And that is exactly why we insist on limiting trade with the aggressor, and why we are burning Russia’s revenues ourselves,” he said.

‘End the war before winter’

Washington has recently attempted to revive the long-stalled negotiations between Ukraine and Russia. On Tuesday, Mr Zelensky implored Mr Trump to help Kyiv end the war “before winter”.

Mr Trump appeared optimistic, suggesting an agreement would happen “more quickly than people understand”.

Sergei Lavrov, the Russian foreign minister, told the UN Security Council on Wednesday that Russia was prepared to negotiate for a lasting peace but would not “pause the war”.

Mr Zelensky sought to remind world leaders that the conflict was not constrained within Ukraine’s borders at a time when the global community was distracted by a myriad of conflicts and crises.

Citing the support of Iran and North Korea for Russia, he warned that Putin’s war kept “spreading further”.

“Putin is always looking for someone who can help him kill more, kill more people for every kilometre of land, take more territory and take another country instead of simply stopping and running his own country,” Mr Zelensky said at the UN.

He noted that fighters from at least 47 countries were helping to prosecute Moscow’s war against Ukraine and urged leaders to prevent their citizens from being dragged into the conflict.

After Mr Zelensky’s address, reports emerged that Kirill Dmitriev, Putin’s envoy, was on his way to the US where he would meet Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, the Trump administration representatives.

Sources told Reuters that the meeting would take place in New ‌York on the sidelines of the UN summit.

Marco Rubio, the US secretary of state, also confirmed Mr Trump had invited his Russian counterpart to attend the G20 summit of world leaders in Miami in December.

News.title: Male contraceptives could hit pharmacies in ‘three to five years’, says WHO
News.content:
Game-changing contraceptives for men could be on pharmacy shelves as soon as 2029, according to the World Health Organization.

Speaking to the Telegraph, Dr James Kiarie, head of the UN agency’s contraception and fertility care unit, said he expects male birth control to be available in just a few years, in a major expansion of contraceptive options for men.

“In three to five years, we will actually have a method available, [so] men can be more than supporters of their female partners in using contraception – men can actually be users,” he said.

On Tuesday, the WHO released its first Target Product Profiles (TPPs) for these products, setting out guidelines for the desired and minimum standards any male contraceptive product must meet.

“[The TPPs] signals that this is a priority issue for the WHO,” said Dr Kiarie.

“Currently men do not have much option in terms of their contraceptive methods. They have to either use condoms… [or] they have to use withdrawal, which has a high failure rate, or they have to use vasectomy, which is a permanent method.”

At the moment, the most advanced new product is called NES/T. It is a daily hormonal gel that is applied to the shoulders and upper arms, and suppresses sperm production without affecting testosterone levels.

Other candidates include injectable hydrogels that block sperm travel, an approach that has been described as a “reversible vasectomy”. ADAM, developed by Contraline, is in phase 1 trials while Next Life Sciences is set to trial a similar product called Plan A.

A third option is YCT-529 – the first non-hormonal, daily male birth control pill. It is currently in phase 1b and 2a clinical trials.

Dr Kiarie said it was important to have multiple options as “there’s no one size fits all” approach, but warned development could take longer than five years if clinical trials face unexpected hurdles.

Sports.title: 'In his prime!' Can Purdy lead 49ers to Super Bowl contention?
Sports.content:
There isn't a more unusual or more fluctuating expectation spectrum than that of Brock Purdy, who has seen to the San Francisco 49ers flying out of the blocks through two weeks of the NFL season.

He entered the league devoid of pressure or projections as Mr Irrelevant. Not long after he was tasked with leading perennial Super Bowl contention for the 49ers. Football onlookers have since been fiercely divided on where he stands among the NFL's premier quarterbacks. Was it the Kyle Shanahan system and the star-studded cast? Or is he just good? It is allowed to be both.

It comes with the asterisk of premature two-week conclusions territory, but Purdy is playing as well as any quarterback in football right now.

He enters week three with the highest completion percentage in the league at 80.4 having completed 45 of 56 passes for 492 yards and five touchdowns at 8.8 yards per attempt.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Atlanta Falcons at Green Bay Packers from Week 3 of the NFL season.

"We're starting to witness Brock's prime, and I think it's going to be a sight to behold," said 49ers offensive tackle Trent Williams.

"I've always loved Brock, but I think he's starting to get his respect now. He doesn't even relish in it. It's all about next week, going 1-0, and that's why he's a great leader."

Purdy doesn't earn acclaim for being one of the league's most athletic or dynamic out-of-structure two-way killers, but instead thrives on high-level processing, field diagnosis, anticipation and accuracy. It should also be said he is a far better scrambler than he gets credit for.

The best of what Purdy represents came in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Miami Dolphins on a precision-perfect strike to Mike Evans, the 49ers quarterback moving one defender with a pump-fake before sliding left and threading a stunning off-platform bullet to his new wide receiver. Evans had run what began as a crossing route before momentarily adjusting into a corner break, Purdy picking him out with expert touch and timing to execute on a flood concept.

Twice Purdy has threatened one of the great underdog stories in NFL history. He famously guided the 49ers to the NFC Championship Game as a rookie after being selected with the 262nd and final pick of the Draft, only to suffer an elbow injury in the first quarter as Josh Johnson replaced him in a 31-7 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. He went one better the next season by taking San Francisco to Super Bowl LVIII, where they were beaten in overtime by the Kansas City Chiefs.

The system quarterback label has overshadowed him at times, while others have underlined his success in a scheme others have been unable to execute at such a high level. His 49ers have meanwhile been as unlucky with marquee injuries as any team in the league, as much hampering Shanahan's offense in recent years as they seek to work their way back to Super Bowl territory.

He now has a healthy Christian McCaffrey, a healthy George Kittle and, perhaps for the first time in his career, a proven elite veteran receiver in Mike Evans.

Sports.title: Russell claims Azerbaijan GP pole as Antonelli crashes
Sports.content:
George Russell claimed a dominant pole position for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix as championship leader Kimi Antonelli crashed in Q1 and will start 16th.

Russell had been in superb form throughout the three practice sessions and continued his mighty speed in Q3 to beat Ferrari's Charles Leclerc by eighth tenths of a second.

Antonelli clipped the inside wall into Turn 1 in Q1 and was told to stop the car in the middle sector, despite his efforts to carry on and get back to the pit lane.

"I turned in and had a lot more front end compared to the lap before and I touched the wall," explained Antonelli, whose perfect Q3 appearance record in 2026 came to an end.

"So mistake from my side. Very unnecessary. To be fair, I'm very mad about it and will try to do better tomorrow."

It means Russell has a big opportunity to make significant inroads into his 81-point deficit to Antonelli when the lights go out on Saturday at 12pm (build-up from 10.30am), live on Sky Sports F1 and Sky Sports Main Event.

"It's probably the biggest margin of my whole career, even including F2 and F3 days," said Russell, who has not won since June's Austrian Grand Prix.

"The lap felt really sweet. The car has been feeling great this weekend and on a track like this when you can hook it up like that it feels really amazing.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli hits the wall during Q1 at the Azerbaijan GP

McLaren's Oscar Piastri qualified third, his best result since the Hungarian Grand Prix at the end of July, while Red Bull's Isack Hadjar was fourth on his return from a wrist injury, having missed the last three race weekends.

Max Verstappen looked to be a genuine pole threat to Russell but was caught out by yellow flags which Lando Norris caused after locking up into Turn 3 on the last Q3 runs.

Norris will still start fifth but Verstappen is only eighth, behind Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton in sixth and Alpine's Pierre Gasly in seventh.

Williams reached Q3 for the first time this season after Carlos Sainz qualified ninth, making the most of their major upgrade package which has cut all of their excess weight, while Alpine's Franco Colapinto was 10th.

2) Charles Leclerc, Ferrari

6) Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari



7) Pierre Gasly, Alpine

Russell takes full advantage of Antonelli mistake

Russell had topped both of Thursday's practice sessions but the field closed up in final practice on Friday morning with Verstappen topping the session.

It felt like Mercedes were still favourites going into qualifying, but not by a big margin, and Q1 and Q2 underlined that as Russell topped both segments but was being pushed hard by Verstappen.

Due to the lack of high-speed corners, most teams apart from McLaren unusually ran the same set of tyres for the whole of Q3 to bring them into a better operating window.

Piastri took provisional pole after the first runs before Russell went quicker by half a second, then found even more pace on his last flying lap to set an unbeatable 1:42.526 which nobody came close to threatening.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Craig Slater breaks down the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, including why the race takes place on a Saturday, while doing his best Craig David impression!

Leclerc, a four-time Baku pole-sitter, qualified second but was still 0.837s behind while Piastri and Hadjar largely maximised what they had underneath them to get onto the second row.

Norris pushed too hard and went deep into the run-off area at Turn 3, which also compromised Verstappen's lap but Russell's remarkable speed would have been tough even for Antonelli to beat.

"It has been a while so definitely feels good. It's probably the biggest margin of my whole career, even including F2 and F3 days," said Russell.

"The lap felt really sweet. The car has been feeling great this weekend and on a track like this when you can hook it up like that it feels really amazing.

"It was just the perfect lap at the end. I was in a good gap behind to Hadjar, which gave me a nice little slipstream probably by another tenth or two down this backstraight, so it was great."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli was left frustrated after an 'unnecessary' crash which ended his qualifying early at the Azerbaijan GP

Antonelli has made very few mistakes this season but on a weekend Mercedes clearly have the best car, he simply misjudged the amount of grip available and caught the inside wall which immediately damaged the track rod between his left front tyre and the car.

Just three weeks ago, Antonelli remarkably won from 19th at the Italian Grand Prix but Monza is the easiest track on the calendar to overtake at.

While you can overtake around Baku, the field spreads out more due to the successive slow-speed corners so Antonelli is unlikely to repeat his Italian heroics on Saturday.

Russell told Sky Sports F1: "I'm feeling good but there are some fast drivers around.

"Kimi has started lower down the order in some races this year and finished on the top step, so I wont take anything for granted."

Sports.title: Will Littler defend World Grand Prix title? Humphries, Price, Smith in the mix
Sports.content:
Will Luke Littler successfully defend his World Grand Prix title? Can Luke Humphries, Gerwyn Price, James Wade or Ross Smith trouble the world No 1 in the unique double-in, double-out format?

Littler will be hoping the home crowd at Leicester's Mattioli Arena is more welcoming after the two-time world champion was booed and whistled at during the World Series of Darts Finals exit in Amsterdam earlier this month.

The 19-year-old headed into the tournament chasing a historic clean sweep after winning the first six major titles of the season but suffered a crushing 10-4 defeat to Jonny Clayton in the last eight.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on Love The Darts, Paul Nicholson backed Littler's reduced schedule for the rest of the season

Stephen Bunting backed Littler, saying he has "changed" darts since bursting onto the scene a few years ago.

"It's really hard, isn't it? Obviously, Luke is the best player in the world. For whatever reason, the crowd got on his back, they didn't want him to do the [clean sweep]," said Bunting.

"He was probably on edge, anyway, going into [the tournament]. Maybe in Germany, in Belgium, I've had it a few times where the crowd has whistled out.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mark Webster and Michael Bridge discuss Littler's concerns over crowd whistling at the World Series of Darts in Amsterdam

"If you let the crowd know they're getting to you, it can be 10 times worse. It's a hard one to say, but I don't like the whistling. I'd rather have someone shouting abuse at me than whistling.

"It's a horrible noise to hear when you're trying to concentrate. But I understand it'll keep happening, no matter how much we talk about it.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Stephen Bunting says Littler has 'changed' darts since bursting onto the scene a few years ago

"Punishments need to be brought in, maybe. Until that happens, it'll keep happening."

Littler takes on Luke Woodhouse in the first round and if he wins he will go on to play either Nathan Aspinall or Kevin Doets in round two.

Humphries under pressure?

Image: Humphries has been back on the practice board in preparation for the World Grand Prix

Luke Humphries lost the World Grand Prix final two years ago but 'Cool Hand Luke' must at least match that run this time, otherwise he will surrender second place in the world rankings to Gian van Veen.

The former world champion opens his campaign against Dave Chisnall, with a potential second-round showdown against Chris Dobey or Jermaine Wattimena.

Humphries, who suffered a shock defeat to Mike De Decker in the 2024 final, only returned to competitive action at the end of August for the first time since his shock round-one exit to Cameron Menzies in the World Matchplay on July 20 and went on to win Players Championship 28 before defeat to Littler in the final of the Czech Open.

Humphries said: "I'm going to get back on the practice board at home as much as I can now and I'm going to dedicate the rest of the year to trying to be my best and trying to push Luke - and not just Luke, but everyone else because I want to stay at No 2.

"Whether that happens or not, I'm going to fight for it because I'm going to try my best."

"Wadey this year, last year even, he's just someone that you just can't really bet against," Polly James said on the Love The Darts podcast. "His scoring power, his doubling, just everything. And when it's on and he's in a good mood up for it, he could easily win this."

Paul Nicholson added: "What's he going to do next? Win the Worlds? We've talked about how the fact he's never going to win that. Well, maybe he could now."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on Love The Darts, Smith feels he is ready to play in the Premier League

Smith, who told Love The Darts he feels ready to play in the Premier League, has appeared in two major finals and has won both after winning the recent World Series of Darts Finals to add to his European Championship in 2022.

Nicholson, nicknamed 'The Asset', advised former trucker Smith to "stay energised" and "stay sharp" and "keep believing" as he prepares to face Cameron Menzies in the opening round of the World Grand Prix.

"When he wins in Amsterdam, it's not an accident because he's one of the best players in the world right now," said Nicholson. "He's doing a lot right."

What about Price and MVG?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking ahead of the upcoming World Grand Prix, Paul Nicholson questions whether Michael van Gerwen will ever find his best form again

Gerwyn Price will be looking to end a four-year wait for another major crown at the same tournament where he had last lifted one.

Meanwhile, six-time World Grand Prix winner Michael van Gerwen is a player who is struggling for form having recently suffered a first-round exit at the World Series of Darts Finals.

Speaking ahead of Van Gerwen upcoming World Grand Prix game with Ryan Joyce, Nicholson questioned whether he will ever find his best form again.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the 2022 World Grand Prix final which saw Van Gerwen win his sixth title despite a spirited fightback from Nathan Aspinall

"As he slips down the rankings, we should say, 'you're not finished'. He has people in his corner but what are you going to do about it? Ultimately it's up to him. The definition of a comeback is what you do on the stage in moments and those moments are fewer than before."

Other players to watch out for are Wessel Nijman, who is enjoying an outstanding season, already winning four Players Championship titles and two Euro Tour titles, and fellow Dutchman Kevin Doets - who is one of the names every player hopes to avoid in the draw - including his first-round opponent Nathan Aspinall.

Sports.title: Chepstow’s jumps opener to feature no chase races after dry summer
Sports.content:
Chepstow's Welsh Racing Festival, the traditional jumps season opener, will be run without chase races as the track continues to feel the effect of an extreme summer drought.

The three-day meeting staged between October 9-11, all live on Sky Sports Racing, is at the centre of a major fixture reshuffle in response to a prolonged dry period which has left the ground unseasonably dry and hard.

A total of 19 hurdle races and two national hunt flat races will be run across the meeting, with Hereford also reduced to an all-hurdle card on October 13.

Chepstow's high-class chase races will instead move to Ffos Las on October 14 as part of an all-chase card, while Worcester also now hosts an all-chase meeting on October 12.

Ben Cook, ARC Racing Director, said: "We are obviously disappointed to have to make these changes to the DragonBet Welsh Racing Festival at Chepstow, but we wanted to make and announce the decision as early as possible.



"The racecourse team have been working incredibly hard over the course of the summer, and into the autumn, to get both of Chepstow's jumps tracks ready for this meeting. We have simply been beaten by the weather, as far as the chase course is concerned.



"Chepstow received 63mm of rain in late August, which made a significant positive impact on the track, alongside the irrigation that the team have been undertaking.

"The track has received only 43mm of rain in September however, with none in the last ten days. This has stalled that progress and meant that the chase course will simply not have sufficient ease in the ground."

Sports.title: Weekend Winners: Kate, Sam and Declan have their say on the Cambridgeshire
Sports.content:
Ahead of another fun-filled Saturday with quality racing, the Weekend Winners team discussed their best bets for the feature Handicap.

The panel of Kate Tracey, Sam Boswell and Declan Rix paid special attention to Newmarket's feature Handicap, the bet365 Cambridgeshire.

With a field of 27 set to go to post, John Gosden looks to enhance his excellent record in the Cambridgeshire, now working alongside his son Thady, their leading light Gavriel heads the market in their pursuit of a record-extending sixth success in the race.

Attheraces.com Declan Rix…

"I'm going to side with the five-year-old Hand Of God who was second to the well handicapped Raamee. Don't be afraid of horses towards the top of the handicap in this race with class coming to the fore in recent years.

"He looks like he is enjoying his racing at the minute having gone a little cold last year. This nine-furlong distance is perfect for him as they go hard throughout. I think he's a nice bet at a double figure price."

Host Kate Tracey…

"This race sees the return of Tracey's Trends, this race shows you need to be a four-year-old, rated bet 102-109 and drawn low. The horse that comes out on top with these is the Alan King trained Alcarath.

"He wears the first time cheekpieces which shows sign of intent and you need a prominent runner in this style of race with the winners of previous year. The draw has completely switched in the last few years and the favourites in the race are drawn badly."

BetVictor's Sam Boswell…

"I don't match any of Kate's trends and I'm clutching at straws in this competitive handicap. The pace looks spread across the field and wanted a horse that is towards the front. I landed on Spanish Voice who loves the course and distance.

"He's been well fancied on starts on the turf but slightly disappointed recently but this trip should be in his remit and I think he could go very well for Oisin Murphy who is looking clutch Billy back in the Jockeys' title."

Sports.title: Manchester City guilty of almost all Premier League charges, according to reports – live news and reaction
Sports.content:
2m ago 10.23 EDT Further background via the Press Association: “City were referred to the commission in February 2023, at a time when they were en route to the third of four consecutive Premier League titles. “The investigation which ultimately resulted in more than 100 charges being laid started back in 2018. City had been charged with failing to report accurate financial information for nine seasons stretching from 2009-10 to 2017-18, as well as failing to provide full details of former manager Roberto Mancini’s pay between 2009-10 and 2012-13. “They were also charged with failing to provide full details of remuneration in contracts with players between 2010-11 and 2015-16, and with failing to co-operate with the investigation over a period from 2018 to 2023. “The club said at the time the charges were laid that they welcomed the opportunity for a commission “to impartially consider the comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence that exists in support of our position”. Four months after the charge was issued, the club won the Champions League for the first time in their history. The commission hearing began on September 16, 2024.” Share

9m ago 10.17 EDT Via The Athletic’s David Ornstein, Manchester City have said this: “The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the club’s statement of February 2023. The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair minded regulator, free from partisan influence.” A similar statement has run on The Times. Much more to follow … much more. Share Updated at 10.18 EDT

16m ago 10.10 EDT Manchester City 'guilty' of Premier League charges Good afternoon, and there’s highly significant breaking news, with reports widely emerging that Manchester City have been found guilty of all but one charge of more than 100 breaches of Premier League regulations, though no details of any sanctions have emerged. The expectation is the club will appeal. The club were charged in February 2023. Share

39m ago 09.46 EDT Kane: World Cup hurt takes a long time to fully get over Harry Kane was also asked how he gets over the pain of not winning the World Cup: double quotation mark It’s not easy to get over but you don’t have a choice. I think it is something that isn’t spoken about a lot but when you are in that bubble and in that environment for seven weeks in the same routine, highest pressure, biggest games and then you go out and all of a sudden you are back to reality. Being a husband, being a father, you have been away from your family a lot so that takes an element of that away. It’s still there but you get back to normal life and enjoy being with your kids and they are the most importnant thing and they help you get over it. But it takes months, it takes a long time to fully get over it. You heal while you are moving on. There are still moments I think about it and I am sure the team think about what could have been, what if, especially meeting up again here and wearing the badge, it stays in your mind. I think that is where tomorrow comes into it, the quicker you can put in good performances [the better] especially against bigger teams. So I think it is a good thing we are playing against Spain and Croatia and these top teams because if you do win those games I think it brings you back to the excitement of what is to come. Can we win the Nations League? Can we win the Euros in a couple of years? So I think tomorrow is important in terms of momentum. Share

That isn’t to say you can’t take things from other teams like probably club football you do as well. But ultimately it is about being England and showing our identity, especially in the bigger games as well. Share

I think so far in my career it is the best chance without a doubt. I spoke quite openly last season was my best from a personal point of view, it was my best year without a doubt. From a team point of view it was my best year in terms of trophies and performances. It’s something that would be amazing to win. I know there has been a lot of talk about it and I am sure there will be over the next month until it is announced. That is part of it. I would be extremely proud to win it. I did a lot of great things I can be proud of last year but ultimately it is down to other people now. Share

1h ago 09.22 EDT Tuchel: Palmer misses too many camps Thomas Tuchel was also asked about Cole Palmer, who withdrew from England camp. double quotation mark My understanding is he plays with discomfort and pain and he cannot compete on the highest level with discomfort and pain so he withdrew and informed us. Chelsea informed us, that is my understanding. We are not managing load. When I was in club football I often used the term international break, this is when you hear it on the other side totally different picture. This is not an international break and I think that is what we created now. It is a competitive environment but it is also an environment that players love to be in. They love to train with each other and be with each other. That is what togetherness and brotherhood looks like. That is what we created from last September. We will never compromise on that. We will never let this creep in that players don’t want to come. It is fair enough but we focus on the guys who absolutely want to play for England. For sure it is a missed opportunity and and it’s another opportunity, he misses too many opportunities. I don’t blame him for it, it is just a fact. He misses way too many camps with injuries. I only want to rely on what I personally witness and what I see within my team. If you are not in camp there is a next level to impress that you cannot achieve because you can only actually do it when you are with me on the pitch and with us on the pitch. Share

The door is always open and you have to make sure to be available and produce top level performances in camp and if you do so that counts for something. Right now there is nothing to do. It is not on my list of worries. I am not wired like this. It is what it is. From the moment I arrive at SJP [St James’ Park] my full focus is on the staff and players. That is how I am wired. There is not threat, there is no distrust and there is no threat of consequence. It will come naturally. I think we have the opposite, everyone is desperate to come. You talk to our captain who has the most minutes in club and country who is happy to be here while some teammates of him are enjoying a seven or two day break but he wants to be here. Wales, who fly to Copenhagen on Saturday, lost their Nations League opener after Joao Felix scored the only goal in Lisbon. Koumas, who started the game on the left flank, spurned a golden chance to equalise late on but Bellamy was impressed by the 21-year-old. “I was looking at him and I thought he was outstanding,” Bellamy said. “I was thinking: he belongs here, he belongs here. You don’t always pick up on the intensity – if you pay £140m for a player, you’re paying for his running level as well as his ability. 5h ago 05.38 EDT Pablo Iglesias Maurer US men’s national team head coach Mauricio Pochettino says he regrets not being “more involved” in the situation surrounding US forward Folarin Balogun at this summer’s World Cup. Balogun was given a red card after a challenge against Bosnia and Herzegovina defender Tarik Muharemović, which by rule is accompanied with a one-game suspension. Balogun’s ban for the next game against Belgium was suspended after the US Soccer Federation and US president Donald Trump lobbied Fifa, with Trump saying that he personally placed a call to Fifa president Gianni Infantino to ask the ruling be reviewed. 6h ago 04.31 EDT The Premier League, Bundesliga, La Liga and Serie A have issued a joint statement calling for reform at Fifa. In a rare coordinated move, the leagues have criticised the Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, making reference to his abandoned World Cup sell-off plan – the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme – and the Folarin Balogun affair.



The four leagues have taken aim at Fifa’s “relentless expansionism” and said leagues, together with national associations, clubs, and players, need a greater role in decision-making.



“Football’s longstanding foundations have, in recent years, been threatened by a fundamental governance problem, whereby Fifa’s president has actively promoted exploitative ideas rather than safeguarding against them,” the statement said. “And while football’s stakeholders ultimately forced the withdrawal of the Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme, the conditions that led to FFE remain.



“The Fifa president has now acknowledged the need for reform, but it is not enough for surface-level, process changes to be explored in the aftermath of FFE – fundamental governance reform is essential to restore clear constitutional boundaries within Fifa, including confidence that individual disciplinary matters remain demonstrably insulated from political interference.” Share
