Sports.title: Man City's 115 charges timeline: The German bombshell that raised suspicions, overturning a UEFA ban and going to war with the Premier League - now, the bombshell verdict is FINALLY in
Sports.content:
Manchester City have finally learned their fate with the Premier League finding the club guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought against them in early 2023.

It has been a two-and-a-half-year legal battle with Premier League chiefs, but the whole affair dates much further back after they were also investigated by UEFA.

Mail Sport's MIKE KEEGAN gives a full timeline of how City's case played out.

THE GERMANS DROP THE BOMB

In 2018, German publication Der Spiegel dropped a series of bombshell articles based on a tranche of emails obtained by subsequently convicted Portuguese hacker Rui Pinto, which they claimed showed Manchester City had been effectively cheating by using a variety of underhand techniques to swerve both Premier League and UEFA rules on financial fair play.

The first, explosive piece, claimed City executives suggested £59.5m of sponsorship money from Abu Dhabi-based Etihad Airways, the club’s shirt and stadium partners, had in fact been paid by the Abu Dhabi United Group, the investment group led by City owner Sheikh Mansour, with just £8m paid by the airline.

With the pin on the grenade removed, another story followed hot on its heels.

Roberto Mancini, it was alleged, had signed a £1.45m a year deal with the club when he took over as City manager in 2009 but had also picked up £1.75m a year for four days’ work as a consultant for Abu Dhabi side Al Jazira, which is also owned by Sheikh Mansour.

Other potentially-damaging claims followed, including an allegation that City officials had been backdating sponsorship deals with Abu Dhabi-based partners.

German publication Der Spiegel claimed Man City had been effectively cheating by swerving UEFA and the Premier League's financial rules under owner Sheikh Mansour (pictured)

Der Spiegel also claimed Roberto Mancini received a separate payment for four days' work as a consultant on top of his Man City salary after being appointed the club's manager in 2009

WHY WAS THIS A PROBLEM?

To UEFA, and officials at Premier League rivals, this was evidence of a flagrant breach of a system of rules which all clubs had signed up to.

The suspicion was that, following their takeover by Sheikh Mansour’s group in 2008, City had been finding ways to pay players and coaching staff more than others and that the moves had been key to their era of success.

In 2019 both UEFA and the Premier League launched investigations.

AN ‘ORGANISED AND CLEAR ATTEMPT’ TO SMEAR US

While they did not challenge the authenticity of the emails, a clearly outraged City described the claims as ‘entirely false’.

In a terse statement, they said: ‘We will not be providing any comment on out of context materials purported to have been hacked or stolen from City Football Group and Manchester City personnel and associated people. The attempt to damage the Club’s reputation is organized and clear.’

UEFA WIN THE BATTLE, CITY WIN THE WAR

UEFA went first and saw off an attempt by City at the Court of Arbitration for Sport to get their investigation thrown out. In February 2020 they banned City from the Champions League for two years and fined them 30m euros, finding them guilty of ‘serious breaches’ of their rules.

City said they were ‘disappointed but not surprised’ and immediately appealed to CAS. With Lord Pannick KC leading a team of expensive lawyers, their appeal emerged successful, with the ban overturned.

Two of three judges found most of the alleged breaches were either ‘not established or time-barred’. The ban was thrown out, and the fine reduced to 10m euros for non-compliance.

City’s lawyers defended a lack of co-operation by claiming they should not be forced to address detail contained in emails that were effectively stolen.

UEFA - fronted by president Aleksander Ceferin (pictured) - banned City from the Champions League for two years in 2020 for 'serious breaches' of their rules

Man City got the ban overturned upon appeal, with Lord Pannick KC (pictured) leading their team of expensive lawyers

DER SPEIGEL STRIKE AGAIN

After City had tried and failed to get the Premier League probe thrown out at CAS, Der Spiegel went again.

In April 2022 they published Mancini’s contracts, along with new claims around image rights payments to former captain Yaya Toure and a contract between ADUG and an off-shore firm owned by the player’s then-agent.

THE PREMIER LEAGUE CHARGES

In February 2023 the Premier League announced that City had been hit with 115 charges and the number stuck. However, the figure – as they subsequently corrected – was actually 130.

Of those, 54 were charges of ‘failure to provide accurate and up-to-date financial information’ while there were 14 charges of ‘failure to provide accurate financial reports for player and manager compensation’. Both sets related to alleged offences between 2009 and 2018 (2009-2018).

There were also five charges of ‘failure to comply with UEFA’s regulations, including Financial Fair Play Regulations’ and seven charges of breaching the Premier League’s profit and sustainability regulations (PSR) between 2015 and 2018.

There were also 35 counts of failure to co-operate with Premier League investigations between 2018 and 2023. Similar to the UEFA charges, the more serious allegations could be split into two categories.

City were basically accused of falsely inflating sponsorship deals (in an attempt to pump more money into the club and circumvent financial rules), and of making payments via third parties to players and coaches to top up their salaries (and again get around the system). Unlike UEFA, there is no time-barring period at play.

Over the period involved, post-ADUG takeover, City have become the most successful club in the country, landing eight Premier League titles, three FA Cups, six League Cups and a treble which included a first Champions League triumph in 2023.

The Premier League - fronted by chief executive Richard Masters (pictured) - hit City with 115 charges in February 2023. The number was later corrected to 130

Later that season, City won the Treble as they lifted the European Cup for the first time

Pep Guardiola has always maintained City's innocence, and famously said 'I am not moving from this seat' after the club were hit with the charges in 2023

CITY GO TO WAR

In June last year, with the investigation ongoing, City went nuclear. The champions launched legal action against the Premier League over its rules on sponsorship deals with parties linked to the ownerships of clubs (strengthened following the Saudi takeover of Newcastle) after its own proposed new agreement with Etihad was blocked.

The Associated Party Transaction (APT) rules represented a ‘tyranny of the majority’ they claimed, as part of an attempt by the established elite to protect themselves. City won, with the tribunal ruling the regulations, in play from 2021 to 2024, were unlawful and void. The league and its clubs, ironically including City, face a legal bill running to tens of millions.

New, replacement rules, the introduction of which City strongly warned against, are now also subject to a legal challenge. While the two cases are not related, Pannick and Paul Harris KC – key in City’s 115 fight – were behind their victory on APTs and were hoping for a repeat.

THE HEARING AND THE LONG WAIT

The hearing into the 130 alleged breaches began last September at London’s International Dispute Resolution Centre. The Premier League also spared no expense, enlisting KCs Adam Lewis and Andrew Hunter to take its case.

With so much at stake, speculation over the outcome has been feverish. Indeed, Mail Sport revealed that Sky Sports had taken the unprecedented step of warning pundits not to jump to conclusions should the verdict drop when they are on air.

That verdict, at last, is now in.

CITY FOUND GUILTY

On Friday September 25 2026, the verdict was in: Manchester City guilty of 114 breaches of Premier League rules.

The bombshell decision sent the football world into bedlam, while it is inevitable that City will launch an appeal.

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel raps Cole Palmer for 'missing way too many camps': Three Lions boss says he wants to 'focus on the guys who absolutely want to play for England'
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel raps Cole Palmer for 'missing way too many camps': Three Lions boss says he wants to 'focus on the guys who absolutely want to play for England'

England manager Thomas Tuchel has admitted Cole Palmer misses 'too many' Three Lions camps after the Chelsea midfielder pulled out of the latest squad.

Palmer withdrew from the squad on Monday morning despite playing in all five of Chelsea's Premier League matches so far, with it understood he is monitoring a minor injury.

England are due to face 2026 World Cup winners Spain first, before two games against Czechia and another v Croatia.

Tuchel did not take Palmer to the World Cup after his last subpar season with Chelsea, and, speaking at Wembley Stadium after announcing his squad for this break, said the player should have 'a point to prove'.

'My understanding is he plays with discomfort and pain and cannot compete at the highest level with discomfort and pain so he withdrew and informed us and Chelsea informed us,' Tuchel said on Friday. 'We are not managing load.

'When I was in club football I used the term of an international break. When you hear it on the other side, it's a totally different picture. It's not an international break, and I think that's what we created now. It is a competitive environment, where the players love to be, they love to train and be with each other, that's what togetherness and brotherhood looks like and that's what we created.

England manager Thomas Tuchel (right) has berated Cole Palmer (left) for missing 'too many camps' with the Three Lions

'We will never compromise on that. We will never let this creep in that we have the feeling players don't want to come. It's fair enough, but we will focus on the guys who absolutely want to play for England.

'For sure it is another missed opportunity. He misses too many opportunities. And I don't blame him for it, it's just the fact he misses way too many camps with injuries and I only want to rely on what I personally witness and what I see with my team, and for that you have to be in camp. If you are not in camp, there is a next level to impress that you cannot achieve because you can only do it when you are with me on the pitch. It is a missed opportunity.'

Despite sources describing Palmer as having a muscular issue, him pulling out of England duty is bound to spark a debate surrounding club v country. The news of his impending withdrawal led to immediate criticism.

His decision comes after Tuchel had issued the 24-year-old with a stern warning upon recalling him to the squad last week.

Tuchel said: 'It is one thing to be nominated, like with Cole, and getting your ticket back in the squad but it's another thing to perform for England.

'Cole needs to step up when he comes and he needs to show these kind of numbers to get his place, keep his shirt and justify the nomination.'

He added: 'So now it is a new competition. Some players, some positions, have more injuries. Some have less injuries. Cole has his starts that he always had but he has his numbers back - he has his assists back, he has decisive goals back - so that is why he is in the squad.

'I think he has a point to prove, and the same goes for Trent (Alexander-Arnold). He was never off the list. He was never non-selectable for us, and it is his chance to show, come to camp and be the best version of himself.'

Palmer has four goals and two assists in seven games this season after struggling during the last campaign through injury.

He battled thigh and hamstring problems as he returned 11 goals and three assists in 34 games, revealing on a live stream last week: 'I had one leg for 10 months, f***ing hell, what do you want me to do?'

Declan Rice, Kobbie Mainoo, Tino Livramento and Marcus Rashford have also withdrawn from the squad.

Sports.title: George Russell's World Championship hopes given major boost with Azerbaijan pole position - while Kimi Antonelli CRASHES out of qualifying
Sports.content:
George Russell's World Championship hopes given major boost with Azerbaijan pole position - while Kimi Antonelli CRASHES out of qualifying

George Russell’s slender world championship hopes were given a major boost when title favourite Kimi Antonelli crashed out of qualifying for Saturday’s Azerbaijan Grand Prix – and he took pole by a mile.

Antonelli badly misjudged the first corner around Baku’s tight ribbon of street track, hitting the wall on the inside and puncturing his front left tyre. He will start Saturday’s race from 16th place.

Russell, on the other hand, was a massive eight-tenths of a second ahead of Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc in second place and Oscar Piastri third for McLaren.

The 20-year-old Antonelli has been imperious this season, almost blemish-free, and leads his Mercedes team-mate Russell by 81 points with 14 rounds of the 23-race season gone.

Antonelli and his race engineer Peter Bonnington discussed how to deal with the smash in the first section of qualifying.

Bonnington told him: ‘We just better park up, mate. We’re not going to be able to fix that.’

George Russell took pole position at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix in a major boost to his World Championship host

Kimi Antonelli crashed out of qualifying, but he is still 81 points ahead of his team-mate

Antonelli: ‘Are you sure?’

Bonnington: ‘Affirm. Stop in a safe place.'

Antonelli: ‘Let me try, mate. Let me try.'

Bonnington: ‘We just better park up, mate. We’re not going to be able to fix that.’ And that is what happened, the instruction followed after Antonelli’s forlorn hopes to resuscitate his afternoon saw his limping car condemned to stop. He was later seen disconsolately seated behind a catchfence.

‘I'm sorry guys. My God,’ he had said.

Bonnington, who has nurtured Antonelli since the Italian arrived at Mercedes as a rookie last year with the daunting task of replacing Lewis Hamilton, replied: ‘No sweat, Kimi.’

Russell, who was strong all weekend, duly claimed his first pole since the Austrian race at the end of June – a grand prix he won, one of his two victories this season alongside Australia, compared to Antonelli’s eight.

But in Baku, both talent and fortune have favoured Russell. He has mastered the circuit, while Antonelli sat out much of Friday’s practice with a hydraulic problem, putting him on the back foot.

Antonelli is disappointed, but he drove from 19th to victory in Monza at the beginning of the month, so he could still salvage this Grand Prix

However, beware George! Antonelli drove from 19th in Monza at the beginning of the month to victory, albeit with a new engine and its extra grunt. And Russell needs to take lumps, not snips, out of his younger team-mate’s lead if he is going to wrest the title away from him.

But this was a major boost for the Briton – the margin of his pole immense. Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar, meanwhile, will start from fourth on the grid for Red Bull, Lando Norris fifth for McLaren and Lewis Hamilton sixth for Ferrari.

A rare bad day for Max Verstappen, who will start eighth in this race which has been moved forward 24 hours to accommodate Azerbaijan’s Remembrance Day on Sunday.

‘It’s been a while and it feels good,’ said Russell. ‘It’s the biggest margin of my career in any formula. It was the perfect lap in the end.’

Sports.title: The next 007? Tennis star Carlos Alcaraz channels James Bond in a sharp tuxedo as he returns to London after missing Wimbledon
Sports.content:
The next 007? Tennis star Carlos Alcaraz channels James Bond in a sharp tuxedo as he returns to London after missing Wimbledon

Tennis sensation Carlos Alcaraz channelled his inner James Bond on Thursday night as he donned a black tuxedo at an event in London.

The 23-year-old Spaniard returned to the capital for the Opening Night Gala ahead of the 2026 Laver Cup, and spoke to reporters at the O2 Arena following his US Open campaign.

There, he reached the quarter-final before losing to home favourite Ben Shelton, with the game finishing at 3.30am local time – the latest ever finish to a game at the tournament.

He found himself throwing up in a towel at his first tournament since a four-month absence from tennis due to a wrist injury, but dusted himself down on Thursday to attend the event in London - the scene of the Wimbledon tournament he missed this year.

'With the breaks I cannot plan them in advance,' Alcaraz told Sky at the event. 'It depends how I feel mentally and physically.

'The tennis calendar has been super tight. There are more important tournaments and even more Masters 1000 events over two weeks, so it's pretty long. You have to be focused from the first day until the last, plus all the Grand Slams and everything else so it depends on how many matches I've been playing.

Carlos Alcaraz channelled his inner James Bond as he attended the Opening Night Gala for the Laver Cup

The 23-year-old posed in a tuxedo after returning to action at the US Open following a wrist injury that kept him out for four months

The likes of Arthur Fery (left) and Alexander Zverev (fourth left) will also be involved

'If I'm injured or mentally a bit down I'm going to need those breaks. I realise it will be better to take it before getting injured.'

Alcaraz took in the attention as he carried out some Bond-style poses, including making a gun sign with his hand.

He will be representing Team Europe at the tournament, but may have his sights on a new career in acting after his appearance in the capital.

'You expose yourself in every tournament, but not only when you go on the court, it's every time you go out for dinner,' he continued. 'The people who stop you, the people rolling with the cameras.

'Sometimes that is hard to deal with when you expose yourself at that level. Mentally, it's hard to deal with. That's why sometimes I have to stay at home alone or with my close people around.

'Home is my peace. When I can chill and be myself. With my friends and family.'

The Laver Cup will take place at the O2 from Friday to Sunday, with Team Europe also including US Open champion Alexander Zverev and former world No2 Casper Ruud.

Team World, meanwhile, includes the likes of Taylor Fritz, Alex De Minaur and Brandon Nakashima.

Brit Arthur Fery has been included as an alternate in the European team.

Sports.title: Ex-Tottenham Hotspur and Newcastle United star Sebastien Bassong is accused of 'dodging £7 Tube fare with expired travelcard'
Sports.content:
Ex-Tottenham Hotspur and Newcastle United star Sebastien Bassong is accused of 'dodging £7 Tube fare with expired travelcard'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Former Tottenham Hotspur star Sebastien Bassong has been accused of dodging a £7 Tube fare after allegedly using an invalid travel pass and following another passenger through a London Underground barrier, it has been reported.

The ex-Premier League defender, who also played for Newcastle United, is allegedly being prosecuted by Transport for London (TfL) after a revenue officer stopped him on the network.

Bassong, 40, has insisted he did not realise the pass he had been given was not valid, telling The Sun that he had been handed the card by somebody else.

'I didn't know about the prosecution and I haven't received a letter. I was using a card given to me, and I was stopped, and I didn't know it wasn't good enough. I use the Tube every day. I'm a good citizen.'

The case centres on an alleged incident in which Bassong is said to have attempted to use an Oyster card before entering the compulsory ticket area without a valid ticket.

In a witness statement, TfL employee Adebukola Anifowose said: 'I observed Mr Bassong pretend to tap an Oyster card enclosed in a white wallet before tailgating through the wide-aisle gate behind another male.

'When requested to produce the card used at the barrier, Mr Bassong presented a Transport for London Staff Nominee Pass without the required accompanying photocard.

'System checks later confirmed that the pass did not belong to him and had last been used in October 2025.'

Sebastien Bassong pictured after scoring for Tottenham Hotspur against Liverpool in 2009

The witness said checks established that the pass had been registered to an acquaintance.

Mr Anifowose added: 'No valid ticket was shown for being in the compulsory ticket area. The fare avoided was £7.'

Bassong, who lives in north London, was reportedly required to respond to the charge by September 15 but has failed to do so.

The allegations come years after Bassong made a name for himself in the Premier League, having moved to Newcastle from French club Metz in 2008.

He moved to Tottenham the following year in a deal reported at the time to be worth £8million and became part of the Spurs side that qualified for the Champions League.

The Cameroon international scored on his Tottenham debut against Liverpool and later netted in the club's Champions League qualifying victory over Swiss team Young Boys.

Bassong made 71 appearances for Tottenham before leaving for Norwich City in 2012.

He also spent time on loan at Wolves and Watford before establishing himself at Norwich, where he spent five years and captained the Canaries.

Bassong later joined Peterborough United in 2018 before moving to Greek side Volos, where his playing career ended later that year.

His career included 19 appearances for Cameroon, and he has since worked as a football pundit.

The Daily Mail has approached Bassong for further comment. TfL declined to comment.

Sports.title: Israel footballer pleads his innocence as he's sent off for 'GUN GESTURE' celebration - but rules show he could have seen red for removing the corner flag!
Sports.content:
An Israeli footballer who was sent off while playing for his country after performing a gun gesture pleaded his innocence – with his manager fighting his corner too.

Sayed Abu Farchi was given his marching orders in the second-half of his side's defeat by Austria, having taken the corner flag out the ground and mimicked a gunshot, though others have suggested he could have been imitating a snooker shot.

Fans were left stunned and judged the move to be in bad taste, given Israel are at war with Palestine, with more than 70,000 people killed by Israeli attacks to date.

Abu Farchi protested with Bulgarian official Georgi Kabakov at the time, insisting he should have stayed on the field.

But he was already on a yellow card, and Kabakov opted to show him a second booking, resulting in his dismissal.

Israel manager Ran Ben-Shimon leapt to the defence of the Colorado Rapids midfielder after the game, insisting the celebration is regularly carried out by Abu Farchi without punishment.

Israel's Sayed Abu Farchi was sent off on Thursday after mimicking a gunshot following a goal

His manager has leapt to his defence amid questions on the Colorado Rapids' midfielder's actions in the game

'I've seen it before and everyone can check,' said Ben-Shimon. 'When this young player scores, in the Israeli national team or the MLS or anywhere he plays, he celebrates in the same situation again and again and he never gets a yellow card about it.

'He didn't know about it, this is his way to celebrate every goal he scores. He's a young player, I'm sure this lesson will stay with him a long time, he made a mistake.'

UEFA rules, meanwhile, suggest the referee was right to show a second yellow card.

They say a player must be booked for 'gesturing or acting in a provocative, derisory or inflammatory way'. Removing the corner flag is also yellow card worthy.

Israel have already been a focus of attention this week with the country to face the Republic of Ireland in two matches over the current international break.

The Israeli FA angrily took to social media on Monday to hit back at Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson's comments when he used the word 'genocide' in previewing the upcoming fixtures.

The Icelandic boss used forceful language in defending his team as they prepare to take the field against a side that the Football Association of Ireland wanted to have suspended from competitions.

'And I've said before, we're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide,' he said at the weekend. 'So, we're playing against Israel. We're not playing with Israel.'

Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson came under fire from the Israel FA for saying his team will be 'playing against genocide' this week

As reports circulated that the Israelis were considering a complaint to UEFA, the Israeli FA posted on X on Monday night: 'We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way,' the post on X stated.

'Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by the Republic of Ireland team coach.

'We're not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we're playing against the coach who embodies them.'

The matches will take place at neutral venues on Sunday and then again on October 4.

Austria, meanwhile, beat Israel 3-1 on Thursday, with Romano Schmid, Philipp Mwene and Sasa Kalajdzic all scoring.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland slip to deserved defeat in Kosovo
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland slipped to a 1-0 defeat away to Kosovo in their Nations League opener in Pristina.

The build-up to the League B3 encounter had been overshadowed by the controversy around upcoming fixtures against Israel, which Republic boss Heimir Hallgrimsson had admitted many of his squad members were uncomfortable about playing.

Chiedozie Ogbene had fired an early chance over before Kosovo responded to finish the first half strongly at the Fadil Vokrri Stadium.

The home side saw two shots cleared off the line and Ireland goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher then clawed away a header from Vedat Muriqi as Hallgrimsson's side got to the break on level terms.

Ireland - who are scheduled to play Israel in Hungary on Sunday and then again in a 'home' tie at another neutral venue in Serbia seven days later - dug in for the second half but were eventually undone with seven minutes left when Kosovo captain Muriqi bundled the ball in from close range.

Udinese defender James Abankwah was handed a first competitive start as part of a back five, with in-form Real Betis striker Troy Parrott the lone forward and Dara O'Shea taking the captain's armband.

Image: The Republic of Ireland have won two of their six games in 2026 so far

Ireland created what ended up being their only real clear chance in the 22nd minute. Abankwah got away down the right and ran into the Kosovo penalty area before cutting the ball back to Ogbene, who sent a curling effort over the crossbar.

Kosovo, who are in League B for the first time, went close on the half-hour mark when a cross from the left found its way through to Muriqi, whose angled shot was cleared off the line by Jayson Molumby.

Veldin Hodza then saw his 10-yard strike blocked in front of goal by O'Shea before Kelleher got up to claw away a looping header from Muriqi, which was set for the top corner.

Ireland made a positive start to the second half, with a deep cross from the right by Abankwah finding Parrott at the far post and his header was gathered by Kosovo goalkeeper Arijanet Muric.

Image: Vedat Muriqi scored the winner for Kosovo

Kosovo, though, continued to carry a threat themselves. Baton Zabergja sent a 20-yard effort just wide of the top corner, which again got the home supporters into full voice.

Muriqi forced Kelleher into another smart reaction save from an angled shot at the near post before Kosovo eventually made the breakthrough in the 83rd minute.

Ermal Krasniqi's shot was deflected onto the crossbar and Muriqi reacted quickest in a crowded six-yard box to nod the ball over the line.

Kosovo should have got a second late on when substitute Krasniqi dragged his shot wide after being set up by Muriqi following a break onto a long ball.

Ireland pay price for 'off day'

Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson told RTE:

"[Kosovo are] a good team, momentum with them, crowd with them, and to be honest they deserve the win.

"There was nothing that we didn't know about how they would play, where their threats would be, but [it was] an off day for a lot of our players and [it is] a tough place to come to if you have an off day, so a deserved win for Kosovo."

Hallgrimsson added: "We were the team that needed to defend today and didn't connect in possession or passes, not as sharp as we have done.

"We have to quickly find out the reason that we had an off day. We can all do better than we did today.

"It is a two-day turnaround for the next one, so we better be quick…and do better than this versus Israel. They are probably in the same position as us [having lost to Austria]."

Asked if the controversy from playing the fixtures against Israel had impacted on his team's performance against Kosovo, Hallgrimsson said: "I couldn't say now. It is difficult to measure that one."

He added: "This is the situation, we have to cope with it. And like I said before the game, this camp is a test of character.

"We need to do better in that area than we did here today. We knew that we needed to win the duels, win the one-vs-ones, but sadly they had the upper hand on all the basics."

What it means and next fixtures

Sports.title: Why have the Republic of Ireland's two games against Israel become so controversial?
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland will face Israel in a men’s football fixture for the first time since 2005 in this international break, but there have been calls for the two UEFA Nations League games not to be played at all.

Both meetings - the first played in Debrecen, Hungary on Sunday and the second scheduled for the Serbian town of Backa Topola on October 4 - have been overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

Uncertainty over the games going ahead might have subsided, but the tensions between the two nations have not.

Heimir Hallgrimsson, the Republic of Ireland head coach, has been accused of "stupidity and hypocrisy" by the Israel Football Association after last week suggesting his team would be "playing against genocide" when facing Israel, while his players are not ruling out their own protests ahead of the games.

The Athletic examines the key issues ahead of the first meeting this weekend.

Why have these games caused controversy?

This has been a contentious issue rolling down the tracks ever since the 2026-27 Nations League draw was made in February. Group B3 saw the Republic of Ireland pitted against Kosovo, their opening opponents this evening, and Austria, but it was the prospect of facing Israel which created immediate unease.

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) had overwhelmingly approved a motion that called on UEFA to ban Israel from its competitions just four months earlier due to violations of the governing body's statutes, including "the organisation of clubs in illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank without the consent of the Palestinian Football Association".

The Nations League draw duly reignited the row. Irish politicians, including the FAI member Joanna Byrne, were quick to call for a boycott of the Israel games in the following days and protests ensued when Qatar visited Dublin's Aviva Stadium for a friendly in May. Tennis balls featuring the Palestine flag were thrown on the pitch by supporters, twice causing brief interruptions.

Image: Tennis balls with a Palestinian flag on were thrown onto the pitch in Dublin during protests in May 2026

The FAI had already confirmed its plans to go ahead with the Israel games by then, and that decision was formally approved at an EGM in July.

That saw only 32 votes in favour of a boycott, with 75 members voting for the games to be played. The FAI had argued that boycotting games would cause "significant and lasting harm to Irish football" due to the likely disciplinary sanctions from UEFA.

A measure of the opposition to the Republic of Ireland facing Israel also came with the acceptance that the "home" fixture would not be played in Dublin. The FAI cited "operational challenges (that) could impact the delivery of the game on home soil" and the decision was eventually made in late June, with the support of UEFA, to move the game to Backa Topola, a small town in northern Serbia, on Sunday week.

No tickets for the game will be made available to Ireland fans.

The FAI has subsequently revealed that a request to see the two nations kept apart in future competition draws has been rejected by UEFA.

"The answer I got was very clear," FAI chief executive David Courell told reporters on September 18. "That would not be possible because Ireland and Israel have never been in direct conflict."

What is the political backdrop?

The Republic of Ireland has consistently outlined its backing for the Palestinian people since the conflict with Israel began almost three years ago, joining Norway and Spain when officially recognising a Palestinian state in 2024. Taoiseach Micheal Martin has also made his stance clear, accusing Israel of committing "genocide" last year in comments reported by the Irish Mirror.

The conflict in Gaza began after Israel responded to attacks by Hamas militants on October 7, 2023, which saw around 1,200 people, mostly civilians, killed in Israel and 250 taken hostage. The war has subsequently seen 73,000 people killed, according to figures from the Gaza Health Ministry and used by the UN.

Strained relations between the Republic of Ireland and Israel have continued this year. Two Israeli government ministers were the subject of travel bans in June, while foreign minister Helen McEntee also confirmed Ireland's intent to limit goods trading with settlements in the Israeli-occupied West Bank this summer.

Image: Taoiseach Micheal Martin

A meeting between the Republic of Ireland and Israel on a football field this weekend has subsequently taken on enormous significance against such a backdrop.

There are similarities in Ireland's political stance with those of Norway, who faced similar calls for a boycott when Israel travelled to Oslo last October. The Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) had aligned itself with its government and said in a statement leading up to Israel's visit that the "tragic humanitarian suffering in Gaza" had made the fixture challenging.

That World Cup qualifier, won 5-0 by Norway, saw thousands take part in a protest march to the stadium.

Who has opposed the games taking place?

Moving a home game 1,500 miles away has not stopped the objections building ahead of the two teams meeting on Sunday. More than 160 Irish sportspeople signed an open letter asking their national team to boycott the Israel games under the banner of the Irish Sport for Palestine Group, who have also run the "Stop the Game" campaign that protested outside of the Irish team hotel in Dublin on Monday.

"This is a significant moment and with this moment you have an opportunity to do the right thing," the letter said.

Kevin Kilbane, the former Republic of Ireland international who holds 110 caps, has also been unequivocal in his views. "The Republic of Ireland should not be playing Israel… not while Israeli forces are committing genocide," he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.">he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.

Amnesty International also issued a fresh statement on Tuesday that said UEFA risked letting football "rubber-stamp apartheid" by allowing Israel's continued participation in its club and international competitions. A spokesperson for the Israeli FA responded to that by saying: "Their obsession with the idea of Israel as a state is incurable, as is their need of attention."

The Irish media, meanwhile, has faced its own dilemmas in the coverage of the Israel games. RTE, the public broadcaster behind Ireland's boycott of the Eurovision Song Contest in the last two years due to Israel's continued involvement, has stripped back its coverage. Contractual obligations will be met, RTE confirmed in a statement, but there would be no studio coverage or commentators sent to either fixture.

Image: Kevin Kilbane, former Ireland international, has spoken out

What have the key stakeholders said ahead of this weekend?

Relations between the two nations have grown increasingly hostile in the last week. Hallgrimsson appeared in front of the media to announce his squad for the upcoming friendlies and made pointed remarks when asked how his players would focus on football.

"We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide," the former Iceland head coach told reporters. "We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel."

The reaction to those words, in a social media post from the Israel FA account, raised temperatures further still. "We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way," it read. "Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by @IrelandFootball team coach. We're not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we're playing against the coach who embodies them."

Martin, who was among the world leaders attending the UN General Assembly in New York, was then drawn back into debate on Tuesday. "I think those are unacceptable remarks. They should be withdrawn. Israel can't keep denying what the world knows and what the world understands."

The FAI has not addressed Hallgrimsson's comments publicly, but the Republic of Ireland's head coach said on Wednesday that he had been "grateful for the support" he had received.

"Maybe from a leadership point of view, it was not clever from me to take the attention (away) like this. It's a tricky time for us," Hallgrimsson said in his pre-match press conference ahead of facing Kosovo.

The same extends to his players, too. Dara O'Shea, the Ipswich Town defender, said, according to the BBC, that he and the rest of the players would come together on Friday to "openly discuss" the prospect of a protest ahead of the first Israel game in Debrecen on Sunday.

Image: Dara O’Shea, left, and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson during Wednesday’s press conference

Why are the games being played in Hungary and Serbia?

Hungary has acted as an adopted home for Israel since the start of the conflict. They first played there in November 2023, when resuming their attempts to qualify for Euro 2024 when hosting Switzerland at the Pancho Arena in Felcsut, a small village 26 miles west of Budapest.

Victor Orban, who lost his position as Hungary's prime minister this year, had been a long-standing ally of Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and claimed Hungary to be the "safest country in Europe" for Jews.

The World Cup 2026 qualifiers against Estonia, Norway and Italy were all held in Debrecen, which has also previously hosted European games for Israeli sides Maccabi Haifa and Maccabi Tel Aviv.

The Republic of Ireland's choice of Backa Topola, Serbia, is less clear. Dublin ceased to become an option, even behind closed doors, as the opposition to Israel visiting became clear, which left limited options for relocation.

It needed to be a nation sympathetic to Israel to avoid further protests and Serbia, neighbouring Hungary to the south, has forged strong diplomatic relations. According to the Associated Press, Serbia's president Aleksandar Vucic inaugurated an assembly factory for Israel-made drones last week, with plans for three more production sites.

A switch to Serbia was reliant on UEFA approval and it will be Backa Topola's home of the TSC Arena where this story ends on October 4.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
