Sports.title: Antonelli “very mad” with himself after crashing out in first round of qualifying | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli was frustrated with himself after crashing out of qualifying for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

The championship leader hit the wall at the inside of turn one during Q1. He tried to drive his car back to the pits but his race engineer Peter Bonnington told him to stop as the suspension damage was too extensive for them to repair during the session.

Speaking after the session Antonelli said he was caught out by how quickly the grip levels increased at the track during the session.

“The grip was coming up very quickly lap-by-lap,” he told Sky. “Obviously I turned in and suddenly I had a lot more front-end compared to the lap before and I touched the wall.

“So it was mistake from my side. Very unnecessary, to be fair. I’m very mad about it and we’ll try to do better tomorrow.”

Antonelli missed a significant proportion of the first and second practice sessions yesterday due to a hydraulic problem. While Antonelli is set to start tomorrow’s race from 16th on the grid his team mate George Russell claimed pole position for the race.

“The car has been very strong this weekend, so George has been doing incredibly well,” said Antonelli. “We’ll try our best tomorrow to recover as many places as possible.”

Sports.title: Russell dominates Baku qualifying for pole after Antonelli crashes in Q1 | 2026 Azerbaijan GP qualifying report
Sports.content:
George Russell took pole position for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix in dominant fashion.

His best lap of 1’42.526 was over eight tenths of a second quicker than anyone else could manage. He claimed pole position by the biggest margin for over three years

However his team mate Andrea Kimi Antonelli will start only 16th after he crashed out in the first round of qualifying.

The championship leader already had a time on the board when he clipped the barrier on the inside of turn one. The contact immediately broke his front-left suspension, and although Antonelli tried to drag his car back to the pits, race engineer Peter Bonnington persuaded him the suspension was so significant that the team wouldn’t be able to fix it in time and he should stop.

Compounding Antonelli’s misery, the time he had already set proved quick enough to secure him a place in Q2.

Russell’s bid for pole position briefly looked under threat from the McLaren drivers in Q3. However Lando Norris locked up heavily at turn three on his final lap and went into the run-off area. That also scuppered Max Verstappen’s final attempt to set a time, leaving him eighth on the grid.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Charles Leclerc produced his usual top-drawer performance at Baku to join Russell on the front row of the grid. Oscar Piastri, who set the quickest time at one stage in Q3, took third. Isack Hadjar out-qualified Verstappen on his return from injury.

Norris’s error left him fifth on the grid ahead of Lewis Hamilton. Both Alpine drivers reached Q3 but Franco Colapinto went off at turn 15 and ended up tenth, while Pierre Gasly took seventh ahead of Verstappen.

Carlos Sainz Jnr made good use of Williams’ upgrade, putting his car in Q3 for the first time this year. He will start ninth ahead of Colapinto.

Oliver Bearman narrowly failed to claim the final place in Q3 after Colapinto beat his time. Esteban Ocon also dropped out in Q2 in the other Haas. Alexander Albon was frustrated at his failure to join his team mate in the final 10 and dropped out along with the two Racing Bulls.

There was no great surprise that neither of the Aston Martins nor Cadillacs were able to beat Antonelli’s time in Q1. However the elimination of both Audis following their major upgrade was unexpected.

Sports.title: Verstappen leads close final practice session in Baku ahead of Russell and Hamilton | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen denied George Russell a clean sweep of all three practice sessions for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

But there was little to choose between the three quickest teams at the end of the final hour of running before qualifying.

The Red Bull, Mercedes and Lewis Hamilton’s Ferrari were covered by little more than a tenth of a second.

Drivers found the soft tyres were capable of producing multiple quick laps. Verstappen improved his fastest time repeatedly over a 12-lap run on softs at the end of the session, but skidded into the turn 15 run-off area during his final attempt.

His last run nosed him ahead of Russell’s Mercedes, which had set the pace for much of the session. Russell and team mate Andrea Kimi Antonelli, who was fourth-quickest, ducked back into the pits and switched to the medium compound before the session ended, while others continued to improve.

Charles Leclerc was half a second slower than Hamilton after going off at turn seven. Russell also came to a stop there during the session.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Pierre Gasly underlined Alpine’s potential again by setting the sixth-fastest time. That put him ahead of both McLaren drivers.

The two Red Bull drivers were separated by 1.2 seconds. Isack Hadjar complained of being repeatedly stuck in traffic on his way to the ninth-fastest time. “Unfortunately I don’t control all the cars,” replied his race engineer Richard Wood.

Franco Colapinto completed the top 10. Sergio Perez put his Cadillac in 16th place but was unhappy to see Arvid Lindblad overtake him by cutting across the inside of turn 15, which he reported to the stewards. Both Racing Bulls ended the session in the bottom five places.

Aston Martin’s tough weekend continued. The team told Lance Stroll to park up after just eight laps after he clipped the wall at the inside of turn one.

Although many drivers explored the track’s run-off areas the session ran without interruption, except for a brief Virtual Safety Car period to allow marshals to move a fallen branch.

Sports.title: Featured Comment: Why swapping Ocon for Camara makes sense for Haas | Brief
Sports.content:
Formula 1 could have one fewer race-winner on the grid in 2027 as Esteban Ocon has given the strongest indication yet he won’t remain at Haas.

Ocon is a mid driver at best. His race win in Hungary was not to do with skill and in a poor car, a mid driver cannot shine. The fact that Bearman is untroubled by Ocon’s ability is plain to see.

From a Haas perspective, keeping Ocon is a neutral equation. He’s not bringing in anything and having someone else in the car would make little to no difference to them from a sporting standpoint, it if having a Ferrari academy driver in the car gets them cheaper parts, why wouldn’t you?

Camara would be obvious for them given his current visibility across the F2 standings and the media. Couple that with his corporate backing and the fanaticism of Brazilian fans with wallets, he is a more attractive choice than a Mercedes journeyman with little in the way of an affiliation package.

Performance comes first, allegedly, but you can’t ignore financial performance. Besides, they’re not going to get Tsolov, Mini or Dunne so why not?

Sports.title: Spotlight: Scheckter plans appeal over court’s demand he pay £1.5m tax bill | Brief
Sports.content:
Jody Scheckter has vowed to fight on after losing a court battle over a £1.5 million tax bill.

The 1979 Formula 1 world champion closed his organic farm business in Hampshire two years ago but faces a demand for £1,457,634 from His Majesty’s Revenue and Customs.

A court ordered Scheckter to pay the bill last week. However he told The Telegraph he believes he did not break the law and will appeal against the decision. The 76-year-old added illness prevented him from attending much of the two-week tribunal hearing and he struggled to hear some of the questions.

He told the paper: “My wife said ‘You should have paid it long ago’ She’s right. Except, you know… I blame my mother, she always told me: ‘You’ve got to fight for what’s right’. And I absolutely believed I was doing the right thing.”

Sports.title: Johnny Fisher Weighs 243 Pounds for Michael Pirotton Fight at Zuffa Boxing 11
Sports.content:
Fisher headlines Saturday’s Copper Box Arena card, live on Paramount+ in the US and Sky Sports in the UK.

Johnny Fisher tipped the scales at 243 pounds ahead of his heavyweight clash with Michael Pirotton at London’s Copper Box Arena on Saturday, September 26. Belgium’s Pirotton weighed 240.6 pounds for their scheduled 10-round main event at Zuffa Boxing 11.

Fisher was 2.4 pounds heavier. Paramount+ will broadcast the event in the US, with Sky Sports carrying it in the UK. The event starts at 2 pm ET / 7 pm UK.

The Romford heavyweight enters at 14-1 with 12 knockouts after signing with Dana White’s promotion. Saturday will mark his third appearance at the Copper Box, where he also suffered his only professional defeat against Dave Allen.

Fisher had edged Allen by split decision in their first meeting before Allen stopped him in the rematch. He has since returned to winning ways, stopping Ivan Balaz in four rounds.

His move to Zuffa brings an immediate headline slot.

“The most exciting chapter of my professional career begins,” Fisher said when announcing his signing. “Thank you to Dana White, Nick Khan, and the Zuffa Boxing team for this opportunity. Everything has led to this point. Bull Army, get ready to assemble. Bosh!”

Richards and Kalajdzic Make Weight

Craig Richards registered 174.2 pounds for his 10-round light heavyweight bout against Radivoje Kalajdzic, who weighed 174.5 pounds. Both came in below the 175-pound limit.

Two middleweight bouts are scheduled for 10 rounds each. Lee Cutler weighed 159.5 pounds, with Louis Greene at 159.1, while Cesar Mateo Tapia hit 159.9 pounds against Leo Ruiz’s 159.2.

Kayla Allen and Edina Kiss will contest six rounds, weighing 142.9 pounds and 142 pounds, respectively. Alex MacMillan registered 149.9 pounds for his six-round meeting with Guillaume Azagier, who came in at 151.6.

Those bouts complete the six-fight main card.

Three Bouts on the Prelims

Rogelio Romero weighed 199.2 pounds ahead of his eight-round cruiserweight contest with Aurel Ignat, who registered 199.6 pounds.

Alexis de la Cerda and Cain Lewis both made the featherweight limit for their eight-rounder. De la Cerda came in at 125.4 pounds, with Lewis slightly heavier at 125.6.

Fred Pullen faces Leonardo Faretina over four rounds at lightweight. Pullen weighed 131.4 pounds, while Faretina registered 132.7, completing the nine-bout London bill.

Sports.title: Tim Bradley Calls Shakur Stevenson’s Pacquiao Pursuit Easy Money
Sports.content:
Tim Bradley sees Shakur Stevenson’s pursuit of Manny Pacquiao as a soft move. With plenty of active fighters available, Shakur has picked a 47-year-old for the proposed co-feature on the Tyson Fury–Anthony Joshua card.

“Ain’t nobody waiting on no damn Manny Pacquiao and you to fight, boy,” Bradley said in a video on his channel. He challenged Zuffa Boxing’s interest in the matchup, too: “Y’all talking about y’all supposed to be changing boxing? This ain’t changing boxing. This downplaying and downgrading boxing.”

Bradley first fought Pacquiao in 2012, when Manny was 33. Stevenson would face a far older fighter who has not recorded an official win since beating Keith Thurman in 2019. Putting Pacquiao’s name on Shakur’s record would be a commercial prize. It would say much less about Shakur’s place among today’s best fighters.

A Fury–Joshua stadium card would put Stevenson in front of viewers who rarely watch him. That opportunity comes with a trap. If he controls the distance and wins a quiet decision, a crowd waiting for Pacquiao’s old bursts of action may turn on him. If Shakur stops Pacquiao, many will see the result through the lens of Manny’s age. Winning the fight and winning over that audience are different jobs.

Stevenson also holds the WBO light welterweight title he took from Teofimo Lopez in January. Bradley pointed to Raymond Muratalla and O’Shaquie Foster while questioning why Shakur is pursuing Pacquiao. A catchweight attraction would take time away from a title defense, although the WBO has not approved this proposed fight or granted Stevenson an exception.

Bradley went further, claiming Floyd Mayweather wants Shakur to beat Pacquiao before Gervonta Davis gets the opportunity. That is Bradley’s speculation. His stronger point concerns Shakur’s own career: a famous opponent cannot give him the same credibility as beating a top fighter in his prime.

Pacquiao–Stevenson remains in talks for the proposed Fury–Joshua card in Cardiff. Bout agreements had not been delivered when the latest report was published.

Turki Alalshikh built his entire reputation among boxing purists on eliminating cherry-picks, forcing unifications, and making the fights the old promotional machinery spent a decade sabotaging. For Riyadh Season and Netflix to rubber-stamp an official, sanctioned bout between a prime pound-for-pound champion and an elderly senator looks like a total betrayal of that brand. It lowers the bar to YouTube celebrity boxing standards. Purists will openly question how the same organizers who put together elite 50-50 matchups can suddenly justify an exploitative nostalgia stunt on the biggest British stadium card of the year.

It lowers the bar to YouTube celebrity boxing standards. Purists will openly question how the same organizers who put together elite 50-50 matchups can suddenly justify an exploitative nostalgia stunt on the biggest British stadium card of the year.

Putting this fight as the co-feature in Cardiff sets a stylistic trap for everyone involved. Those stadium fans want blood, violence, and dramatic exchanges to warm them up for Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua. Instead, they will watch Shakur do what he always does: use elite footwork, control distance from twenty feet away, and tap his way to a quiet, low-output decision against an icon whose forty-seven-year-old legs cannot track him down.

If Shakur refuses to engage and cruises to a boring points win, eighty thousand spectators will boo him mercilessly. If he turns aggressive and stops Pacquiao, fans will feel disgusted watching a faded legend get battered by someone nearly two decades younger. It produces a scenario where nobody wins, the sport loses credibility, and the fans leave feeling cheated by a spectacle disguised as competition.

Sports.title: Frank Warren Questions Hamzah Sheeraz’s Title Exit
Sports.content:
Frank Warren won the purse bid for Hamzah Sheeraz’s defense against Janibek Alimkhanuly. Days later, Sheeraz gave up the WBO super middleweight title. Warren’s response raises a question Sheeraz’s next fight will have to answer: what was the belt worth if he would not defend it against this challenger?

“Very, very disappointed,” Warren said in an interview this week. “It was a purse bid. We bid the highest amount of money for it.” Queensberry’s winning bid was $1,001,809, with Sheeraz due roughly $750,000 under the purse split. Warren said to iFL TV his team had worked to put Sheeraz in position to win the title.

Sheeraz mentioned Alimkhanuly’s previous failed drug test in objecting to the WBO’s order. He has grounds to question the sanctioning body’s decision. Still, surrendering the belt after Queensberry won the bid leaves him open to another question: what fight is worth giving up a guaranteed title defense?

Alimkhanuly would have been a serious test. Sheeraz had trouble controlling the mobile Simon Zachenhuber in July and kept his title by majority decision, with one judge scoring the fight level. Against Alimkhanuly, he would have faced a southpaw with greater power and a stronger claim to world class standing.

Warren also criticized the advice Sheeraz is receiving, then said Queensberry still has a contract with him. If Sheeraz is approaching his final fight under that deal and intends to leave, Warren has little incentive to arrange an easy farewell. A dangerous opponent would give Queensberry a fight to sell and give Sheeraz another chance to prove himself. Warren has announced no such plan, but his frustration makes the next matchmaking decision worth watching.

A champion brings a belt to the table when pursuing Canelo Alvarez or another major fight. Sheeraz no longer has that bargaining chip. If his team has a better opportunity ready, it can make the decision look shrewd. Until then, fans have seen him leave a difficult fight and a world title behind.

Fans never buy noble moral stances when a fighter surrenders a title to avoid an absolute nightmare. If Janibek were a feather-fisted fringe contender or an overmatched mandatory, Sheeraz walking away over money or a past testing issue might pass the smell test. When the mandatory opponent happens to be an avoided Kazakh wrecking ball with an elite amateur pedigree, the narrative completely crumbles.

Janibek represents the worst possible opponent profile in professional boxing: high risk, modest commercial value, and desperate hunger. He has been frozen out of massive unification bouts for years precisely because champions know the danger he brings. He saw Sheeraz holding that WBO belt as his golden ticket to finally force the sport to take him seriously and secure the life-changing purses he has been chasing. Facing a motivated, heavy-handed southpaw who knows his entire career trajectory hinges on dismantling you is a terrifying proposition.

Sheeraz clearly did the math and panicked. Taking Janibek for seven hundred and fifty thousand dollars offered terrible risk-to-reward math, especially after Simon Zachenhuber exposed how vulnerable Sheeraz looks when opponents start landing clean counters. Getting knocked out on home soil by Janibek permanently erases the mystique Queensberry spent years building.

The public sees right through the sudden ethical concerns. Turning down a dangerous fight against a prime killer while simultaneously campaigning to share the ring with Canelo Alvarez—who served a well-documented suspension for clenbuterol—makes the excuse look laughably dishonest. Sheeraz wanted the prestige of calling himself a world champion, but when the real tax for holding that strap arrived at the purse bid, he chose self-preservation over genuine greatness.

Sports.title: Richardson Hitchins Faces Cardiff Payday Reality
Sports.content:
Richardson Hitchins says he’ll fight Keyshawn Davis in Wales. He also wants the money to remain the same as when the bout was pitched for Madison Square Garden. If Pacquiao–Shakur joins Fury–Joshua in Cardiff, that demand becomes much harder to satisfy.

Hitchins says he has accepted the Davis fight and that Keyshawn told him he was ready to sign. He dislikes the proposed move overseas but would make the trip for the opportunity. The opponent isn’t his sticking point. The terms might be.

“As long as the pay is the same, I’m cool,” Hitchins told Sean Zittel and Radio Raheem.

The original plan, by Hitchins’s account, put him and Davis in the co-feature beneath Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua in New York. Cardiff changes the audience and the setting. A possible Manny Pacquiao–Shakur Stevenson fight changes the card’s pecking order as well. If that bout is added, Hitchins–Davis would likely sit beneath two much bigger attractions.

Hitchins has every right to ask for the purse he wants. Promoters have to decide what the fight adds at that price. Two skilled Americans meeting at welterweight is an excellent matchup for boxing followers, but Hitchins’s patient style may be a tough sell to a stadium crowd waiting for Fury and Joshua. Twelve rounds of careful jabbing and clinching would put pressure on the event’s pace, especially if his bout runs close to the headliners.

Madison Square Garden would have given Hitchins familiar surroundings and supporters in the building. In Cardiff, he would need to win over a crowd with little reason to favor either American. Davis may have the more crowd pleasing combinations, though he still has to land them against a boxer who excels at controlling distance.

None of this means Hitchins is refusing Wales or that his purse is holding up the deal. No figures have been disclosed, and Pacquiao–Shakur has not been finalized. The offer Hitchins liked in New York may look different on a crowded Cardiff bill. He has accepted the opponent. Now he needs the terms to work.

Hitchins holding out for co-feature money while sitting in the number three slot shows a complete failure to grasp how Zuffa, TKO, and Netflix operate.

Dana White and TKO do not overpay undercard fighters who bring zero ticket sales or subscriptions. They run a business built on leverage. When a card features heavyweight giants like Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua alongside a pairing like Manny Pacquiao and Shakur Stevenson, every dollar is already allocated to the top of the marquee. Those headliners drive the subscriptions and pack eighty thousand seats in Cardiff. The third fight on the bill is there to fill airtime, not eat up premium budget.

Hitchins is confusing his personal ambition with actual market value. Fighters slotted third on a mega broadcast do not get multimillion-dollar packages. If he demands the same guarantee he was pitched when he thought he was the primary co-feature in New York, Zuffa and the organizers will simply look past him. Keyshawn wants the fight, but Keyshawn also has promotional backing and mainstream interest.

If Hitchins digs his heels in over money, matchmakers can easily replace him with another welterweight or junior welterweight hungry for global exposure on Netflix. By overplaying his hand, Hitchins risks sitting at home watching Keyshawn fight someone else under the brightest lights in the sport.

Matchmakers have an endless line of hungry contenders ready to take Hitchins’ spot for half the money just to get on a global Netflix stage. If Hitchins walks away over purse demands, nobody is shedding a tear, and the promoters will not hesitate to pivot to a replacement who comes to throw leather.

Keyshawn comes out ahead regardless. If Hitchins drops out, Keyshawn gets matched with an aggressive, fan-friendly welterweight or junior welterweight whom he can likely dismantle in style. Looking explosive on a bill featuring Tyson Fury, Anthony Joshua, Manny Pacquiao, and Shakur Stevenson does infinitely more for Keyshawn’s market value than chasing Hitchins around the ring for twelve rounds of clinches and jabs.

For Hitchins, walking away would be career self-sabotage. His style has never drawn mainstream attention or moved live gates. He needs marquee dance partners to stay relevant. Accepting smaller money to fight Keyshawn in Wales is the necessary cost of entry to unlock the division’s real moneymakers.

Beating Keyshawn is Hitchins’ only path to force his way into conversations with the big money names at welterweight. If Hitchins prices himself out now, he shuts the door on all of them [Ryan Garcia, Devin Haney, Teofimo Lopez and Rolando Romero]. He gets left in the cold, relegated to low-profile headline slots on small cards. Taking the fight, taking the pay cut, and taking the trip to Wales is his only real lottery ticket.

Sports.title: Fundora and Hadribeaj Give Fans Little to Talk About
Sports.content:
Sebastian Fundora promised to burn down Las Vegas. Ermal Hadribeaj promised a hard fight. Both sounded ready during Thursday’s virtual press conference, but the first media push for their October 17 title fight gave casual fans little reason to stop scrolling. That is a problem for a card whose main event already needs an introduction.

Fundora said he intends to extend his three-fight knockout streak. Hadribeaj spoke about the work that earned him a shot at the WBC super welterweight title and what becoming Albania’s first world champion would mean to him. Those stakes are real. Neither man, though, gave the press conference a line that made the matchup feel urgent.

“We’re only focused on this fight. We know that we can’t overlook anyone. We focus on the work and take it one fight at a time,” Fundora said during Thursday’s virtual press conference.

That is sensible preparation from a champion. It is a tough sales pitch. Hadribeaj was equally respectful, calling Fundora “a great guy” and recalling that they met three years ago. His most interesting answer came when he rejected the obvious advice to attack Fundora’s body. He said others have tried it and suggested he has worked on specific answers, but kept those details to himself.

The rest of the card has the same problem. Jermall Charlo was once a name that drew attention on its own. Long stretches out of the ring have cost him that pull, and a bout with Koen Mazoudier offers little to restore it before the opening bell. Their fight had been scheduled for July in Australia before Charlo’s trip fell through; moving it to Las Vegas has given the card a former champion, but not a matchup many fans were asking to see.

Brandon Figueroa’s title defense is harder to understand. He stopped Nick Ball in the final round to win the WBA featherweight belt, a result that should have set up another fight with immediate appeal. Instead, he faces 35-year-old Tomoki Kameda, who lost to IBF champion Angelo Leo in 2025. Kameda is ranked by the WBA, so this is a legitimate title defense. Still, Leo is the opponent who would give fans a clear answer about where Figueroa stands among the featherweight champions.

Fundora and Hadribeaj may produce an excellent fight. Figueroa usually makes opponents work, and Charlo’s return will interest those who have followed him for years. But Thursday was a chance to make people care before October 17. The fighters gave the promoter very little to work with, while the matchmaking left the card’s biggest questions unanswered.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua Fight for WBA Super Title
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua are receiving an unearned gift from the World Boxing Association. Neither Briton holds a world title, and their December 11 spectacle in Cardiff on Netflix certainly requires no manufactured hardware to pack a stadium. The sanctioning body is tossing its top heavyweight prize into the ring anyway, staging a brazen demotion of the actual titleholder standing in the wings.

Murat Gassiev did everything asked of him. He earned his position in the ring, collected his status after Oleksandr Usyk vacated, and defended his position by stopping Peter Kadiru in July. His reward is watching the WBA invent a higher tier out of thin air to accommodate two fighters who enter the ring with zero championship claims.

The super champion designation was created to honor unifications and dominant multi-belt reigns. Fury and Joshua possess none of that hardware today. Handing an elite designation to a pair of contenders coming off non-title bouts shreds the integrity of the rankings. The organization relies on discretionary clauses in its rulebook, but pulling bureaucratic rank to vault two big-name fighters past an active titlist exposes pure promotional favoritism.

Commercial convenience drives the maneuver. Attaching a world title to a global Netflix event allows the sanctioning body to secure maximum bout fees and purse percentages capped at five hundred thousand dollars total between both corners. That payday completely derails the campaign the organization spent years trumpeting, abandoning its pledge to eliminate duplicate titles and reduce every division to a single recognized champion.

Cardiff promises massive global exposure, but it leaves the division splintered. The victor will inevitably chase an immediate rematch, an undisputed bout, or walk away into retirement. Gassiev will find zero incentive from the winner to stage a dangerous, low-reward clash.

If the sanctioning body possesses any credibility, it must establish a mandatory deadline ordering the Cardiff winner to face Gassiev within six months. Without an enforceable consolidation order, the super title remains an arbitrary marketing prop manufactured to reward commercial power while the real champion stays shoved to the curb.

Throwing a manufactured Super title onto this Cardiff event is an outright insult to the sport. Neither Fury nor Joshua enters this fight carrying championship momentum. Both were thoroughly solved and dethroned by Oleksandr Usyk, and both have spent the latter stages of their careers surviving shaky outings against fringe opposition rather than beating top-tier contenders.

Inventing a world title specifically for them rewrites the entire definition of what a championship represents. The primary outrage sits squarely with the blatant demotion of Murat Gassiev. The sanctioning body spent years running a public relations victory lap, swearing to clean up its reputation by phasing out multiple champions and establishing one belt per weight class.

That promise evaporated the second Netflix and the Saudi backers dangled a massive live event. Gassiev took care of business in the ring against Pulev and Kadiru, only to be shoved down to secondary status. For the casual viewers tuning in on Netflix, the graphics package will do its job. The broadcast will flash world title belts across the screen, the commentary team will talk about legacy, and the mainstream audience will swallow the idea that the winner is the true king of the heavyweight division.

Hardcore fans know better. A real world title cannot be handed out as a promotional party favor to two aging fighters years past their absolute prime. It degrades the division, reduces the belt to a rented stage prop, and reminds anyone paying close attention that in the heavyweight hierarchy, money and broadcast leverage will always trump genuine athletic merit.

Casual fans will view it as a real world title fight because the television screen tells them to. The mainstream audience does not follow sanctioning body mandates, title unifications, or mandatory rankings. They see two names they recognize from mainstream headlines, a stadium packed with seventy thousand screaming fans. To someone who watches boxing once every two years, whoever walks out of Cardiff with that belt looks like the king.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury vs  Anthony Joshua Finally Official: December 11 in Cardiff on Netflix
Sports.content:
The British heavyweight rivals will meet at Principality Stadium after a dispute over the venue delayed their long-awaited fight.

Tyson Fury (36-2-1, 25 KOs) and Anthony Joshua (30-4, 27 KOs) will finally fight on Friday, December 11, 2026, at Cardiff’s Principality Stadium, live on Netflix. The confirmation ends months of negotiations over where the British heavyweight clash would take place.

The venue dispute is settled. Joshua’s camp had insisted on staging the bout in Britain, while New York’s Madison Square Garden became a serious alternative.

“I can now confirm that Fury Vs Joshua will be coming to the UK, as I promised British boxing fans. The time for talking is over……..” Turki Alalshikh wrote on X.

Both fighters signed earlier this year. A date and venue remained unresolved, however, allowing the dispute to drag on despite their agreement to face each other. Fury repeatedly blamed Joshua in public and suggested he could pursue a third fight against Oleksandr Usyk.

Dana White said: “For more than a decade, boxing fans have been clamoring for the heavyweight showdown between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua. Together, they bring 66 wins, 52 knockouts and multiple heavyweight world titles into the ring. On December 11, two of the biggest heavyweights of this generation finally collide and the winner will take a significant place in heavyweight history.”

Netflix says White and The Ring will collaborate to promote the fight, despite Eddie Hearn’s earlier insistence that White would not be its promoter.

Joshua has boxed at Principality Stadium twice before, stopping Carlos Takam and then outpointing Joseph Parker to add the WBO heavyweight belt to his collection. He returns to face the British rival whose name has followed him through years of callouts and failed negotiations.

Both men came through summer bouts.

Joshua survived two first-round knockdowns against Kristian Prenga in July before stopping him in the second. Fury stopped Mariusz Wach after seven rounds in Thailand that month, having returned in April to outpoint Aslanbek Makhmudov at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

Those victories kept their meeting alive. Now the former heavyweight champions have a confirmed December date in Britain, with Netflix carrying the broadcast.

Sports.title: Manny Pacquiao and Shakur Stevenson Remain in Cardiff Talks
Sports.content:
Manny Pacquiao against Shakur Stevenson remains under discussion for the proposed Anthony Joshua-Tyson Fury card in Cardiff. It would give the event a second major fight, but neither Pacquiao nor Stevenson has received a bout agreement.

BoxingScene’s Lance Pugmire reports that two people connected to the talks say Netflix wants the matchup as part of a “double main event.” December 11 is the date under consideration at Principality Stadium, with December 18 also possible. Pacquiao adviser Jas Mathur told BoxingScene that Pacquiao’s financial terms are still being negotiated.

That leaves a great deal to settle before anyone can call this a fight. The Cardiff show itself has yet to be formally announced, and moving Joshua-Fury from the previously discussed Madison Square Garden setting means assembling the rest of the card around a different venue and date.

Pacquiao-Stevenson would bring two very different attractions to that card. Stevenson, 29, is coming off his January win over Teofimo Lopez and has since signed with Zuffa Boxing. Pacquiao, 47, drew with Mario Barrios in his July 2025 return. His name would draw attention far beyond the usual boxing audience, though the long layoff and age difference would become part of the conversation as soon as the fight was announced.

The proposed pairing also raises a practical question: what weight would they fight at? Pacquiao’s return came at welterweight, while Stevenson’s recent work has been at lighter weights. No weight, number of rounds, or title terms have been announced.

For now, the news is that Pacquiao-Stevenson has survived the reported switch to Cardiff and remains in Netflix’s plans, according to BoxingScene. The decisive development would be agreements reaching both fighters. Until then, it belongs on the list of fights being negotiated, rather than the Joshua-Fury undercard.

Pacquiao turns 48 on December 17. If the fight lands on December 18, Shakur would face him one day after his birthday. Pacquiao won his first world title in 1998, before Shakur turned two.

That age difference makes the matchup a hard sell as a competitive fight. If Shakur wins easily, how much credit does he get for beating a man nearly two decades older? If he boxes his way to a quiet decision, Pacquiao’s name may bring viewers to Netflix, but the fight may give them little reason to watch Shakur again.

Pacquiao’s fame can make this a major event. Turning it into a fight that helps Shakur is another matter. First, both men need to agree to terms; neither has received a bout agreement.

Ghana News.title: Adu-Boahene case: Atta Akyea files no-case submission, cites evidential gaps and missing witnesses
Ghana News.content:
Lead counsel for former National Signals Bureau (NSB) Director-General Kwabena Adu-Boahene, Samuel Atta Akyea, has filed a submission of no case to answer, citing alleged evidential gaps, inconsistencies and the prosecution’s failure to call material witnesses.

The submission was filed after the prosecution closed its case in the trial involving Mr Adu-Boahene, his wife Angela Adjei-Boateng and another accused person.

The defence contends that the evidence presented by the prosecution does not establish a sufficient case requiring the accused persons to open their defence.

A key issue raised by the defence is the prosecution’s handling of evidence surrounding the alleged misuse of GH¢49.1 million earmarked for a cybersecurity project.

The State alleges that the money was transferred through three cheques from an account associated with National Security into an account belonging to BNC Communications Bureau Limited, a company linked to the accused persons.

The prosecution has further alleged that the funds were subsequently diverted and used for purposes unrelated to the intended cybersecurity procurement.

The defence, however, has challenged aspects of the prosecution’s evidence, including the circumstances surrounding the transactions and the extent to which the disputed funds can be directly traced to assets and expenditure attributed to the accused persons.

Mr Akyea has also pointed to what the defence considers inconsistencies in the evidence presented by prosecution witnesses.

Another key argument concerns the failure to call what the defence considers material witnesses whose evidence, it argues, could have shed light on the management and authorisation of the funds.

The defence has previously raised questions about the absence of senior officials connected to the National Security arrangements surrounding the disputed transactions.

The prosecution's final witness, EOCO investigator Frank Marshall Cromwell, was subjected to extensive cross-examination by Mr Akyea before the State closed its case.

During the proceedings, the defence questioned the investigation into the alleged cybersecurity procurement and whether sufficient steps had been taken to independently establish that the project had not been delivered.

The defence also challenged aspects of the financial investigation, including the tracing of funds and the basis for linking particular transactions and assets to the GH¢49.1 million.

The prosecution, for its part, maintains that it has presented sufficient evidence to support the charges against the accused persons.

The State has relied on financial records, bank statements and other documentary evidence to establish its case concerning the alleged diversion and use of the funds.

Mr Adu-Boahene and the other accused persons have pleaded not guilty to the charges.

The charges include stealing, conspiracy to steal, defrauding by false pretences, wilfully causing financial loss to the state, using public office for profit and money laundering.

Following the filing of the no-case submission, the Attorney-General has been given 14 days to respond.

The defence will subsequently have an opportunity to reply to the prosecution's response before the court determines whether the accused persons have a case to answer.

A ruling on the no-case submission is expected to determine whether the trial proceeds to the defence stage or whether the accused persons are discharged.

Ghana News.title: Manchester City ‘found guilty of majority of 115 charges’
Ghana News.content:
Khaldoon Al Mubarak, chairman of Manchester City, and Ferran Soriano, chief executive officer

Manchester City have been found guilty of breaking the majority of the 115 financial rules they were accused of breaching, sources have told BBC Sport.

The Athletic is reporting that the sanctions have not been decided but that the independent panel has reached its decision, finding them guilty of all but one count.

Sources have told BBC Sport a decision has been made in the case, and City have been found guilty of the majority of breaches.

The Premier League declined to comment.

Asked if the report was correct, City did not comment either way.

Instead they released a statement saying that the “Premier League process remains ongoing with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality”.

“The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence,” it added.

BBC Sport has also been told that, in the event of a defeat, Manchester City will appeal against the findings.

Ghana News.title: From abandoned ruins to model residence: How Techiman North DCE fulfilled 9-month promise
Ghana News.content:
When the District Chief Executive (DCE) for Techiman North Adom Kwabena Johnson led journalists through the dilapidated remains of the official DCE residence in early 2025, the sight was grim.

Broken roofing sheets flapped in the wind. Weeds had swallowed the compound. Floor tiles, once pristine, lay cracked and discoloured. The building initiated under the previous National Democratic Congress (NDC) administration but abandoned when the New Patriotic Party (NPP) took power in 2017 had become a symbol of wasted public resources.

"The erstwhile NPP government deserted this project when they took over, leaving a valuable public asset to waste away," Johnson said at the time.

But rather than merely lament, the DCE made a pledge that many dismissed as political rhetoric: the bungalow would be completed within nine months.

A Promise Kept

Nine months later, that pledge has been fulfilled and then some.

The once-decrepit structure now stands proudly as a fully roofed, tiled, and painted facility, with a paved compound and modern finishing. The project is approximately 98% complete, with the contractor expected to hand over the keys to the Assembly in the coming weeks.

The transformation was enough to impress the regional minister, who visited the site for an inspection tour alongside the DCE. Walking through the corridors of the revitalised facility, the minister could not hide his satisfaction.

"I recall instructing the various MMDCEs in the area during my first meeting with them to work on their accommodations under the legacy module," the minister said. "I am excited that the DCE has made this possible. This is judicious use of state funds."

The Man Behind the Mission

For Adom Johnson, the motivation was simple: fiscal responsibility.

"The Assembly has been spending heavily on rent for successive DCEs," he explained. "What motivated me is to save the Assembly from spending more on paying rents."

But the benefits extend beyond cost savings. According to the DCE, the facility will serve multiple purposes:

1. A permanent residence for successive DCEs, ending the cycle of rental payments

2. Accommodation for government officials visiting the district on official duties

3. A future event centre for national events, with plans for an extension

"The facility will also help in hosting government officials who visit the district in line of work," Mr Johnson noted. "The extension of the project will also in the future serve as an event centre for national events."

A Community's Relief

Local residents, who had long complained about the abandoned structure, have welcomed the development with optimism. Some had described the building as "a symbol of wasted resources." Now, hope has replaced frustration.

Some Assembly Members who spoke to Joy News expressed their appreciation to the DCE, noting that the project had not only provided a befitting residence but also created jobs and boosted local economic activity during the construction phase.

What's Next?

The Techiman North District Assembly is expected to commence final procurement and construction processes in the coming weeks, with the contractor set to officially hand over the project shortly after.

For a district that watched a valuable public asset rot for nearly a decade, the revival of the DCE's bungalow is more than just a construction project — it is a statement that with the right leadership, promises can be kept.

As the DCE put it, "We have been instructed by President Mahama to ensure that such projects are completed for the benefit of the district. So I have resolved to complete this project."

Ghana News.title: Francis Spio Jungo appointed to FanteFest 2026 planning committee
Ghana News.content:
Francis Spio Jungo has been appointed to the planning committee for FanteFest 2026, scheduled to take place in London on 26 September 2026.

Jungo, the Ghanaian creative entrepreneur popularly tagged as one of the youngest artistes to retire from music after a remarkably short career, has secured another major role in the entertainment and events industry.

Interestingly, Jungo’s journey in the music industry began in February 2011, when he released his first official song. However, barely five years into his music career, he decided to call it quits in 2016, making his transition from recording artiste to industry professional particularly notable and earning him the description of Ghana’s youngest retired musician.

Rather than completely walking away from entertainment, Jungo moved behind the scenes and ventured into event organisation, where he has since been actively involved in creating platforms and opportunities for young and emerging musicians.

His work has seen him support upcoming artistes and contribute to efforts aimed at helping new talents gain visibility, perform on bigger platforms and take their careers to the next level.

Jungo is also the Chief Executive Officer of Heritage Promotions, the organisation behind the Central Music Awards (CMA), which has become a major platform for recognising and celebrating music talents from Ghana’s Central Region.

His latest appointment to the FanteFest 2026 planning committee further highlights his growing involvement behind the scenes in Ghana’s creative and events space.

With his experience as a former artiste, event organiser and talent supporter, Francis Spio Jungo is expected to bring his industry knowledge and organisational experience to the planning of FanteFest 2026 in London.

Ghana News.title: Roots and Routes uses health walks, air sensors and tree planting to tackle air pollution in Ghana
Ghana News.content:
On the streets of Accra, the things that threaten people’s health are not always visible.

Traffic moves through the city, rubbish accumulates at the roadside, and smoke rises from burning waste. People walk, work and exercise through it all, often without knowing what is in the air they are breathing.

A youth-led initiative is trying to make some of that invisible pollution visible.

Called Roots and Routes, the project combines health walks with air-quality monitoring and tree planting as part of efforts to raise awareness about air pollution and push for action in Ghana.

The name captures its two main approaches: the roots represent trees planted to help improve the environment, while the routes represent the paths taken by participants as they walk through parts of Accra, collecting data on the air around them.

“Essentially a project that seeks to create awareness and then take action for clean air under the World Economic Forum's Clean Air Collaborative,” said Dr Jonathan Caleb Akuaku, the project lead.

Walking through Accra’s polluted spaces

The project began with an assessment of Ghana’s air-quality standards, according to Dr Akuaku, before moving into a more practical phase of mapping routes and collecting data.

So far, the team has completed two of four planned health walks.

The first covered about eight kilometres around Accra’s central business district, including Independence Square.

The second took participants through Nima, Kanda and the Independence area, covering a little more than five kilometres.

But these are not simply walks for exercise.

Participants carry AirBeam sensors supplied by partner organisation Ever and Better, using the devices to measure the quality of the air as they move through different parts of the city.

“These devices help us go on this while we're on the walk, we're collecting data about the air around us,” Dr Akuaku said.

The sensors measure fine particulate matter, including PM2.5 — tiny particles that can remain suspended in the air and be inhaled without being seen.

For the team, the value of the walks is therefore not only in getting people moving. Each route becomes an opportunity to gather evidence about the environments through which people live and work.

The project plans to collect data from about four different areas, allowing the team to compare air quality and build a clearer picture of how pollution varies across the city.

Why air pollution?

For Dr Akuaku, the decision to focus on air pollution is closely tied to its consequences for young people.

He cited World Economic Forum findings indicating that one in four young people die prematurely because of the harmful effects associated with air pollution.

He also pointed to respiratory illnesses linked to poor air quality.

“The goal is to live long and healthy life. And so if there's something that is taking the lives of young people prematurely, that it needs attention. That's why air pollution is on our radar so strong,” he said.

The concern is particularly relevant in rapidly growing urban areas, where transport, waste and construction can all affect the air people breathe.

In Accra, the sources highlighted by the project include vehicle emissions, open burning of rubbish and uncollected waste.

These are problems residents encounter daily, but their health consequences can be difficult to see or immediately connect to the air around them.

From the streets into schools

Roots and Routes is also taking its message into schools.

The project plans to work with five schools, engaging students in discussions about air pollution while helping them plant trees.

“We are going into the schools to help them to create more awareness, engage them, help them understand what is happening, then partner with them to build or to plant trees,” Dr Akuaku said.

The target is to reach at least 500 students and plant at least 153 trees across the participating schools by October.

The intention is to make young people participants rather than simply recipients of information.

The walks show them how pollution can be measured. The school activities introduce them to practical environmental action.

Together, the two approaches are intended to turn an abstract issue — air quality — into something young people can observe, measure and respond to.

Turning measurements into pressure for change

The project’s organisers say the data will ultimately have to travel beyond the people carrying the sensors.

After completing the four planned walks, the team intends to organise a policy dialogue with policymakers and present the findings.

“One of the things that we've earmarked is after the four walks that we set to take, we would engage policymakers in the policy dialogue and then get these issues to their attention,” Dr Akuaku said.

That could bring discussions about air quality closer to some of the everyday decisions that shape urban life — from waste collection and disposal to transport and city planning.

For the organisers, the measurements matter because advocacy is stronger when it is supported by evidence.

Instead of simply telling authorities that pollution is a problem, they want to show how air quality changes from one location to another and identify the conditions contributing to those differences.

Making the invisible visible

The project is being implemented under the World Economic Forum’s Clean Air Collaborative, with support from the Global Shapers community.

Ever and Better is providing the air-quality sensors used during the walks.

For Dr Akuaku and his team, however, the larger ambition goes beyond four walks, a few hundred students or a few hundred newly planted trees.

It is about changing how people understand the air around them.

Air pollution does not always arrive with the obvious signs of environmental damage. There may be no warning when fine particles enter the lungs, no visible boundary separating clean air from polluted air and no immediate sensation telling a commuter that one street may carry a different pollution burden from another.

That makes measurement important.

And it explains why the project begins with something as ordinary as walking.

Across Accra, the routes people take every day can become a map of the air they breathe — while the trees planted along the way offer a reminder that the response to pollution cannot stop at measuring the problem.

The challenge now is whether the data gathered on those routes can translate into action in the places where decisions about Ghana’s air are made.

Ghana News.title: Stanbic Bank moves to boost electric vehicle through ‘Be Powered’ campaign
Ghana News.content:
Stanbic Bank Ghana is seeking to support the growth of electric mobility in Ghana through its 'Be Powered' campaign, offering financing to individuals and businesses seeking to acquire electric vehicles and other e-mobility equipment.

The initiative forms part of the bank’s broader sustainable mobility drive, which also includes financing for solar energy systems.

Stanbic Bank says the campaign is intended to help customers overcome the financial barriers associated with transitioning from conventional vehicles to electric alternatives.

Speaking on Joy FM 's Super Morning Show on September 25, Kwame Offei, Head of Product at Stanbic Bank, says electric mobility is becoming increasingly important as countries and businesses look for more sustainable transportation options.

“In terms of electric vehicles, that is where the world is moving to.”

He says the potential benefits of electric vehicles go beyond their environmental advantages, pointing to possible savings in fuel and maintenance costs.

The technology can also offer a different driving experience, including quieter operation and features associated with newer vehicle technology.

Mr Offei says the opportunities are not limited to private passenger cars.

“For companies that are into trucks and other equipment, they are e-vehicles or e-mobility type of equipment that they can also jump into.”

Stanbic Bank's Head of Vehicle and Asset Financing, Wendy Nelly Sarpong, also says the campaign is available to both individuals and businesses, including existing and prospective customers.

“This is open to both our existing and prospective customers. And we're doing this for both individuals and businesses.”

Under the initiative, Stanbic Bank says it can finance up to 100 percent of the value of an eligible electric vehicle or e-mobility requirement, subject to assessment of the customer's ability to repay.

The bank says financing can be structured over a period of between six and ten years, giving customers a longer period over which to spread repayment.

Ms Sarpong says the bank does not rely on a single financing formula for all customers.

“We understand you as an individual. We understand you as a business. And we co-create the parameters together.”

She explained that the bank assesses an individual's income when determining affordability, while businesses are assessed based on their cash flows and financing needs.

The 'Be Powered' campaign also incorporates vetted vendors to help customers make informed decisions about the technology they are purchasing.

Ms Sarpong says the bank wants customers to make financially sustainable decisions rather than simply complete a purchase.

“Our goal is to help our customers make a financially successful decision and not just a purchase.”

She says the vetted vendors can provide support beyond the sale of the vehicle or equipment, including technical assistance and after-sales service.

Stanbic Bank says its approach is intended to reduce some of the uncertainty customers may face when considering electric mobility, particularly around technology, vendors and long-term support.

The bank also believes the cost savings associated with electric vehicles could make them increasingly attractive to individuals and businesses.

Mr Offei noted that electric vehicles can reduce reliance on petrol and diesel and potentially lower some maintenance expenses.

For businesses operating fleets, trucks or other equipment, the bank says electric alternatives could also provide opportunities to reduce operating costs while supporting their sustainability objectives.

The 'Be Powered' campaign therefore combines financing with access to expertise and approved vendors as Stanbic Bank seeks to support the development of sustainable mobility in Ghana.

With financing available to both individuals and businesses, the bank says the initiative is designed to make electric mobility more accessible and encourage more customers to consider the transition to electric vehicles.

Ghana News.title: Tears in Damongo court as accused persons show alleged torture wounds while in police custody
Ghana News.content:
A Damongo Circuit Court was thrown into concern after two accused persons appeared unable to stand in the dock and told the court they had allegedly been beaten while in police custody.

Abdulai Seidu and Karim Yakubu were asked by the presiding judge, His Lordship Livingston Lartey Yao Ameevor, why they could not stand upright when their names were called.

The two reportedly told the court that they had been subjected to beatings by police officers since their arrest and during their time in custody.

The court subsequently directed the accused persons to remove their shirts, allowing the judge to examine their alleged injuries.

The sight of wounds on their backs reportedly left the courtroom in shock, prompting the judge to immediately order the police to take the two men to hospital for medical attention.

Seidu and Yakubu were arrested by the Police Intelligence Department (PID) on August 18, 2026, at Kintampo.

The two, residents of Salaga in the East Gonja District of the Savannah Region, are being held in connection with investigations into a robbery on the Salaga-Bimbila highway.

The case follows investigations launched by the National and Savannah Regional PID into reported robbery incidents in the Salaga area.

According to information presented in court, the police arrested the two suspects at Kintampo after receiving information believed to be linked to the robbery investigations.

Meanwhile, concerns are growing among some residents over alleged police brutality against suspects and accused persons in the Savannah Region.

Some residents, speaking on condition of anonymity, alleged that several people had died following similar incidents of alleged brutality in the region.

However, the Savannah Regional Police Command has yet to publicly comment on the allegations.

Ghana News.title: Telecel Business Runaway in Takoradi equips SMEs with practical tools for growth
Ghana News.content:
A large number of entrepreneurs and small and medium-sized business owners have participated in Telecel Ghana’s Business Runway in Takoradi, describing the engagement as an eye-opener on what it takes to move their businesses beyond survival.

The programme, held in the Western Region for the first time as part of Telecel’s SME Month activities, brought together entrepreneurs, business leaders and experts for practical discussions on financing, digitalisation, marketing, tax compliance, leadership and access to markets.

The initiative was held under the theme “Connect to Growth: Unlock More.”

For many participants, the sessions offered practical lessons on challenges they encounter in their businesses but often struggle to address.

The Chief Executive Officer of Telecel Ghana, Ing. Patricia Obo-Nai, said the company’s decision to bring the Business Runway to Takoradi was intended to take its SME support closer to businesses outside Accra.

She said many entrepreneurs have passion and good products but face difficulties with visibility, accessing new markets and acquiring the practical skills required to grow.

The Business Runway, she explained, was therefore designed to connect SMEs with the knowledge, tools, networks and opportunities needed to unlock further growth.

W/R Minister Urges Entrepreneurs to Focus on SMEs

The Western Regional Minister, Joseph Nelson, said the focus on SMEs was particularly important to the region given its significant economic potential.

According to him, the Western Region has opportunities across oil and gas, mining, agriculture, agro-processing, manufacturing, tourism and logistics.

He said the challenge was to ensure these opportunities translate into sustainable businesses, jobs and wealth for people in the region.

“Small and medium-sized businesses remain critical drivers of economic growth. However, many entrepreneurs face challenges with access to finance, markets, skills, technology and business networks,” he said.

Mr Nelson urged entrepreneurs to formalise their operations, invest in skills and technology, understand their markets and seek opportunities to add value to products and services.

He also called for stronger collaboration between government and the private sector to create an environment where businesses can start, grow and compete beyond their immediate communities.

For entrepreneur and Founder and Executive Chairman of McDan Group, Dr Daniel McKorley, one of the biggest lessons for SMEs is that access to finance does not automatically translate into business growth.

He challenged entrepreneurs to first determine what additional capital would achieve before seeking funding.

“There’s a big difference between needing money and knowing what to do with money,” he said.

Business Owners Urged to Understand their Revenue

Dr McKorley urged business owners to understand their revenue, costs, profits, cash flow, receivables and liabilities before taking on financing.

He also emphasised the importance of people and systems as businesses expand.

According to him, many businesses struggle when they move from the founder-led stage into an organic growth phase without establishing proper structures and corporate governance.

“What actually builds a lasting company is not strong personality. What builds a strong company is systems and structures,” he said.

He further encouraged entrepreneurs to use technology to solve specific problems rather than adopting digital tools simply because they are fashionable.

Artificial intelligence and other digital solutions, he noted, can help businesses with research, marketing, customer communication, data analysis and repetitive processes.

But technology, he cautioned, cannot compensate for poor leadership, weak financial discipline or a business that does not understand its customers.

Participants at the Business Runway welcomed the practical nature of the programme, with several describing the sessions as an eye-opener.

For some entrepreneurs, the discussions offered new perspectives on managing finances, using technology, building teams and positioning their businesses for growth.

The networking opportunities also allowed business owners to connect with other entrepreneurs and potential partners while exploring opportunities beyond their existing markets.

Telecel Ghana says it remains committed to supporting SMEs through reliable connectivity, digital solutions and programmes that provide entrepreneurs with knowledge and networks to grow their businesses.

The company also reiterated its commitment to continued investment in Ghana’s digital infrastructure and to developing solutions that can improve productivity and enable businesses to participate more effectively in the digital economy.

For participants, however, the real test begins after the Business Runway applying the lessons from the sessions to improve their businesses.

And the message emerging from the engagement was clear: starting a business may be the first step, but building one that can scale requires the right financing, people, systems and technology.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
