Hughes-led delegation explores technical cooperation, infrastructure support and funding opportunities to modernize Liberia’s airport system

HARBel, Margibi County — The Liberia Airport Authority (LAA) says it is seeking technical partnerships, investment and logistical support to strengthen Liberia’s aviation infrastructure as it participates in a major regional airport conference in Abuja, Nigeria.

The LAA delegation, led by Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer Ernest R. Hughes, with Chief Financial Officer Victor Debah, is attending the Airports Council International (ACI) Africa 35th Annual General Assembly, 75th Board and Committee Meetings, Regional Conference and Exhibition, running from September 19 to 25, 2026.

According to a press release issued by the Authority, the weeklong gathering is bringing together airport executives, policymakers, regulators, development partners and aviation industry stakeholders to discuss the future of African aviation under the theme, “Next-Gen Airports: Driving Performance and Resilience.”

The LAA said its participation is intended to strengthen Liberia’s engagement with regional and international aviation institutions while exploring opportunities to improve airport operations, infrastructure and service delivery.

During the conference, the delegation is expected to hold bilateral and multilateral discussions with airport authorities, aviation agencies, development partners, financial institutions and industry stakeholders.

The proposed engagements will focus on technical assistance, operational support, logistics cooperation, capacity development, infrastructure advancement and institutional strengthening.

The Authority said it also plans to explore opportunities for investment, innovation, knowledge transfer and resource mobilization to support the development of Liberia’s airports.

Hughes Pursues Regional Aviation Cooperation

Beyond the ACI Africa conference, Hughes is undertaking separate engagements with key Nigerian aviation institutions, including the Nigeria Airspace Management Agency (NAMA), the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) and the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN).

The discussions are intended to strengthen technical cooperation and secure logistical and capital support that could improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of Liberia’s aviation infrastructure.

The LAA said the engagements align with its broader objectives of strengthening aviation safety, advancing airport infrastructure development and building technical partnerships to support the long-term growth of the sector.

The Authority also views the conference as an opportunity to deepen regional integration, exchange best practices with other airport operators and explore emerging technologies that could support Liberia’s aviation modernization efforts.

LAA Links Participation to National Development

The Authority said its participation reflects its commitment to President Joseph Nyuma Boakai’s national development agenda, particularly in improving infrastructure, strengthening regional cooperation and expanding transportation connectivity.

ACI Africa, the regional arm of Airports Council International, represents African airports and promotes advocacy, capacity-building, innovation, connectivity and sustainable growth across the continent’s aviation industry.

The LAA said it remains committed to developing a modern, safe, secure, efficient and resilient airport system capable of supporting economic growth, trade, tourism and regional connectivity while improving services for the traveling public.

The press release did not specify the amount of funding or capital support being sought, identify any agreements finalized during the engagements, or provide a timeline for the anticipated infrastructure improvements.

World.title: Liberian Leader Demands Two Permanent African Seats On Security Council, Fairer Global Finance System
World.content:
UNITED NATIONS, New York – President Joseph Nyuma Boakai on Thursday night told world leaders that trust in the United Nations has been broken by the uneven application of its founding principles, and called for sweeping reforms of the Security Council and the global financial system to restore it.

By Rodney D Sieh, rodney,[email protected]

Addressing the 81st Session of the UN General Assembly, held under the theme “Restoring Trust, Managing Transformation: A United Nations that Delivers for All,” the Liberian leader said the world is facing “a lingering crisis of legitimacy and relevance that demands urgent attention.”

“Our answer to that fragmentation cannot be less multilateralism,” President Boakai declared. “It must be better multilateralism!”

‘Eighty years of patience is enough’

The President reserved his strongest words for the Security Council, noting that Africa, home to 1.5 billion people and nearly one-third of UN membership, still has no permanent seat, even though 80 percent of the Council’s mandates concern African peace and security.

“Eighty years of patience is enough. The time for structural reform is now,” he said, describing the imbalance as a “historical injustice” that “is no longer tenable.”

Reaffirming Liberia’s support for the Common African Position, President Boakai said Africa demands no fewer than two permanent seats with full rights, including the veto for as long as it exists, plus additional non-permanent seats. “Correcting this imbalance is not a favor to Africa,” he said. “It is necessary to restore the United Nations’ trust, credibility, and legitimacy.”

Security Council seat and the drug war

Speaking as a current member of the Security Council, the President highlighted threats facing West Africa, including transnational organized crime, cyber warfare and narcotics trafficking along maritime routes in the Gulf of Guinea.

He said Liberia’s Joint Security forces are “tightening the vise on transnational drug cartels,” but stressed that no nation can fight global criminal networks alone. He appealed to international partners for targeted support in coast guard surveillance, intelligence sharing and port security technology.

He also called for an immediate end to hostilities in conflict zones, unhindered humanitarian access and stronger investment in preventive diplomacy, arguing that “the cost of preventing a war pales in comparison to the cost of rebuilding a broken society.”

‘Governed by so few’

On the economy, President Boakai said developing nations are being “squeezed by unsustainable debt, shrinking fiscal space, and mounting external shocks” as the 2030 deadline for the Sustainable Development Goals approaches.

He called for structural reform of the World Bank and International Monetary Fund, whose governance, he said, still reflects the world of 1945. “A financial system that decides the fate of billions cannot continue to be governed by so few,” he said.

At home, he pointed to progress under the ARREST Agenda for Inclusive Development – focused on Agriculture, Roads, Rule of Law, Education, Sanitation and Tourism – citing gains in revenue administration and rural farm-to-market roads. He also said his administration is strengthening accountability, financial management and the fight against corruption.

Climate justice, youth and AI

The President noted that Liberia contributes virtually nothing to global emissions yet suffers coastal erosion, flooding and disrupted farming seasons, while holding 42 percent of the remaining Upper Guinean Rainforest. He urged industrialized nations to honor their climate financing pledges and put loss-and-damage mechanisms into operation.

He called for investment in STEM education and digital skills for Africa’s youth, more than 60 percent of whom are under 25, reaffirmed Liberia’s commitment to equality for women and girls, and joined calls for binding rules on artificial intelligence, particularly in warfare. “Innovation must protect human development, not automate human destruction,” he said.

From San Francisco to today

Recalling that Liberia was one of only four African nations to sign the UN Charter in 1945, President Boakai presented the country’s journey from civil war to constitutional democracy as proof that “institutions can be rebuilt.”

He opened his address by congratulating Khalilur Rahman on his election as President of the 81st Session, thanking outgoing President Annalena Baerbock, and saluting Secretary-General António Guterres as he prepares to end his tenure.

“Let us leave this Assembly committed to a United Nations that not only deliberates on crises but also resolves them,” he concluded.

World.title: Liberia: Kwarbo vs. Coleman: The Drug Van Order that Nobody Owns
World.content:
A statement attributed to detained former Highway Patrol Chief Wadell Kwarbo says IG Gregory Coleman ordered him to escort the drug van. His family denies he made it, and the IG calls it part of a four-month disinformation campaign.

MONROVIA — A few days ago, Wadell Kwarbo’s father appeared on Spoon FM with an account of what his detained son had allegedly told him before he was taken into custody.

By Rodney D. Sieh

According to the father, a senior officer had called Kwarbo and instructed him to escort a shipment of drugs. At the time, he did not publicly identify the officer.

This week, however, a name emerged.

A statement attributed to Kwarbo, the former chief of the Liberia National Police Highway Patrol Division who remains detained at the Monrovia Central Prison, identified Police Inspector General Gregory O. W. Coleman as the officer who allegedly made the call.

“Police IG Gregory Coleman ordered me to escort the van. He instructed me to escort the drugs with my patrol vehicle (RL-141). And I acted on his order,” Kwarbo was quoted as saying on Spoon FM.

The statement reportedly went further, calling for his telephone records and written statement to be made available.

“Let them get my call log. My call log can be subpoenaed through the Court,” he was quoted as saying. “Let them release my written statement also. Why are they keeping it? They have it.”

But there is now a direct contradiction over whether Kwarbo actually made those statements.

Family: “He Never Made Such A Statement”

On Thursday, Kwarbo’s wife, Bendu Kwarbo, issued a statement on behalf of the family distancing her husband from the allegations against Coleman.

The family said it “categorically dissociates” Kwarbo from reports attributing the allegations to him and said neither the family nor his lawyers knew about or authorized any statement accusing the police chief.

“Mr. Kwarbo himself firmly rejects and denies this allegation in its entirety and maintains that he has made no such statement,” the family said.

The family said Kwarbo’s lawyers had advised him to remain silent and allow the court process to determine the case.

It described the statement circulating in his name as “malicious” and urged media organizations and the public to verify information before publishing or repeating allegations.

The family also maintains that Kwarbo should not have been arrested and that the case against him is based on what it described as false and misleading allegations.

Coleman: “Sustained Disinformation Campaign”

Coleman, meanwhile, has rejected the allegation and characterized it as part of what he says has been a prolonged campaign to undermine his credibility.

“For the past four months, I have been the target of a sustained disinformation campaign intended to damage my character and silence my fight against the culture of impunity, including the ongoing drug investigation,” Coleman said.

The police chief said freedom of expression must be respected but warned against spreading what he described as false information concerning an active criminal investigation.

“The facts must be established through evidence and lawful process. Anyone found to have broken the law must be held accountable under that same process,” Coleman said. “I will remain focused on my duty. I will not be intimidated.”

The US$ 317 Million Drug Case

The dispute comes against the backdrop of Liberia’s largest cocaine trafficking investigation, involving a shipment authorities have valued at approximately US$317 million.

Kwarbo, a former Highway Patrol chief, was stripped of his duties and later arrested and charged alongside Anthony T. Blaye, who served as Chief of the Liberia National Police Financial Crime Division.

The two have been accused of using marked police vehicles to escort a large cocaine shipment.

According to findings attributed to a joint Liberia Drug Enforcement Agency and Liberia National Police investigation, the cocaine was transported from a coastal landing site to a stash house using two police vehicles in an escort formation, with one vehicle reportedly positioned ahead of the shipment and another behind it.

Coleman said investigators uncovered evidence indicating that state security personnel played a role in moving the narcotics from the landing site to a holding location.

The foreign nationals, a Serbian and a Colombian, are being accused of bringing the cocaine into Liberia through aircraft and shoreline landing operations.

Liberian authorities publicly destroyed the seized cocaine on July 30 in what officials described as the country’s largest-ever drug destruction exercise.

Kwarbo’s Bail Fight

Kwarbo has denied wrongdoing and, in August, filed a motion seeking bail before Criminal Assizes “C” at the Temple of Justice.

His lawyers, including Cllr. Sayma Syrenius Cephus, maintain that he is being detained largely on allegations that he provided an escort to principal defendants after the alleged crimes had already been committed.

Kwarbo’s lawyers argue that the prosecution has not presented objective evidence placing him at the scene before or during the commission of the alleged offenses.

The defense has also challenged allegations attributed to co-defendant Christian Nyantee, arguing that Nyantee may have a motive to shift responsibility and that uncorroborated accomplice testimony should not be sufficient to establish the legal standard required for continued detention.

Kwarbo’s lawyers further contend that he had no prior knowledge of the alleged drug operation and that providing security escorts can form part of routine security duties during major national-security operations.

The Questions That Remain

The latest dispute leaves several questions unanswered.

It remains unclear who spoke to Spoon FM on Kwarbo’s behalf, whether the statement attributed to him was actually made by him, and how the statement emerged from the prison.

It is also unclear whether the written statement Kwarbo was quoted as referring to exists, what it contains, and whether investigators have sought or obtained his telephone records through the court.

Analysts say those questions may be resolved through evidence presented in court rather than competing accounts outside the courtroom.

For now, the public has two sharply different versions: one attributed to Kwarbo naming Coleman as the officer who allegedly ordered the escort, and another from Kwarbo’s family saying he never made the statement.

Kwarbo remains in detention and, under Liberia’s Constitution, is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty by a court of competent jurisdiction.

World.title: Liberia: Bail Denied, The Former Vice President’s Lawyers Weigh A Trip To The Supreme Court And a Long Legal Fight
World.content:
MONROVIA – For three weeks, the most important document at Jewel Howard-Taylor’s home has been a visitors’ log.

By Willie N. Tokpa

Every person who passes her gate is written down. Police officers stand watch around the clock. She may step outside only when the court has approved a trip to the hospital in advance. The former vice president, once second in line to lead the country, now needs a judge’s permission to see her doctor.

On Thursday, her lawyers went to court hoping to change that. They left with the same restrictions in place and a stinging rebuke from the bench.

By evening, the defense team had gathered in Monrovia to decide what comes next. For lawyers who have shifted strategy more than once in five weeks, the choices are narrowing. The road now leads up Capitol Hill, to the Supreme Court.

“We believe that she is eligible”

Atty. Gbawu Kowou, one of her lawyers, said the defense would take its case to the Justice in Chambers.

“The court argued that the crime extended up to 2026 based on the allegation that she received US$15,000. We disagree,” he told FrontPageAfrica. “The defense believes the court did not properly apply Liberia’s law on bail and pretrial detention, and that is the reason we are filing a petition for certiorari before the Justice in Chambers. We believe that she is eligible for bail.”

The papers are ready, he said. The team hopes to file on Friday, September 25, or by Monday, September 28 at the latest. Cllr. Kabina Ja’neh and former Associate Justice Lavalah Supuwood will lead the fight.

And the woman at the center of it? “The Vice President has been briefed on the latest decision from the court,” Kowou said.

A judge’s rebuke

The defense’s argument was simple. The 2023 Controlled Drugs and Substances Act makes the charges against her grave and non-bailable. But her lawyers said the conduct she is accused of happened in 2021 and 2022, before the law existed. A law, they argued, cannot reach back in time.

Judge Ousman F. Feika of Criminal Court “C” turned to the defense’s own paperwork to answer them.

Attached to their motion was the Writ of Arrest. It alleges that she received US$15,000 from the cartel through Sheikh Bashiru Kante as recently as August 2026. If true, the judge reasoned, the alleged conduct did not stop in 2022. It ran well past the new law.

Then he went further. He accused the defense of ignoring a major part of its own exhibit and warned that such conduct runs against the lawyers’ code of ethics. It is rare for a judge to scold counsel this way in a pretrial ruling.

Her lawyers noted their exception and told the court they would “take advantage of the statute controlling.” In Liberian courtrooms, everyone knows what that means: we’ll see you upstairs.

The road upstairs

The tool they will likely use is a writ of certiorari. Just last month, on August 28, the Supreme Court ruled in the Capitol arson case that certiorari is the proper way to challenge a trial judge’s interlocutory ruling. Chief Justice Yamie Quiqui Gbeisay explained that it lets the high court review a lower court that has jurisdiction but is alleged to have acted irregularly or contrary to law.

Recent history offers the defense both hope and caution.

In March 2025, Justice in Chambers Ceanneh Clinton Johnson overturned a Criminal Court “C” decision revoking the bail of Peach Bility, son of Representative Musa Hassan Bility, and sent him home.

Six years earlier, it went the other way. Justice Joseph Nagbe granted the State’s petition and overturned a trial judge who had found grounds to admit murder suspect Oliver Dillon to bail. Dillon stayed behind bars.

A filing could also buy time. In a 2024 case, the State’s certiorari petition automatically halted scheduled Criminal Court “C” proceedings until a conference with the Justice in Chambers. A similar pause here would freeze action before Judge Feika while the high court looks at his ruling.

Whatever the outcome, the question reaches beyond one defendant. The Justices may have to decide whether a no-bail law passed in 2023 can apply to conduct that allegedly began before it. Judge Feika’s order leaned on the continuing nature of the alleged offense and did not squarely answer that argument. The defense is likely to press the gap.

Waiting on the grand jury

Other fights remain unresolved. Judge Feika still has to rule on defense motions to quash the arrest writ, a habeas corpus petition and a motion to suppress evidence.

The defense has already shown it is willing to change course. On September 17, it withdrew the preliminary examination before Magistrate L. Ben Barco, giving up an early chance to test the State’s evidence. That evidence includes WhatsApp messages and audio recordings investigators say came from Kante’s phone. No one has yet heard them played in court.

And over all of it hangs the grand jury. Judge Feika can decide whether she goes home or stays confined. He cannot put her on trial without an indictment, and more than a month after her arrest, there is none.

Her allies have noticed. Lenn Eugene Nagbe, chief of staff to former President George Weah, said the government’s failure to indict her raises questions about the strength of its case.

The August Term of Court is in its 39th day of jury sitting. The clock is running.

The bigger picture

Her case sits at the heart of Liberia’s widest drug investigation. It began with a cocaine seizure valued at about US$317 million and has reached into the police, the intelligence services and the prison system.

Her party, the Coalition for Democratic Change, calls it political persecution. The government says she is presumed innocent and will have her day in court.

She was released from Monrovia Central Prison on medical grounds on September 4. The court has warned she could be sent back if her health improves significantly.

So she waits. Behind her gate, under guard, with each visitor’s name written in a book, while her lawyers climb the hill to argue that the case against her belongs to 2021, and the State insists it runs right up to this summer.

World.title: Liberia: Judge Gives Police ‘Last Opportunity’ in Cybercrime Suspect’s Detention Case
World.content:
Court says it will make an ‘informed decision’ if the IG and the arresting officer miss Friday’s hearing

MONROVIA – Criminal Court “B” at the Temple of Justice has given the Liberia National Police (LNP) one last chance to appear and explain why it is holding Jerry Nyantee Wrato. Wrato is charged with several cybercrime offences, and his lawyers say the police arrested him illegally and have held him far beyond the 48 hours allowed by the Constitution.

By Rodney D Sieh

Assigned Circuit Judge Pape Suah postponed the habeas corpus hearing on Thursday, September 24, 2026. No police officer appeared in court for the second straight hearing. The judge moved the matter to Friday, September 25, at 11 a.m. and warned that if the police fail to appear again, the court “will make an informed decision and will use the appropriate legal authority.”

Wrato faces charges of misuse of device, cyberstalking, distributing data messages that incite damage to property or violence, and distributing intimate images without consent. He sat in the dock during Thursday’s proceedings.

Prosecution blames officials’ absence

Government lawyers Cllr. Isaac B. Williams, Sr. and Cllr. Irene N. D. Saie represented the Ministry of Justice. They asked for the postponement. According to the court minutes, they said the arresting officer, the Inspector General of Police, officers of Units 102, 103 and 106, the chief investigator and other senior officers were all out of Monrovia and out of the country.

The prosecutors told the court they had “belief and assurance” that the officers would be back in Montserrado County in time for Friday’s hearing.

Defence: ‘bad faith’ and ‘disrespect’

Wrato’s lawyer, Cllr. Garrison D. Yealue, told the court the request was “made in bad faith” and was “a complete disrespect” to the court. He said the police had “illegally arrested the Petitioner and illegally kept him for more than 120 hours.” He argued that the police were now refusing to answer to a key provision of the 1986 Constitution.

The defence also rejected the excuse that the officials were away. Counsel argued that the police is an institution. Even if the Inspector General is abroad, he said, more than 60 deputies and assistant directors remain in the country, and “they choose to disrespect this Honorable Court.”

Counsel asked Judge Suah to reject the prosecution’s request. He also asked the judge to issue contempt proceedings against the Inspector General and his senior officers for “intentionally, willfully and disrespectfully ignoring” the court’s order.

Judge questions government’s paperwork

In his ruling, Judge Suah said the court had halted the previous hearing because the police and the Ministry of Justice did not appear to show cause why the writ should or should not be granted.

The judge said the Ministry of Justice claimed the defendant was already before the court, but it had not provided “sufficient and convincing evidence” that the case was sent to court in keeping with law. He said the documents the state described as a return from the Magisterial Court did not show who made the return, when it was made, or when the case was received.

The court had ordered government lawyers to make sure the police authorities and the arresting officer came to Thursday’s hearing. Judge Suah said “not even a single police officer” appeared. He noted that under habeas corpus, whoever has a person in custody must come to court and show why that person should or should not be released.

The judge said that “to its greatest surprise,” the prosecution then asked for a continuance because the officers were outside the country. He described the police’s refusal to come to court as “a disrespect.” He said he would use all relevant legal authority under the 1986 Constitution and the habeas corpus statute to make sure the arresting officer appears.

Even so, Judge Suah granted the continuance as the respondents’ “last opportunity.” He ordered the Clerk of Court to serve notices of assignment on the Ministry of Justice and Attorney General, the Solicitor General, the Montserrado County Attorney’s office, and the Office of the Inspector General of Police.

The defence took exception to the ruling. The matter was then suspended until Friday.

World.title: Liberia: CMC Pulls Out of Weah-Led Opposition Coalition Talks
World.content:
MONROVIA – The Citizens Movement for Change (CMC) has withdrawn from the opposition coalition process convened by former President George Manneh Weah, less than three weeks after the party’s political leader, Rep. Musa Hassan Bility, sat at the table with other opposition leaders in Paynesville.

By Rodney D. Sieh, [email protected]

In a statement issued Thursday, September 24, and signed by National Chairman James M. V. Yougie, the CMC said it has formally informed Weah and the other political leaders who attended the September 6 Opposition Political Leaders Forum that it will not endorse the current draft communiqué or remain in the process leading to the proposed coalition.

The party said the decision followed a review of the draft by its National Executive Committee, National Advisory Council and Diaspora Leadership, which concluded that the arrangement, in its current form, does not reflect the objectives for which the CMC was founded.

At the heart of the CMC’s objection is what it describes as the absence of a binding reform program. The party said any coalition seeking public confidence must first agree on changes to the country’s system of government, institutions, laws and political culture, including constitutional reform, institutional independence and transparent leadership.

“Liberians should not be asked to choose only between continuing the present order and returning to the immediate past,” Bility said in the statement. “Our country deserves a new option built around a new governing system and a serious program of national reform.”

The CMC said it will instead continue national consultations with citizens, civil society groups, community leaders and like-minded parties toward what it calls a “broad national third lane.”

The party stressed that its decision “does not close the door” to opposition cooperation. It said it remains willing to work with other opposition parties on electoral integrity, the rule of law and public accountability, and is open to future political cooperation in which every party is treated as an equal and decisions are reached through transparent consultation and consensus. The CMC also said its position should not be read as a personal criticism of Weah or any other participating leader.

A reluctant participant from the start

The withdrawal is not entirely a surprise. Before the forum, Bility had objected to how it was structured. In an August 28 letter to CDC Chairman Atty. Janga A. Kowo, he said the CMC appreciated the effort to promote dialogue among opposition parties but would not attend, arguing that opposition unity cannot begin with predetermined leadership and authority. He specifically questioned provisions designating a presiding leader and establishing a National Convening Secretariat under an already appointed coordinator.

Bility later reversed course and attended the meeting. At a press conference afterward, he welcomed the gathering, saying the focus should remain on ordinary Liberians and describing the goal as uniting to rescue them from the “so-called rescuers” — a reference to the Unity Party’s campaign slogan.

The September 6 forum

The forum was held at the Jamaica Resort in Thinker’s Village, Paynesville, four days after Weah returned to Liberia. Attendees included ANC Political Leader Alexander B. Cummings, Bility, MPC Political Leader Simeon Freeman and MOVEE Political Leader D. Maxwell Kemayah, along with senior CDC officials including former House Speakers J. Alex Tyler and Bhofal Chambers. Benoni Urey’s All Liberian Party was also represented.

Under the agreement reached there, each participating party was to nominate two representatives to a steering committee responsible for drafting a framework document defining the principles, structure and mechanisms of cooperation. Participants stressed that the initiative was not an electoral alliance or an agreement on a presidential ticket for 2029.

The push came amid sharp opposition criticism of the Boakai administration. The CDC had described President Boakai’s August 26 national address on the rule of law as “dishonest and nefarious.” On his return, Weah said the opposition has an obligation to speak collectively and argued the country is moving in the wrong direction under the Boakai administration.

The effort has also exposed divisions elsewhere. The National Patriotic Party suspended three senior partisans for allegedly using the party’s official letterhead to endorse the roundtable. Unity Party Secretary General Amos B. Tweh dismissed the gathering as posing no serious threat to the ruling party or to President Boakai’s reelection prospects.

The shadow of the CPP

The CMC’s exit revives memories of the last major opposition alliance. In February 2019, the Unity Party, ANC, ALP and Liberty Party formed the Collaborating Political Parties, which won six Senate seats in 2020 before a September 2021 dispute over its framework document triggered its collapse. The ALP walked out in December 2021, the Unity Party followed in February 2022, and a Liberty Party faction left the next month. The remaining Cummings-Brumskine ticket won 1.61 percent of the presidential vote in 2023, and the CPP formally dissolved in April 2024.

The CMC itself is a young party. Bility, who represents Nimba County District 7, founded it in March 2025 after resigning from the Liberty Party in September 2024.

World.title: Dignity at the Podium, Deportees at the Airport
World.content:
PRESIDENT JOSEPH NYUMA BOAKAI went to the United Nations on Thursday night and spoke powerfully about dignity. He demanded that Africa, a continent of 1.5 billion people, stop being discussed without a permanent voice on the Security Council. He said a global system “governed by so few” cannot keep deciding the fate of billions. He pledged that Liberia stands ready to “guarantee human dignity, and leave no one behind.”

FINE WORDS. BUT Liberians are entitled to ask how they square with what happened at Roberts International Airport just five weeks ago.

THE DEAL THE SPEECH LEFT OUT

IN AUGUST, LIBERIA agreed to accept up to 1,200 third-country deportees from the United States over the coming year, one of the largest such arrangements under the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown. The first 20 arrived at Roberts International Airport outside Monrovia. They are not Liberians. They include Africans as well as nationals from North America, South America and the Caribbean.

THE GOVERNMENT CALLS this humanitarian. Perhaps. But the facts warrant pause. According to Reuters, these deportees have in most cases won legal protection against repatriation after U.S. immigration judges found they risked torture or other abuses. In other words, Washington cannot legally send them home, so it sends them here.

IMMIGRATION LAWYERS SAY such deportations work as a loophole to push asylum seekers back to their home countries indirectly, and that many end up with little choice but to return to the very places they fled.

Is that what “leave no one behind” means?

NOT LIBERIA ALONE

LIBERIA IS NOT the only African country in this business. At least eight African governments now have confirmed agreements or arrivals, including Eswatini, South Sudan, Ghana, Rwanda, Uganda, Equatorial Guinea, Cameroon and the Central African Republic. The record elsewhere is troubling.

IN ESWATINI, DEPORTEES have been held at a maximum-security prison pending repatriation. Human Rights Watch has warned that transfers to Eswatini, Ghana, Rwanda and South Sudan exposed several hundred people to the risk of arbitrary detention, ill-treatment and refoulement. One regional outlet reports Ghana has repeatedly sent protected deportees home anyway, and that these deals have paid African governments more than $32 million.

SO HERE IS the contradiction. Africa goes to New York demanding to be treated as an equal partner in global decision-making. Yet at the same time, African governments, Liberia among them, are quietly agreeing to serve as holding grounds for people a powerful nation does not want and cannot lawfully return. That is not the posture of a continent seeking a permanent seat. It is the posture of a continent still taking instructions.

WHAT DID WE GET, AND WHAT DID WE GIVE?

LIBERIANS HAVE NOT seen the terms of this deal. The information minister said Liberia will receive U.S. support to manage the program and strengthen its migration system. What support? How much? Who decides who comes? Where will these people live, and who will protect them? What happens if one of them is later sent back to face torture after passing through Liberia’s hands?

A government that told the UN that trust is broken because principles are applied “inconsistently and selectively” cannot keep its own agreements hidden from its own people.

A SEAT MUST MEAN A SPINE

WE SUPPORT AFRICA’S demand for permanent seats on the Security Council. But visibility is not the same as influence, and a seat is worth little if it comes without the courage to say no. If Liberia wants a louder voice on the world stage, it must show that voice is its own and not borrowed from whoever holds the purse.

LIBERIA ALREADY SITS on the Security Council. It could use that seat to demand transparency and legal protections for every African nation being asked to host deportees. It could lead on the rights of migrants rather than quietly serve the policy that tramples them. That would be leadership worthy of a permanent seat.

THE PRESIDENT TOLD the world that Liberia is “living proof that dialogue can overcome division.” Let that dialogue begin at home. Publish the deal. Explain the benefits. And show Liberians that the dignity promised in New York applies at Roberts International Airport too.

World.title: Govt. pushes for competitive construction industry
World.content:
Government has called for a stronger and more competitive Zambian construction industry capable of creating jobs, developing local skills and driving economic growth.

Ministry of Infrastructure Housing and Urban Development Permanent Secretary, Albert Malama says Zambia must build an industry in which local construction companies can grow from small contractors into major firms.

Prof. Malama said this in a speech read on his behalf by National Council for Construction Acting Board Chairperson, Collins Sitali at the Build Zambia 2026 Awards in Lusaka last night.

He said the country should also create opportunities for young engineers, architects, quantity surveyors, artisans and technicians to build meaningful careers.

Prof Malama added that the construction industry should embrace innovation and technology to improve productivity and ensure that infrastructure investment creates opportunities across the economy.

He noted that nations are remembered not only for the infrastructure they build, but also for the people who participate in building it, the standards they maintain and the economic opportunities they create.

“⁹We mast build an industry in which Zambian enterprises can grow from small contractors into major construction companies,” Prof Malama said.

He also commended the National Council for Construction (NCC) for creating a platform that recognises excellence and promotes higher standards in the construction sector.

And NCC Board Chairperson, Collins Sitali has urged players in the construction industry to prioritise quality, professionalism, integrity and responsibility in delivering projects.

In a speech read on his behalf by NCC Board Member Lucy Kanekwa, Mr Sitali said construction goes beyond completing projects, as infrastructure such as roads, schools, hospitals, bridges and houses directly affects people’s lives and contributes to national development.

He said the industry should focus not only on completing contracts and increasing market share, but also on protecting its reputation through quality workmanship.

“Not only to construct more, but to even construct better,” Mr Sitali said.

Meanwhile, Image Construction Limited Founder, Jonathan Mwendabai has called on contractors undertaking Constituency Development Fund (CDF) projects to prioritise quality and ensure communities receive value for money.

Mr Mwendabai said his company’s recognition by NCC in the Small-Scale Contractors and CDF Funded Infrastructure categories has reinforced its commitment to quality project delivery.

He said Image Construction Limited has completed a veterinary office in Serenje, a 1×2 classroom block in Masaiti and health post in Chama, while a warehouse under CDF in Serenje is at an advanced stage and expected to be completed within six weeks.

Mr Mwendabai has encouraged Zambian contractors to uphold quality whenever entrusted with public projects.

“We should just ensure that we deliver, the clients need to have value for their money.”

World.title: Zambia set to join American Giant J.P. Morgan’s market index
World.content:
Zambia is set to enter a new phase of international recognition for its local-currency government bonds as J.P. Morgan prepares to include the country in its new GBI-EM Edge index, covering nearly 330 billion United States dollars in government debt across 26 frontier economies.

Ministry of Information and Media Director Spokesperson, Henry Kapata, says the new GBI-EM Edge is specifically designed for frontier markets, meaning Zambia is now being brought into a new benchmark created for economies at an earlier stage of financial-market development.

Mr KAPATA has told the media business news that the development comes about eight months after President Hakainde Hichilema met investors in a J.P. Morgan-facilitated engagement at State House.

He said it also follows stronger demand for Zambia’s domestic bonds and efforts to increase the size and accessibility of the local bond market.

Mr Kapata explained that the development will help the country continue to rebuild confidence in its economy and domestic financial markets following the debt crisis and restructuring.

The index inclusion is therefore another development to watch as Zambia works to strengthen its financial markets and attract investment.

World.title: Govt, UNDP hands over CRRF Project in Mambwe
World.content:
The National Disaster Risk Management Division (DRMD) says the Community Recovery and Resilience Facility (CRRF) project in Mambwe highlights the importance of investing in disaster preparedness and prevention before disasters occur.

Disaster Risk Management Division National Coordinator, Norman Chipakupaku, says the CRRF investments of about K2.5 Million in Mambwe District, implemented with support from the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and Government is aimed at strengthening the resilience of vulnerable communities to droughts, floods and erratic rainfall.

Speaking during the handover ceremony of the investments in Mambwe, Mr Chipakupaku who was represented by Assistant Secretary for Eastern Province Clement Chilembo, said lessons from the 2023/2024 drought had shown the need for Government and its partners to strengthen community preparedness and resilience instead of relying mainly on emergency response.

He stressed that the CRRF will also serve as a pilot project whose lessons can guide wider disaster risk reduction and climate resilience programmes in other vulnerable communities.

Mr Chipakupaku added that the (CRRF) project includes the drilling and equipping of boreholes in Kajumba Village and at Mambwe Farmer Training Centre, rehabilitation of a borehole in Pitilila, Kakumbi Ward, and construction of two water kiosks.

He revealed that the project also strengthens irrigation at Mnkhanya Farmer Led Irrigation Scheme through the installation of a booster pump and 18 solar panels, alongside the construction of four livestock drinking troughs.

Mr Chipakupaku further noted that the interventions are particularly important as Zambia prepares for anticipated El Niño conditions during the 2026/2027 rainy season.

He said the Mambwe experience shows that investments in water security, climate-smart agriculture, livelihoods, early warning systems and community preparedness can help communities withstand climate shocks and reduce dependence on emergency assistance.

Meanwhile, United Nation Development Programme Resident Representative in Zambia James Wakiaga, represented by Community Recovery Resilience Facility Project Engineer, Patrick Muchimba said the K2.5 million Kwacha had been spent on the project, which has improved access to water for domestic use, irrigation and livestock.

Mr Muchimba, disclosed that the handover transfers responsibility for the investments to local authorities and community structures.

And Chief Mnkhanya’s representative, Ackim Nkhoma also urged the residents to protect the infrastructure from vandalism.

This is contained in a statement issued to the media by Disaster Risk Management Division Senior Communication Officer, Mathews Musukwa.

World.title: Govt. launches Integrated Media Reporting System
World.content:
Government has launched the Integrated Media Reporting System (IMRS), which will strengthen media monitoring, information management, analysis and reporting across institutions under the Ministry of Information and Media.

Speaking during the orientation meeting on the IMRS, Ministry of Information and Media Permanent Secretary, Thabo Kawana, says the system developed by the ministry will enable it to move from fragmented reporting arrangements to a coordinated and integrated reporting framework that supports evidence-based decision-making.

He said the system will also support the ministry in monitoring the implementation of the eight presidential priorities under the presidential delivery unit, the country’s growth agenda and El Niño-related matters.

Mr Kawana stated that the system will help strengthen the ministry’s ability to track achievements, identify challenges, measure impact and provide accurate updates on government programmes and interventions.

He has since urged institutions to support officers nominated to use the system and embrace the IMRS as a strategic tool for improving institutional performance, government communication and reporting.

Mr Kawana commended the Ministry’s Information Communication Technology Unit, Planning Department and other officers involved in developing the system for their efforts.

And Ministry of Information and Media Chief Planner, Peggy Zulu said the introduction of the IMRS is an important step towards modernising the collection, management, analysis and reporting of information.

Ms Zulu said the system is expected to enhance coordination, improve the timeliness and accuracy of reporting, and support effective planning and decision-making.

She said the digital platform will help government institutions improve efficiency and provide timely feedback on achievements and programmes particularly the presidential deliveries.

Ms Zulu encouraged participants to actively participate in the orientation and raise questions to ensure they fully understand how the new system works.

Meanwhile, Ministry of Information and Media Information Technology Senior Systems Analyst, David Mwape said successful adoption of the IMRS will improve institutional performance, coordination between the ministry and institutions under it as well as government line ministries and tracking of government programmes and priorities.

Mr Mwape said the system will also provide reliable historical information, strengthen accountability for submitted information and improve evidence-based planning and decision-making.

The workshop held at the Mass Media Complex was attended by some media heads, Independent Broadcasting Authority Director General Webster Malido, ICT experts, and senior government officials among others.

World.title: Chipasula clinches Denmark move
World.content:
Zambia’s Copper Queens forward Mercy Chipasula has joined top Danish club HB Køge Women.

Both Køge and Chipasula have confirmed the deal without disclosing the contract duration.

Chipasula, 18, joins Køge from Zambian side Kamfinsa Blue Eagles Queens of Kitwe.

Chipasula said moving to Køge will blossom her career.

“I chose to move to the club because I believe that it is the best place for me to develop. I am still young and know that I have a lot to learn, so I feel that HB Køge Women is the right place for me to take the next steps in my career,” she told the club media in Denmark.

“The club’s proud history was also an important reason why I chose to come here. I am really looking forward to getting started and starting a new chapter in my career. I promise to work hard and do everything I can to contribute to the club’s continued success,” said Chipasula.

Sporting Director Jonas Nielsen is pleased to see Chipasula complete her move to Denmark.

“We have been very much looking forward to the paperwork around Mercy’s work permit falling into place, so it is great that she is finally here. Mercy has something extra that we rarely find in young players in Denmark. She is strong one-on-one and can do some things with the ball that we have been missing in the squad,” Nielsen said.

“Therefore, we are also proud that we have managed to sign her in front of some of the biggest clubs in the world, and we are already feeling interest before she has played her first game for us. She has just turned 18, so we have to give her time and be patient. But I would like to promise our fans that we have brought in a player who will entertain,” Nielsen said.

Chipasula has played for the Under-17 and Under-20 National Teams before graduating to the Senior Team.

She represented Zambia at the 2025 and 2026 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations.

Chipasula has been handed number 10 by Køge Women.

World.title: US Backs HH’s New Mandate, Pledges Deeper Cooperation
World.content:
The United States has reaffirmed Zambia’s position as a key strategic partner and called for deeper cooperation in health, investment, critical minerals and border transparency following bilateral talks held on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly (UNGA81) in New York.

The discussions were led by US Deputy Assistant Secretary of State Chris Kulukundis and Zambia’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation Mulambo Haimbe, who represented President Hakainde Hichilema at the meeting.

During the talks, the United States congratulated President Hichilema on his re-election and reiterated its commitment to strengthening a forward-looking partnership with Zambia.

Both countries pledged to deepen cooperation through increased investment, value-addition initiatives and broader economic collaboration aligned with Zambia’s Grow Zambia Agenda.

Minister Haimbe emphasised that economic diplomacy remains central to Zambia’s development strategy, noting that the country highly values its partnership with the United States and views continued collaboration as critical to advancing national development objectives.

The meeting also saw both governments reaffirm their commitment to strengthening bilateral relations across multiple sectors.

The two sides agreed to maintain close communication and continue high-level engagements in both Washington and Lusaka.

The discussions highlighted areas of mutual interest, including economic growth, health cooperation and the responsible development of critical mineral resources.

The bilateral engagement formed part of a series of meetings taking place during UNGA81, where world leaders and senior government officials are convening to address global and regional priorities.

This is according to a statement issued by Namatama Njekwa, First Secretary for Press and Public Relations at the Permanent Mission of the Republic of Zambia to the United Nations.

World.title: Musokotwane Pins Growth on Export Expansion
World.content:
Finance and National Planning Minister Situmbeko Musokotwane says economic growth over the next five years will be driven by increased exports in line with the Grow Zambia Agenda.

Speaking during the 2026 Combined Second and Third Quarter National Development Coordinating Committee Meeting in Lusaka, Dr Musokotwane said increased export earnings would make it easier to reduce the cost of living for Zambians.

Dr Musokotwane also encouraged public and private sector players to attract more foreign direct investment to support economic expansion.

He said the country’s strong Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth and declining inflation should translate into tangible benefits for citizens across the country.

Meanwhile, Permanent Secretary for Economic Management and Finance Mulele Mulele said Central Government’s external debt stock had declined by the end of December 2025.

Mr Mulele attributed the reduction largely to the Government’s Liability Management Operation undertaken during the second quarter of 2026, which included the partial repurchase of Eurobond obligations through the African Development Bank (AfDB).

At the same event, Presidential Delivery Unit Head Kusobile Kamwambi said the unit had already set annual targets to support the implementation of the Grow Zambia Agenda.

Ms Kamwambi said the targets focus on key sectors, including agriculture and food security, energy and infrastructure, the digital economy and innovation, mining and natural resources, among others.

World.title: Hichilema Calls for Fairer Global Health Systems at UN General Assembly
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema has called for stronger and fairer global health systems, telling a high-level meeting on the margins of the United Nations General Assembly that poverty and geography must not decide who gets vaccines, medicines and other health technologies.

The speech was read on his behalf in New York on Thursday by Health Minister Professor Roma Chilengi, at a meeting held alongside the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly. Mr Hichilema said countries should be able to protect their own populations, and that regions should have the capacity to respond together to health threats.

He said a strong public-health system must work at every link in the chain, from detecting an illness to laboratory testing, regional coordination and access to vaccines and treatment.

“Our shared task is to make those systems more dependable, in everyday care and in times of crisis. At the heart of that task are the people who need care and those who provide it,” he said.

The President then turned to how those systems are paid for. He said Zambia’s experience with debt restructuring had reinforced the need to create fiscal space for essential public services, particularly health. He called for timely and workable debt restructuring and, where necessary, debt relief, saying debt agreements should leave countries room to invest in essential services.

On emergency preparedness, Mr Hichilema called for health-security financing that does not worsen debt distress. He said grants should support cross-border preparedness, while concessional lending should remain consistent with debt sustainability.

He also raised concern over declining development assistance, citing preliminary figures from the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) showing a real-terms fall of more than 23 per cent in official development assistance in 2025. Zambia, he said, remained committed to working with health partners while increasing its own domestic investment in programmes addressing HIV, tuberculosis and malaria.

The Head of State asked for carefully planned aid transitions, so that patients do not lose access to essential services when donor support changes.

Climate change was the next point on his list. Mr Hichilema said heat, floods and drought threaten safe water, nutrition, disease control and the continuity of healthcare services. He pointed to Zambia’s 2023–2024 cholera epidemic and the severe drought of 2024 as proof of the close links between health, water, sanitation and food security.

He said no country could manage every cross-border health threat alone, which is why regional preparedness matters.

On access to health technologies, the President said the COVID-19 pandemic had exposed major inequalities in access to vaccines. He said the World Health Organisation (WHO) Pandemic Agreement offered a chance to build a fairer system, particularly through arrangements on pathogen access and benefit-sharing. Countries that share pathogen samples and genetic information, he said, should receive timely access to vaccines, diagnostics and treatments in return.

He also called for increased regional production, pooled procurement, technology sharing, predictable demand, effective regulation and investment in research and development.

“Africa must produce knowledge and solutions, not only receive products,” he said.

Mr Hichilema asked countries to create and use fiscal space for health by bringing finance and health authorities, creditors and development partners together around credible investment priorities, timely debt solutions and transparent delivery.

At home, he said, Zambia’s 2026 National Budget allocated K26.2 billion, equivalent to about US$1.1 billion, to health services, representing about 10.3 per cent of the national budget. He said the investment should translate into tangible improvements, including the recruitment of health workers, stronger health infrastructure, the availability of medicines and improved access to healthcare.
