World.title: 5 ways India is kicking car safety into top gear with Bharat NCAP 2.0: What buyers need to know
World.content:
Bharat NCAP 2.0, planned for October 2027, will look beyond what happens when a car crashes. The proposed system will examine the entire safety chain: from how a vehicle helps avoid a collision to how well it protects occupants, pedestrians and other vulnerable road users, and what happens after an accident.

Union road transport and highways minister Nitin Gadkari announced the proposed timeline at the SIAM Annual Convention in September 2026. The second phase is being planned as the first phase of Bharat New Car Assessment Programme, or Bharat NCAP, approaches the end of its current cycle.

According to the ministry of road transport and highwaysâ draft AIS-197 Revision 1, the first phase of Bharat NCAP began on October 1, 2023 and is valid until September 30, 2027.

The draft revision has been prepared as the framework for Bharat NCAP 2.0.

The proposed changes could make the safety rating a much broader measure of a carâs performance, not just in a crash, but before, during and after one.

About Bharat NCAP

What is Bharat NCAP?

Bharat NCAP is Indiaâs own vehicle crash-testing and safety-rating programme. It was formally launched by the ministry of road transport and highways in August 2023 and became operational from October 1, 2023.





The programme applies to type-approved passenger vehicles in the M1 category with a gross vehicle weight of less than 3.5 tonnes. It is voluntary, which means manufacturers can offer eligible vehicles for assessment.

The programme is anchored by the Central Institute of Road Transport (CIRT), while testing is carried out through designated agencies with the required infrastructure.

At its core, Bharat NCAP gives car buyers a common safety benchmark.

A vehicle must already meet mandatory regulatory requirements to be sold in India. Bharat NCAP goes a step further by putting eligible vehicles through specified tests and awarding them a rating of between one and five stars.

India's own car safety assessment programme

The idea is fairly simple: instead of looking only at a carâs price, design or features, buyers get an additional reference point to understand how the vehicle performs in standardised safety tests.

The government has also positioned the programme as a way to encourage manufacturers to improve vehicle safety and strengthen the safety standards of cars made in India.

How does the current Bharat NCAP system work?

The existing programme broadly assesses three areas:

Adult Occupant Protection (AOP)

(AOP) Child Occupant Protection (COP)

(COP) Safety Assist Technologies (SAT)

Vehicles are subjected to prescribed crash tests and other assessments. Their performance across these parameters is then used to arrive at the overall star rating.

The current framework includes a 64 kmph offset frontal impact test, a 50 kmph side movable deformable barrier test and a pole side impact test, among other checks prescribed under AIS-197.

The assessment therefore goes beyond simply asking whether the passenger compartment remains intact.

Adult Occupant Protection examines the risk of injury to adults in different crash conditions and seating positions. Child Occupant Protection looks at the protection offered to younger passengers, including the use and installation of child restraint systems.

Safety Assist Technologies, meanwhile, covers technologies designed to help prevent crashes or reduce their severity.

Quote

Why are adult and child safety assessed separately?

A car may offer different levels of protection to adults and children, so Bharat NCAP evaluates the two separately.

The adult assessment focuses on occupant protection during prescribed crash scenarios, while the child assessment considers how effectively younger occupants are protected and how child restraint systems work within the vehicle.

This also means that a carâs overall star rating is not simply a score from one crash test.

It reflects performance across several safety parameters.

For consumers, the individual scores can therefore provide more information than looking at the star rating alone.

Who tests the cars?

Bharat NCAP is anchored by CIRT, with testing carried out through designated testing agencies that have the required facilities.

The wider automotive testing ecosystem includes agencies such as the Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) and the International Centre for Automotive Technology (ICAT).

Manufacturers submit eligible vehicles for assessment under the programme. The existing framework specifies procedures around the variant selected for testing, including provisions concerning the base variant of a model.

That distinction matters when reading a Bharat NCAP result. A rating should not automatically be assumed to apply to every variant of a model unless the official assessment covers those variants.

Four assessments of NCAP

Bharat NCAP ratings

Bharat NCAP ratings range from one to five stars. A higher rating indicates stronger performance under the programmeâs prescribed assessment criteria.

But a five-star rating is not a guarantee that occupants will escape injury in every real-world crash. NCAP testing is conducted under standardised conditions and is intended to provide a basis for comparing vehicle safety performance.

It is also important to distinguish Bharat NCAP from the mandatory certification requirements for selling a vehicle in India.

Bharat NCAP is voluntary and is designed to provide consumers with additional information beyond the mandatory regulatory framework. A vehicle being tested or rated under Bharat NCAP should therefore not be confused with regulatory approval.

Since its launch, Bharat NCAP has increasingly become part of the safety conversation around new car launches. The ratings have also become a factor in how manufacturers present their vehicles to consumers, particularly as safety becomes a more visible consideration in the passenger-vehicle market.

What do the stars represent?

So, what changes with Bharat NCAP 2.0?

This is where the proposed second phase takes a much wider approach.

The draft AIS-197 Revision 1 divides Bharat NCAP 2.0 into five safety verticals:

Safe driving Crash avoidance Crash protection Vulnerable road user protection Post-crash safety

The change is significant because the current system focuses mainly on occupant protection and safety-assist technologies, while the proposed framework looks at the complete safety chain.

The draft framework uses a 100-point assessment structure, with Crash Protection accounting for 55% of the assessment.

The remaining weightage covers the other safety areas.

In other words, the crash itself will still be a major part of the rating, but it will no longer be the only part of the safety story.

Five crash tests in the proposed new framework

Bharat NCAP 2.0 proposes expanding the Crash Protection assessment to five mandatory crash tests:

64 kmph offset frontal impact against a deformable barrier

against a deformable barrier 50 kmph frontal impact against a full-width rigid barrier

against a full-width rigid barrier 50 kmph lateral impact against a mobile deformable barrier

against a mobile deformable barrier 32 kmph oblique side impact against a rigid pole

against a rigid pole 50 kmph rear impact against a mobile rigid barrier

Adult and child occupant protection will continue to be assessed separately.

The addition of full-width frontal and rear-impact tests means the proposed system will examine crash scenarios beyond the core tests in the existing framework.

That gives the second phase a wider testing footprint and allows different types of impacts to form part of the overall safety assessment.

Not just about surviving crash

One of the biggest differences in Bharat NCAP 2.0 is that the programme is designed to look at what happens before a crash as well.

Crash Avoidance is one of the five proposed verticals. It focuses on technologies and vehicle characteristics that can help prevent a collision or reduce its severity.

Your guide to safer cars

Safe Driving is another proposed category, widening the assessment beyond the vehicleâs passive protection features.

Together, these categories shift the focus from simply asking, âHow well does this car perform when it crashes?â to a broader question: âHow does this vehicle contribute to safety across different stages of a road incident?â

Bharat NCAP 2.0 also proposes a separate Vulnerable Road User Protection category.

This brings pedestrians and other vulnerable road users more directly into the safety assessment.

The proposed framework also asks a different question: what happens once the collision has taken place?

Post-Crash Safety is one of the five proposed assessment areas. Minister Gadkari described Bharat NCAP 2.0 as covering the entire safety chain, including post-crash evacuation and care. âWe are going to evaluate the entire crash chain,â Gadkari said, adding that new technologies developed globally as well as by startups would be considered under the programme.

This means the assessment is intended to extend beyond the instant of impact and examine safety considerations in the period immediately after a crash.

It adds another layer to the programmeâs approach: avoiding the crash where possible, protecting people during the impact, and addressing safety after the collision.

What does Bharat NCAP mean for car buyers?

For buyers, Bharat NCAP offers an additional way to compare cars beyond mandatory safety requirements.

A consumer can look at a vehicleâs overall rating as well as its adult and child protection performance and the safety technologies considered in the assessment.

The rating is not meant to replace other factors involved in buying a car. Price, size, fuel efficiency, features, driving requirements and other considerations remain relevant, but the proposed 2.0 framework would expand that information further.

Buyers could eventually have a broader picture of how a car performs across crash protection, crash avoidance, safe driving, vulnerable-road-user protection and post-crash safety.

Bharat NCAP is one part of a much larger road-safety challenge, focusing on the structure of vehicles. Vehicle design and safety technology can influence the outcome of a crash, but they cannot address every reason why accidents happen.

The ministry has identified several factors associated with road crashes, including speeding, mobile-phone use, drunken driving, wrong-side driving, lane indiscipline, jumping red lights and failure to use helmets and seat belts.

Vehicle condition, road conditions and weather can also play a role.

Several countries have their own NCAPS

Government data recorded 1,68,491 road accident fatalities in 2022.

Bharat NCAP therefore addresses one part of this wider equation: the safety performance of vehicles. Its proposed second phase would broaden that role by looking at what a vehicle can do to help avoid crashes, how it protects people when a crash occurs, how it protects vulnerable road users and what happens afterwards.

The bottom line

The current Bharat NCAP phase remains valid until September 30, 2027. The government has proposed introducing Bharat NCAP 2.0 from October 2027, with the draft AIS-197 Revision 1 serving as the framework for the next phase.

The proposed transition would take Indiaâs vehicle safety-rating system from a relatively focused crash and occupant-protection programme to a broader safety assessment.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The familiar one-to-five-star rating would remain the consumer-facing language of vehicle safety, but the assessment behind it is set to become much more comprehensive.

The bigger shift is in the question Bharat NCAP is trying to answer. Instead of looking only at how a car performs when it is involved in a crash, the proposed system would examine the vehicleâs safety journey from avoiding a collision to protecting occupants and vulnerable road users, and supporting safety after the crash.

That could give Indian car buyers a wider set of safety information to consider when choosing their next vehicle.

World.title: Afspa extended by six months in 'disturbed areas' of Manipur, Nagaland and Arunachal Pradesh
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Centre has extended the Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act, 1958 (Afspa), in specified areas of Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh and Manipur for another six months from October 1, according to Gazette notifications issued on Friday.

The extension follows a review of the law and order situation in the affected areas of the three northeastern states.

The Afspa, which grants special powers to the armed forces, will remain in force in these areas for six months from October 1, unless withdrawn earlier, according to the notification.

The government order cited Section 3 of the act, which empowers the Centre to declare specified areas as "disturbed areas."

Which are these 'disturbed areas'

In Manipur, the ministry of home affairs has extended the âdisturbed areaâ declaration across the state, excluding areas under the jurisdiction of 13 police stations in five districts.

The excluded areas are those under Imphal, Lamphel, City, Singjamei, Patsoi and Wangoi police stations in Imphal West district; Porompat, Heingang and Irilbung police stations in Imphal East; Thoubal police station in Thoubal district; Bishnupur and Nambol police stations in Bishnupur district; and Kakching police station in Kakching district.





In Nagaland, the Afspa has been extended to nine districts â Dimapur, Niuland, Chumoukedima, Mon, Kiphire, Noklak, Phek, Peren and Meluri â which have been declared âdisturbed areasâ under Section 3 of the Act.

The notification also covers areas under the jurisdiction of 21 police stations in five other districts of Nagaland: Kohima, Mokokchung, Longleng, Wokha and Zunheboto.

âInnovation without access has limited impact, and access without evidence cannot be sustained. For India to build a globally competitive medical technology ecosystem, we need stronger indigenous research and development, credible clinical evidence, appropriate health technology assessment and sustainable reimbursement mechanisms.

Manufacturing must be supported by the right clinical skills, infrastructure and technical ecosystem.

Our ultimate objective must be Indian innovation, global-quality technology and affordable access for every patient who needs it.â

Our regulatory system must evolve to ensure products developed in India meet globally credible standards. We also need to strengthen domestic supply chains, engineering capabilities and component manufacturing. This will support healthcare access while contributing to employment and the countryâs prosperity.

â

Dr Prashant P. Joshi

âMedical institutions should not be limited to validating technologies developed elsewhere; they should identify unmet clinical needs and work with engineers, researchers and innovators to develop solutions.

Stronger collaboration between medical and engineering institutions through joint research, academic programmes, fellowships and training can significantly strengthen Indiaâs medical technology ecosystem.

â

Dr Gaurav Shanker Pradhan

âAccess to medical technology is not simply about making a device available. Meaningful impact is possible only when healthcare professionals can use it safely, confidently and effectively.

Dr Shailesh Kumar Yadav, IAS, Joint Director, National Health Authority

Technologies should be introduced systematically and evaluated through comparative, data-based studies.â

Dr Shivaji Kalge

Continued investment in research, quality and innovation can help these technologies gain wider acceptance globally while improving access to quality healthcare.â

Indiaâs healthcare landscape is evolving rapidly, with medical technology playing an increasingly important role in improving diagnosis, treatment and patient outcomes. Against this backdrop, and as the country works towards expanding access to quality and affordable healthcare, the Indian Medical Parliamentariansâ Forum (IMPF) convened the National Policy Summit on MedTech Access on September 22 at Meril Academy, Vapi, under the theme â.â The summit brought together Members of Parliament, senior government officials, healthcare institutions, clinical experts and industry stakeholders to discuss strengthening Indiaâs medical technology ecosystem and expanding access to quality, advanced and affordable healthcare technologies.Established in 2006, IMPF is a non-partisan platform for Members of Parliament from the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha with backgrounds in medicine and healthcare. Discussions covered clinical evidence, health technology assessment, financing and reimbursement, technology adoption, healthcare workforce capabilities and extending advanced technologies across different levels of the health system. The panel was chaired by Dr Jashvantsinh Parmar and moderated by Dr Sharmila Sarkar, with Dr Gaurav Shanker Pradhan, Dr Shailesh Kumar Yadav and Dr Suchita Markan as panellists.Speaking at the summit, Dr Anil Sukhdeorao Bonde said,, said,Highlighting the role of healthcare institutions,said,On clinical adoption and capacity building,said,, highlighted the importance of financing and reimbursement. He said,Emphasising health-system requirements,said,Speaking on grassroots healthcare delivery,said,Highlighting the potential of domestic manufacturers,said,The summit also included representatives from the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), National Health Authority, government medical institutions, clinical experts and industry associations.The discussions underscored the need for a coordinated approach spanning indigenous innovation, evidence generation, regulatory quality, clinical education, health technology assessment, financing, reimbursement and institutional adoption, while connecting MedTech innovation with the needs of healthcare providers and patients, particularly in underserved areas.

World.title: Evening news wrap: CJP's Dipke urges opposition to boycott 'rigged polls'; Air India suspends pilot found tipsy before Zurich-Delhi flight & more
World.content:
Air India has suspended the pilot found unfit to fly due to intoxication before a Zurich-Delhi flight, prompting the DGCA to seek tighter checks.

CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke has asked opposition parties to stop contesting elections if they truly believe the process is rigged.

has asked opposition parties to stop contesting elections if they truly believe the process is rigged. The Delhi high court has ordered police protection for a woman and the takedown of an alleged deepfake photo of her with PM Modi, posted by CJP leaders.

Imran Khan's son has warned PTI supporters against marching to Adiala jail on September 27, fearing it could be used as a pretext to endanger his father's life.

14 Kazakh servicemen have died after being swept into the Caspian Sea during a naval exercise, prompting the detention of five defence officials.

Here are the top 5 news stories of the day

Air India pilot found tipsy just before operating Zurich-Delhi flight, suspended

Air India has suspended the pilot found tipsy ahead of operating a Zurich-Delhi flight on September 6, forcing the flight to be rescheduled until alternate crew was arranged.

The Swiss aviation authority alerted India's DGCA about the incident, which has since asked the airline to improve its checks and balances following similar issues in recent months.

'You will be handed a few wins': Amid SIR row, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke asks opposition parties to stop contesting in 'rigged' polls

Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke has urged opposition parties to boycott elections if they believe the process is rigged, arguing that continued participation legitimises polls they themselves question. In a post on X on Friday, Dipke said parties couldn't claim rigging while still contesting.

Delhi high court orders removal of deepfake pics showing woman with PM Modi; notice issued to CJP leaders, cops

The Delhi High Court has granted police protection to a woman who alleged CJP leaders Saurav Das, Abhijit Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Ratna Singh posted a deepfake picture of her with PM Modi, leading to threats against her. The court ordered immediate takedown of the photos, noting it concerned both the woman and the Prime Minister.

'Could endanger his life': Imran Khan's son warns against Adiala jail protest

Imran Khan's son Kasim Khan has urged PTI supporters not to march towards Rawalpindi's Adiala jail during the party's planned September 27 protest, warning that authorities could use such a move as a pretext for a "counter" assault on the prison, endangering his father's life.





Imran Khan is currently held there.

14 Kazakh military personnel killed during naval exercise, five naval officers detained over negligence suspicion

14 Kazakh military personnel were killed after being swept away by the Caspian Sea while disembarking from a patrol boat during a naval exercise on Thursday, with three others rescued from the total of 17 washed away. Authorities detained five defence officials on Friday in connection with the incident.

World.title: 'Becoming a good citizen more important': BJP chief Nitin Nabin's message to youth amid party's outreach push
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

national president

on Friday urged young people to focus on becoming âgood citizensâ, saying it is "more important" than becoming a good engineer or doctor.

âOne may become a good engineer or doctor, but becoming a good citizen is more important,â PTI quoted Nabin as saying at a âYuva Samvadâ programme at Birla Auditorium in Jaipur.

He further advised youngsters not to fear failure and to avoid shortcuts in life, saying this would lead them to the right destination.

âLife is precious. If you face failure, you should not immediately go in the wrong direction or put your life at stake. If we have been given this life, we should do something meaningful for our parents and for this land,â the BJP chief added.

World.title: 'This cannot be tolerated': Vijay hits out at 'DMK family' over remarks against women
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

C Joseph Vijay turned his attack on the "DMK family" on Friday, taking issue of "derogatory" remarks against women and declaring that he would not let them pass.

Addressing supporters ahead of the October 6 Chengalpattu assembly bypoll, TVK supremo Vijay said he had ignored remarks made against his own mother but drew the line when comments were directed at "my sisters and mothers in Tamil Nadu".

The TVK chief accused the DMK and the "DMK family" of making such remarks and alleged that DMK party head and former CM

and his family had allowed such language.

"This cannot be tolerated," Vijay said.

Vijay also alleged that Stalin and other DMK leaders had spoken in a "defamatory" manner about former Tamil Nadu chief minister

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

.

His remarks came as he stepped up his attack on the DMK ahead of the bypoll, while also targeting the AIADMK and BJP.

Vijay accused the three rival parties of having a "secret understanding, collusion", suggesting that they were working together on issues despite being political opponents.

The TVK chief also referred to the controversy surrounding industrialist Veeramani and alleged that a complaint in a POCSO case had been buried during the previous DMK regime.

"What was the deal, Tamil Nadu is asking. Stalin sir, open your mouth, joining hands with you the AIADMK is also not opening its mouth; should there be a collusion even in this issue, will you not open your mouth by having an understanding even in this matter," he said.

On the issue of crimes against women and children, Vijay said those involved should face punishment regardless of their influence.

World.title: Visakhapatnam City Police arrest 102 in 74 property crime cases
World.content:
The Visakhapatnam City Police arrested 102 persons for their allegedly involvement in 74 different property offence cases in August 2026. The police teams also recovered ₹53.12 lakh worth property from the offenders.

Addressing a press conference at the police conference hall on Friday, Commissioner of Police, Shankabratha Bagchi said that in August, as many as 97 property offences were reported across various parts of the city. Special teams formed under the guidance of the senior police officials, detected 74 cases and arrested 102 individuals.

The recovered property included 796 grams of gold, 9500 grams of silver, ₹14.75 lakh worth cash, and 25 motorcycles.

The police have also recovered 405 missing mobiles worth ₹60.75 lakh.

Out of the 74 detected cases, five cases are of robbery, one case of House Breaking (HB) by day, seven cases of HBs by night, five cases of snatchings, 24 cases of motorcycle thefts, and other property offences.

Mr Bagchi said that as part of preventive measures, during the month of August, 661 CCTV cameras were installed at various places in the city. As many as 472 crime awareness meetings were conducted by the officers. He said that special patrolling is being arranged in crime prone areas during the day and at night. Drone beats continue in isolated areas for surveillance over criminals and illegal activities, he said.

During the programme, the CP and other crime wing officials handed over the recovered property to their rightful owners.

World.title: Farmers in Vizianagaram district bear the brunt of incessant rain
World.content:
Vizianagaram district bore the brunt of incessant rains as over 15,000 acres of standing crop have been damaged and 1,500 families have been evacuated from low-lying areas after the officials of the irrigation department on Friday released 24,000 cusecs of water from Madduvalasa reservoir in Rajam Assembly constituency due to rising water levels in Vegavathi and Suvarnamukhi rivers.

Rajam Telugu Desam Party (TDP) MLA Kondru Murali Mohan visited flood-affected villages in Vangara mandal and assured a quick support from the government to the villagers. He directed TDP leaders and workers to take up service activities in the flood-affected villages after residents complained that they would suffer financial losses due to crop damage. The legislator directed TDP leaders and activists to take up service activities in the flood-affected villages such as Koppara, Kondachakarapalli, Geetanapalli, and Patuvardhanam.

Thotapalli reservoir located near Parvatipuram has received huge waters from catchment areas. Around 23,250 cusecs of water from the Nagavali River was discharged from the reservoir on Friday afternoon. The impact of floods in Parvatipuram-Manyam district has been less compared to Vizianagaram and Srikakulam. However, the two-day rain proved to be a relief for the residents of the district.

World.title: Rain-related death toll in Andhra Pradesh rises to nine
World.content:
Four more rain-related deaths were reported on Friday, taking the total count during the heavy rains triggered by the deep depression over the Bay of Bengal in Andhra Pradesh to nine. The death count was five till Thursday night (September 24).

A 60-year-old man, identified as Punem Bhaskar Rao (60), was washed away in a swelling stream near Kannapuram in Buttaigudem mandal of Eluru district late on Thursday night.

The incident occurred when Bhaskar Rao was trying to cross the overflowing stream on his way to his village, said the local residents.

In another incident, one person died and nine more were injured when a fish-laden lorry overturned near Pathuru village in Bhimadole mandal of Eluru district amid heavy rains.

The deceased has been identified as Ranjit Shah (53), a native of West Bengal. The injured were admitted to a government hospital nearby, the Bhimadole police said.

Meanwhile, two siblings were electrocuted at Jatlapalem village of Pentapadu mandal in West Godavari district on Friday, pushing the total electrocution death toll to seven.

Surya (14) and Sai (12) were electrocuted after they came in contact with an earthing GI wire that was live.

Road cut-off

The road link between Tiruvuru and Utukuru and the neighbouring villages in NTR District was cut off after the main road was submerged on Friday. The police suspended vehicular traffic on the stretch and arranged a picket, said Mylavaram Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) P. Ramchandra Rao.

Trees were uprooted at Tadigadapa and Krishnalanka due to heavy rains in Vijayawada. The officials cleared the roads and resumed traffic on Friday.

World.title: ED searches 16 premises linked to Attica Gold, seizes ₹7.52 lakh in cash and valuables
World.content:
The Directorate of Enforcement (ED), Bengaluru Zonal Office, has seized ₹7.52 lakh in cash, foreign currency, gold jewellery, and silver articles during searches at 16 premises linked to Attica Gold Private Limited and others across Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, and Visakhapatnam.

The searches were conducted on Wednesday and Thursday under Section 17 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002, the ED said in a release on Friday.

The searches targeted the company, its shareholders, and directors over allegations of habitual purchase of stolen gold articles and the generation of proceeds of crime. The premises searched included the residences of directors, former directors, and shareholders, as well as the head office and branches of Attica Gold Private Limited and others.

The ED said its investigation was initiated based on multiple FIRs and charge sheets filed by police in various stations over allegations of habitual purchase, acquisition, and dealing in stolen gold articles. The information from the FIRs was supplemented by information gathered by the agency regarding alleged money laundering activities, it added.

According to the ED, the key persons in the case, including P.S. Ayub alias Bommanahalli Babu, Obedulla A., Mohammed Salman A., and Arbin Taj, did not cooperate with the search proceedings and remained absconding. The agency also alleged that employees at the business premises were instructed by the key persons to remain unavailable during the searches.

World.title: Wellness clinic owner arrested again for alleged sexual assault
World.content:
The owner of a wellness clinic and fitness centre in Payyanur was arrested again on charges of attempting to sexually assault a woman who had approached the facility for physiotherapy. He was produced before the First Class Judicial Magistrate Court at Taliparamaba and remanded in judicial custody.

Sharath Nambiar, 44, owner of the clinic, was arrested following a complaint by the 34-year-old woman who hails from Kasaragod.

The woman had reportedly visited the facility for treatment in October and November 2024. She alleged that the incident occurred when she revisited the clinic in March 2025.

The alleged assault came to light when she disclosed it during a counselling session. She later approached the Payyanur police, who registered a case and arrested Mr. Nambiar.

He had been arrested in July 2024 following a similar complaint of alleged sexual assault by a 20-year-old woman from Payyanur.

World.title: Election Commission row LIVE: Delhi Police detain around 50 protesters over Jantar Mantar agitation seeking CEC's arrest
World.content:
The Congress party held protests across the country as the Opposition steps up its demand over Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation. At Jantar Mantar in New Delhi, several protesters were detained during an agitation by AISA seeking Mr. Kumar’s arrest. New Delhi DCP Sachin Sharma said that 40-50 protesters were detained in the capital city as no permission had been sought or granted to hold the protest at the venue.

Meanwhile, the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke threatened to launch a “Jantar Mantar 2.0” and nationwide agitation on October ‌2 if the CEC removal demand was not met. He also urged opposition parties to stop participating in elections if they believe the electoral process is being rigged, saying their continued participation only legitimises such polls and creates an “illusion” that they are free and fair.

Also read: Opposition calls for CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s removal after report on Election Commissioners’ dissent

The row follows an Indian Express report stating that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had formally objected at least 14 times over 10 months, alleging that key decisions were taken in the name of the full Commission without their knowledge, some of them “unauthorised and illegal.”

The Election Commission said “differing views” are part of its decision-making process, as the poll panel carries out a nationwide revision of the electoral database.

Also watch: LoP Rahul Gandhi addresses Delhi press briefing amid ECI dissent row over SIR

World.title: 18th IDSFFK begins under a cloud of censorship
World.content:
The 18th edition of the International Documentary and Short Film Festival of Keralam got under way here on Friday under a cloud of censorship as uncertainty remained over the 31 films for which the Union Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (I&B) has denied censor exemption. Inaugurating the festival at the Kairali theatre in the capital, Minister for Cultural Affairs P.C. Vishnunadh said that the Kerala State Chalachitra Academy is making all possible efforts, including legal measures, to secure permission for screening.

The screening schedule for the festival, which has been released, now has omitted the 31 films, with the academy planning to update the schedule if permission is secured. According to sources, the Union I&B Ministry has forwarded some of the films for approval to the Defence Ministry, while some have been sent to the External Affairs Ministry.

“Our wish is that all the films that the selection committee selected for the festival be screened. They had selected a total of 347 documentaries and short films from out of 1,800 submissions. The I&B Ministry sought detailed synopsis for 40 films, out of which 31 films are now held up,” said Mr. Vishnunadh.

Academy chairperson

Although it was rumoured that the Minister would make the long-pending announcement of the chalachitra academy chairperson’s name at the opening ceremony, he said that the name will be announced before the closing of the festival. He said steps are progressing to grant industry status to Malayalam cinema.

“One of the issues that we have been facing is that we don’t have any models before us, as no other State has granted industry status to cinema. On the other hand, while trying to grant industry status to the tourism sector, we had so many models because only our State remained to make that declaration. The government has decided to take decisive steps to promote the film sector. A special programme is planned for young documentary filmmakers by bringing together academia and film societies,” he said.

Filmmaker Adoor Gopalakrishnan, the chief guest at the function, said the festival provides a great platform for viewing and discussing serious works of cinema for aspiring filmmakers.

“Keralam is the only State to have its own government-run festival for documentaries and short films. We were keen to have such a festival as normally such films don’t get a release in the cinemas nor would any of the channels show documentaries,” he said.

Opening film

After the inaugural ceremony, the opening film A Fox Under a Pink Moondirected by Mehrdad Oskouei focussing on the struggles of 16-year-old Afghan artist Soraya, who has spent five years trying to escape Iran for Austria, was screened.

The second day of the festival on Saturday will witness the commencement of the competition section screenings. The Competition Short Documentary category features a compelling line-up of films, including Syed Ahmad Rufai’s Anhad: A Way of Looking, Malavika V.N.’s At Reel’s End (Viraamam), Debalina Majumder’s Friends of Jilipibala, Rahul Sood’s Boulevard - The Royal Route, and Sraiyanti’s Auto Queens.

The Competition Short Fiction category launches with standout selections such as Shashank Sahith Nammikanti’s Everything is Connected, Manguirish J. Bandodkar’s Ancessao, Christopher Joseph’s Maayan, Kiran Narayan Dhamale’s Aata Tu Motha Jhalas, and Darwin Annakumar’s Maram Marankothi.

Additionally, the Competition Long Documentaries section will showcase powerful works including Avijit Banerjee’s The Raconteur of the Dark and Kamal K.M.’s Close Up Up Close -The Making of Political Ubu.

World.title: Vijay accuses DMK of covering up POCSO Act case against Veeramani, questions AIADMK’s silence
World.content:
Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) president and Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on Friday (September 25, 2026) accused the DMK of covering up the POCSO Act case against Gem Granites owner R. Veeramani, though the case was registered when the party was in power.

At a meeting organised as part of his campaign for the Assembly byelection in Madurantanakam (reserved for the Scheduled Caste), Mr. Vijay asked DMK president and former Chief Minister M.K. Stalin to “reveal what deal had taken place behind the scenes” and criticised the AIADMK for keeping silent on the issue, asking whether it had an “understanding” with the DMK even on this issue.

He alleged that the accused had been ruining the lives of young girls for many years, and though the case came up during DMK rule, it was covered up. The accused were now arrested. The victims were children, he said, asking what the DMK and the AIADMK were doing all these years if they could not speak about the children’s pain.

At the meeting at a venue adjoining the Attur toll plaza, about 90 km south of Chennai on the Chennai-Tiruchi National Highway, Mr. Vijay, who canvassed votes for the TVK-led Secular Social Justice Victory Alliance’s nominee Maragatham Kumaravel, alleged that the DMK had been continuously spreading slander against the TVK and him.

Mr. Vijay said the reason for his success in the film industry as well as in politics was the people of Tamil Nadu, whom he considered his family. Because of that relationship, the TVK was able to secure 35% of the votes in the Assembly election and emerge as the single largest party in nearly two-and-a-half years of its formation, he said.

He also claimed Mr. Stalin had spoken in a derogatory manner about former Chief Minister Jayalalithaa and the video was still going viral. Not only Mr. Stalin but also his family members and senior functionaries of the DMK had been speaking in a derogatory manner and people were closely watching this. While the DMK members were spreading slander, the AIADMK was supporting it, he alleged. Throughout his speech, Mr. Vijay referred to the AIADMK as “many others”, barring one instance in which he named the party.

Having decided to join hands with those who had spoken derogatorily about Jayalalithaa, the AIADMK stood exposed and its “mask had been torn off”, he said. Calling the AIADMK “a branch of the BJP”, Mr. Vijay said it had now become a local unit of the DMK. He claimed that the DMK and the AIADMK had colluded and plotted to prevent him from coming to power.

“The reason why I spoke about the history of corruption in the Assembly was to tell the younger generation where the source of corruption was. When I raised the issue of the history of corruption, the DMK said I was not even born then. So what? History would show their corruption. Through the DMK, corruption was already born. So what is the point of asking when I was born,” he said.

According to him, whenever he spoke about corruption in the Assembly, the DMK asked him to produce evidence. Even when he produced evidence, the DMK said it had to be proved in court. If a counterargument was put forward, he said, the response was that matters pending in court could not be discussed in the Assembly.

“Even before I began my Assembly speech, I clearly said I am not going to talk about court cases. But the Opposition kept shouting. As this was my first Assembly experience, I was initially confused about whether to speak when they shouted. However, I understood their intention that they did not want me to speak. That’s why I had to shout so that my voice would reach the people,” he said.

He said he had developed a thick skin and had seen all sorts of slander for 34 years before entering politics. He said that as Chief Minister, he had gone to inspect a bridge [Metro Rail viaduct at Kathipara], when Mr. Stalin said, “Why is [Mr.] Vijay standing on the bridge we built and shooting? Was that bridge built on [Mr] Stalin’s own money? From where did the cheque go? Was it from Gopalapuram [where former Chief Minister M. Karunanidhi lived] or Chittaranjan Salai [where Mr. Stalin resides].”

Having only ₹10,000 in cash and no car [a reference to Mr. Stalin’s assets declared in his election affidavit], Mr. Vijay wondered how he had built a bridge. “Did he construct it with the unaccountable money,” he asked.

He said the DMK’s electoral arithmetic and calculations had not worked during the elections and claimed its calculations of taking a shortcut to somehow topple his government now would not work. He said the bond between the people of Tamil Nadu and him was beyond politics.

He said when he assumed office as Chief Minister, he had asked for some time to implement the poll promises due to the severe financial crunch in the exchequer. “Even in that situation, I have been attempting to fulfil promises that I could. Now that the Opposition is alleging that even I am [the Tamil Nadu government] also taking loans. Yes, I am taking loans, not to loot, but to do good for the people,” he said.

He asked how loyal cadres of former Chief Ministers M.G. Ramachandran and Jayalalithaa could accept a plan to form a government by joining hands with the DMK, which they repeatedly referred to as the “evil force”. He said AIADMK cadres were deeply hurt and that this was the reason why Maragatham Kumaravel, despite winning the Madurantakam seat, resigned and joined the TVK.

He accused the DMK of frightening people with a claim that the BJP would enter the State. “But the BJP itself was struggling to breathe. There is no difference between the DMK and the BJP. Delhi’s DMK is the BJP and Tamil Nadu’s BJP is the DMK. The DMK is waiting for the BJP to introduce the delimitation Bill so that it could join hands with it,” he claimed.

The TVK leader alleged that out of frustration at being unable to make any allegation against the TVK, the DMK had taken up the “dangerous weapon” of slandering women. “When they spoke in a derogatory manner against my mother, I tolerated it. However, I cannot tolerate such remarks against the women of the State by the DMK leadership and cadres. Mr. Stalin and his family members were enjoying such remarks,” Mr. Vijay said.

Mr. Vijay appealed to the people to vote for the TVK’s ‘Whistle’ symbol and said every vote cast for it would be the biggest punishment for those who spoke derogatorily about women. He said voting for either the DMK or the AIADMK would amount to supporting those who spoke in a derogatory manner about women.

World.title: Info ministry dismisses Afghan claims of destroying Pakistani post near border in Balochistan as 'fake'
World.content:
The information ministry dismissed on Friday claims by the Afghan defence ministry of a Pakistani post having been destroyed near the Spin Boldak border — the frontier between Balochistan and Kandahar — as “fake and fabricated”.

The information ministry also took note of Afghan claims that there had been no casualties among the Afghan forces in the latest episode of clash between the two sides.

“The claim is fake and fabricated. As per actual facts, an attempted Afghan aggression in the Gulistan sector was thwarted on night between Sept 24 and Sept 25, and during the process and subsequent heavy punishment inflicted on opposing Taliban posts, at least 13 Afghan Taliban personnel were killed and several injured,” the information ministry said in a post on X.

It also shared visuals in the post, which the ministry said were of the incident.

The incident, it added, had already been “widely covered by media and circulated extensively across social media, providing visual evidence of the border engagement and punishment inflicted on the Afghan Taliban after their cowardly attack”.

“The […] Afghan ministry’s attempt is no surprise since the Taliban are habitual liars having no moral and reputational standing,” it added.

The latest clash has taken place amid an uptick in tensions at the Pak-Afghan border.

Pakistan conducted precision aerial and drone strikes in 10 locations across Afghanistan on Thursday in retaliation for drones launched from the neighbouring country a day earlier.

The response came after eight drones, launched from Afghanistan, entered Pakistani airspace near the Torkham border and Kohat on Wednesday. Security sources said they were subsequently shot down. It was also reported that the Afghan Taliban engaged in unprovoked firing the night before near Kurram as security forces foiled an attempt by terrorists to cross into Pakistan.

On Sept 21, Pakistan, in response to recent terrorist attacks in KP, conducted “calibrated” airstrikes in the border region with Afghanistan against terrorist hideouts and safe havens of terrorist organisations.

A statement from the information ministry on Monday said that over 28 terrorists were eliminated in the strikes. “It is a matter of grave concern that Afghanistan continues to remain a hub of terrorism,” the ministry said at the time, specifying that the “threat to Pakistan emanates from Afghanistan”.

The airstrikes had come after a major attack in the old Police Lines in KP’s Kohat claimed 23 lives and injured about 100 others. Eight terrorists were killed during an overnight clearance operation launched to clear the area.

Ghazab lil-Haq

Information Minister Attaullah Tarar described Monday’s action as part of Pakistan’s ongoing counter-terrorism campaign, Ghazab lil Haq.

On the night of February 26, following unprovoked firing by the Afghan Taliban from across the border, Pakistan launched Operation Ghazab lil Haq against terrorist hideouts.

Pakistan also carried out strikes in the border region with Afghanistan in late June , with the government saying they were in response to a wave of terrorist attacks, including one on a Rangers camp in Karachi .

At the time, Tarar said that 25 terrorists were killed in those strikes in Paktia, Paktika and Kunar.

Pakistan had carried out similar strikes on terrorist hideouts along its border with Afghanistan earlier that month, killing 26 terrorists.

In July, security forces responded to unprovoked firing by the Afghan Taliban at border posts in Kurram, security sources had said. In the same month, the Afghan Taliban regime launched four rudimentary drones across the border into Balochistan, which were shot down by security forces. Two drones were also shot down in June in Qila Abdullah and Chagai districts.

Pak-Afghan ties

As clashes continue, tensions between Islamabad and Kabul have remained high. Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Taliban administration in Kabul to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries on Afghan soil, particularly those linked to the banned TTP, that are used for attacks in Pakistan. Officials say those appeals have gone unheeded.

Earlier this week, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar addressed a meeting of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), where he called for steps towards concrete and verifiable action to prevent the use of Afghan soil for terrorism against any neighbouring country, particularly Pakistan.

Dar said Pakistan was “seriously concerned” about the presence of over two dozen terrorist groups in Afghanistan that threatened regional and international peace and security.

Last week, Pakistan also told the UN Security Council that it would respond to terrorist threats emanating from Afghanistan in self-defence as and when needed and in accordance with international law.

Earlier this month, the Foreign Office (FO) declared that meaningful progress in relations with Kabul would depend on the Taliban taking concrete and verifiable action against Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and other terrorist groups operating from Afghan territory.

It maintained that while Islamabad welcomed China’s continuing engagement, the external facilitation could not substitute for action by Kabul against terrorist infrastructure.

According to a UN Security Council-mandated monitoring report — covering the period from December 16, 2025 to June 9, 2026 — Afg­han Taliban’s continued support for TTP has contributed to a rise in the frequency and lethality of terrorist attacks in Pakistan, even as Kabul has taken some initial steps to rein in the group.

The report also pointed to growing operational and facilitation linkages among the TTP, Al Qaeda, Islamic State-Khorasan (ISIL-K) and the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA).

World.title: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye mull meeting of military chiefs to assist Riyadh under Makkah defence pact: FO
World.content:
The foreign ministers of Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia discussed plans on Friday to convene a meeting of the three countries’ chiefs of staff to explore ways to assist Riyadh under the Makkah Defence Alliance, according to the Foreign Office (FO).

The FO statement noted that the tripartite agreement, signed on Aug 7, stipulated that an attack against any one of its parties should be considered an attack against all parties.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar from Pakistan, Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan bin Abdullah and Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan held a discussion on the defence pact on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.

Earlier, Saudi Foreign Ministry also posted on X that the three member states condemned the recent Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia and discussed arrangements to convene an “urgent meeting of the chiefs of staff of the three countries” to support the Gulf state within the pact.

Later, Turkiye’s Defence Ministry said its Chief of General Staff General Selcuk Bayraktaroglu will travel to Saudi Arabia to meet his Saudi and Pakistani counterparts as part of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement.

In their New York meeting, the foreign ministers condemned in the “strongest terms the heinous attacks targeting the holy city of Makkah and civilian and economic facilities in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia”, the FO statement said.

At the same time, it added, the ministers “commended the vigilance of the Saudi armed forces and their ability to defend the kingdom’s security”.

“They reaffirmed the kingdom’s right to take such measures as it deems appropriate to defend its security, in accordance with Article 51 of the UN Charter.”

They further discussed the current situation in the region, underscoring the importance of upholding the principles of international law, good neighbourliness, mutual respect for the sovereignty of states, and non-interference in their internal affairs, as well as ensuring the security and freedom of navigation, the statement said.

Moreover, they reiterated their determination to work together towards achieving sustainable peace and stability in the region, support efforts towards de-escalation and encourage peaceful resolution to crises.

During the meeting, the ministers also reviewed progress made towards establishing the general secretariat and committees and working groups under the Makkah agreement, as well as preparations for the commencement of their work, the FO statement said.

Earlier in the day, Dar also posted on X: “Under the framework of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement (MJDA), we reviewed progress towards establishing the institutional structures under the agreement and exchanged views on regional and international security issues.”

The Makkah Defence Alliance’s inaugural meeting was held on Aug 31, where officials from all member states met in Istanbul to establish the institutional structure of the alliance, and Pakistan was picked to head its secretariat in Riyadh. Retired Lieutenant General Nauman Mahmood has been appointed as the first secretary general.

The latest meeting in New York in relevance to the defence pact took place against the backdrop of Riyadh being dragged into fresh fighting between the Houthis and the Yemeni government, with the former declaring a maritime blockade on the kingdom and targeting its ships in the Red Sea. In recent weeks, Houthis have also carried out attacks in Saudi Arabia.

A day earlier, Saudi Arabia intercepted six ballistic missiles fired by the Houthis after issuing warnings for several regions, including Makkah. This was the second time that a warning was issued for the holy city in the last two weeks.

As Yemen’s Houthi rebels continue to attack Saudi Arabia, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry on Sept 18 said that Pakistan would go to “any extent” to defend Saudi Arabia, adding that Islamabad’s commitment to the kingdom’s security was “unconditional”.

On Wednesday, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had also vowed to stand “shoulder to shoulder” with Saudi Arabia in safeguarding its sovereignty and security.

Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia’s King Salman this week denounced the Houthis as a “terrorist militia” in a rare statement. He condemned the Houthi attempt “to target Makkah”, calling it “a provocation to Muslims around the world”, according to the official Saudi news agency.

Additional input from Reuters.

World.title: PTI decides to postpone Sept 27 Islamabad long march
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The PTI leadership decided on Friday to postpone its planned long march towards Islamabad, originally scheduled for Sept 27, by more than a week.

The party had been preparing for a nationwide protest and march towards Islamabad on Sept 27 to press for the release of its founder, Imran Khan, who is currently incarcerated in Rawalpindi’s Adiala jail.

Speaking to Dawn, a senior PTI leader, who requested anonymity, said the march will now leave from Peshawar on Oct 4.

He added that Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi would formally announce the postponement soon.

“There was a proposal to exhaust the federal government and law enforcement agencies, as they have already closed down the federal capital and a number of routes,” he said.

The leader claimed that the PTI had already achieved what it wanted to do via the march.

“They have closed down roads and are spending hundreds of millions on law enforcement,” he noted.

Asked if the PTI intended to march alongside the Jamaat-i-Islami (JI), which had postponed its own protest march against the petroleum levy on the request of the premier, the leader said that the decision had nothing to do with them.

“We are capable of arranging the march on our own,” he said.

The development comes a day after a PTI leader had hinted at the possibility of postponing its protest march if the federal government agreed to hold elections within six to eight months, release Imran and other political prisoners, and investigate the May 9 and November 26 crackdowns on the opposition party.

Advocate Naeem Haider Panjutha told Dawn that the protest could be postponed if these three assurances were given by the government.

Party spokesperson Sheikh Waqas Akram, however, had denied any such proposal was being discussed at any party forum, saying only Imran could take a decision even if such a proposal was on the table.

Preparations in the Rawalpindi Division and the federal capital territory to maintain security and deal with any emergency situation have been in full swing in light of the potential long march and other protests in Islamabad.

Punjab has already imposed a ban on gatherings across the province for 13 days and prohibited inciting people to “unlawful assembly”. A similar ban under Section 144 has been enforced in Islamabad for two months.

The Punjab government has also sent a letter to the interior ministry requesting mobile and internet services at specific locations in Rawalpindi and Attock to be downgraded or jam­med on Sept 27.

Meanwhile, the federal government on Thursday approved the deployment of Rangers in Islamabad and several districts of Punjab from Sept 20 to Oct 5.

“The deployed troops may respond appropriately in self-defence to any threats or violent activities encountered in the course of their duties as per rules/regulations in vogue,” the notification stated.

Tarar takes aim at KP govt for ‘facilitating terrorism’

Addressing a press conference on Friday, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar slammed the KP government, accusing it of avoiding taking steps to maintain law and order in the province.

He alleged that they also gave “full facilitation” to terrorists and called their policy on law and order “evasive”.

“In one way or another, terrorists have attacked all political parties in KP,” the minister said.

“But the PTI is held in high regard by terrorists. And not only do they avoid condemning terrorists, but they also fully avoid taking any sort of action against them. Facilitating terrorists is part of their policy.”

He called KP’s PTI government the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan’s (TTP) “B-team”, and Tehreek-i-Taliban Afghanistan’s (TTA) “C-team”, claiming that it was facilitating the TTP while also “representing” the TTA.

He also took aim at KP CM Afridi specifically, saying he “looks less like a chief minister and more like a TTP commander, in both his words and actions”.

“When drones are fired at Kohat from Afghanistan, and the Pakistan Army and Air Force very skilfully take them down, you will not see any sort of condemnation or statement from KP government,” Tarar claimed.

“When there is firing from Afghanistan in Kurram … you will never see them go to Kurram and say ‘We have come here, we stand with our forces, and we will not tolerate such firing under any circumstances’.”

He termed this a sign of cowardice from CM Afridi, his cabinet and his entire KP government, adding that this was also the reason they were “running away” from protests.

“They are not even prepared. I’ve just come from KP. They don’t have any sort of preparations,” the minister said.

“Come and protest, if you have the courage,” he said.

He stressed that the provincial government was in charge of controlling law and order, highlighting that 2,456 terror attacks had taken place in KP in 2026 — around 10 a day on average. He added that 472 police, army, rangers, and FC personnel were martyred and over 1,500 people injured this year.

The information minister asserted that the reason the KP government did not want to fix the law and order situation was to maintain a “political terror-crime nexus” and illegal trade and mining activities in the province, through which they “funded terrorists”.

“A provincial government which doesn’t want to stop terrorism and fix law and order, and countless citizens lose their lives — this cannot be justified in any part of the world,” he said.

World.title: Lawyer challenges Islamabad-Peshawar Motorway closure in IHC
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: A lawyer moved the Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Friday against the closure of the Islamabad-Peshawar Motorway (M-1) and sought directions to reopen the blocked routes for lawyers, litigants and emergency services.

The government announced the motorway’s closure earlier this week as it stepped up arrangements to prevent the PTI from marching on Islamabad.

The march was part of the party’s planned nationwide protest to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan, and mobilise people for the supremacy of the Constitution. The protest was originally planned for Sept 27, but the party has now reportedly deferred it.

Advocate Mian Shafqat Jan, a lawyer of the Supreme Court, filed a petition on Friday against the government’s move to shutdown the M-1 Motorway after he was unable to reach the Peshawar High Court (PHC) to appear in a case due to the closure.

According to the petition, the lawyer was scheduled to appear before the PHC on Sept 24. He managed to enter the motorway from the Islamabad toll plaza at around 7am after facing difficulties but found the route closed at the M-1 Attock Bridge.

The petitioner said he sought information from officials deployed at the site about any written order authorising the closure but was unable to obtain a confirmation.

He contended that closing public routes without a notification, written order or disclosed reasons infringed citizens’ fundamental rights and warranted judicial intervention.

The petition named the federation through the interior and information secretaries, the inspectors general of the National Highways and Motorway Police and Islamabad Police, the National Highway Authority through its chairman, the Islamabad Capital Territory administration through the chief commissioner, and the Punjab government through its home secretary and inspector general of police as respondents.

The petitioner also referred to a recent IHC judgement about the planned PTI protest, arguing that the court had recognised constitutional protections for citizens, including freedom of movement and access to courts.

In its detailed 37-page judgement in the case pertaining to the PTI’s planned protest, the IHC held that any activity resulting in the infringement of citizens’ fundamental rights amounted to a violation of the Constitution. It also observed that the right to peaceful assembly could not be exercised in a manner that infringed the rights of other citizens.

The bench, headed by Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar and comprising Justice Muhammad Azam Khan and Justice Muhammad Asif, directed the authorities to ensure that no political party, leader or public office holder occupied roads, highways, interchanges or toll plazas in a manner that obstructed free movement or hindered access to medical and educational facilities.

On the basis of these arguments, Advocate Jan urged the high court in his plea to declare the closure of roads and highways without any notification, written order or disclosed reasons illegal and unconstitutional.

He has also sought directions for the interior secretary, communications secretary and Islamabad chief commissioner to ensure the reopening of blocked routes for emergency traffic, lawyers, litigants, witnesses, sick persons, funeral processions and other emergency services.

According to the National Highways and Motorway Police (NHMP), the M-1 has been closed to all traffic in both directions between the Islamabad Toll Plaza and Chhachh Interchange, while the M-14 was closed from Hakla to Kundal. The GT Road was also closed at Attock Khurd.

The government had also decided to close the Islamabad-Dera Ismail Khan Motorway (M14) — also known as the CPEC road — and GT Road.

Security arrangements were also intensified in Attock, with containers and sandbags placed at key bridges and security tightened at major entry and exit points, as authorities prepared for the PTI protest.

The federal government also approved the deployment of Rangers in Islamabad and several districts of Punjab ahead of the PTI’s planned march on the federal capital.

Punjab has already imposed a ban on gatherings across the province for 13 days and prohibited inciting people to “unlawful assembly”. A similar ban under Section 144 has been enforced in Islamabad as well for two months.

Gatherings in the federal capital are also banned under the Peaceful Assembly and Public Order Act 2024 , which had been rushed through the National Assembly amidst the opposition’s outcry ahead of a PTI gathering .

Meanwhile, Section 144 has also been imposed in Karachi, Hyderabad, Sukkur and Balochistan.

The Punjab government had also sent a letter to the federal interior ministry requesting mobile and internet services at specific locations in Rawalpindi and Attock to be downgraded or jammed on Sept 27 due to the “expected law and order situation”.

World.title: Indian police use tear gas against protesters seeking election chief's ouster
World.content:
Indian police used tear gas and water cannons on Friday to disperse opposition Congress party members during nationwide protests demanding the resignation of the head of the election commission, whom they accuse of manipulating voter rolls.

The “cockroach” youth movement, which counts millions of supporters and forced the education minister out in July, said it would launch protests across India on Oct 2 if Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar does not resign by Saturday.

The protests, which are backed by other opposition groups, mark a new political challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi as Kumar, 62, a former civil servant, was appointed to head the independent Election Commission of India by Modi’s government.

“Theft of votes is happening across the country,” local Congress party leader Amarinder Singh Raja said in Chandigarh in the northwest, one of at least two places where police fired water cannon after protesters climbed buses and barricades.

Congress and other opposition parties have accused the eleciton commission of colluding with Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) to manipulate voter lists and win state elections in recent years, charges both the commission and the BJP have denied. Kumar himself has not commented.

Newspaper reports dissent within the commission

In at least a dozen of India’s 28 states, Congress supporters shouted slogans against Kumar, held up posters demanding his arrest and in one instance, burned an effigy of him and Modi.

In the capital Delhi, hundreds of protesters climbed barricades and hurled insults at a man wearing a Kumar mask.

The demonstrations were triggered by a report in the Indian Express newspaper on Wednesday that Kumar’s deputies had questioned him over changes to voter lists that opposition groups say benefit Modi’s BJP.

“For three years, I have been exposing vote theft. Now, the election commissioners themselves are acknowledging it and bringing the truth to light,” Congress leader Rahul Gandhi said late on Thursday, referring to Kumar’s deputies.

“Gyanesh Kumar has committed treason. He should resign immediately,” he added.

The Election Commission said differences among officers were normal in any institution and that all its actions were lawful. The BJP dismissed the report and said that opposition parties were indulging in a smear campaign because popular support for the BJP meant they lost elections.

State elections next year — including in the most populous state, Uttar Pradesh, and Modi’s home state of Gujarat, both ruled by the BJP — are key tests of support ahead of parliamentary elections due in 2029.

World.title: FBR sets up faceless tax audit, assessment centre in Islamabad
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) has established the National Faceless Centre in Islamabad, under which audits and assessments will be handled by “faceless” wings to reduce official discretion and direct contact between tax officials and taxpayers.

The initiative has been taken under Pakistan’s New Tax Operating Model and was approved by the government in principle in June.

The centralised and faceless tax model is similar to systems used in the UK, Australia, the Netherlands, Singapore and India. It is designed to eliminate physical contact between tax authorities and taxpayers to prevent corruption.

The decision to establish the National Faceless Centre was taken the Board in Council — a body headed by the FBR chairperson — in its meeting on Friday, an FBR statement said.

It described NFC as a major reform that “changes how tax audits and assessments are carried out in Pakistan”.

Until now, a taxpayer whose return was picked for audit had to deal with a particular officer in a particular office, often in person. Under the new system, that contact ends.

Cases will be selected by a computerised, risk-based system rather than by any officer. Each case will then be assigned automatically to an officer who may be sitting anywhere in the country. The taxpayer will not know who the officer is, and the officer will have no say in which case comes to them.

Every case will pass through three separate hands. One officer will conduct the audit, a second will make the assessment, and a third will review the work for quality before any order is issued. No single officer will control a taxpayer’s case from start to finish.

All notices, replies and hearings will take place electronically through FBR’s IRIS system, and where the law requires a physical verification or recovery, it will be carried out by a separate field team, the statement detailed.

The NFC draws its legal authority from the Finance Act, 2026.

It will be headed by an Inland Revenue chief commissioner, with dedicated wings for faceless audit, faceless assessment, quality control and field operations. A Programme Management Unit has already been set up to oversee its rollout.

“The purpose of the reform is same rules for every taxpayer, decisions based on data rather than personal judgement, and an end to the face to face contact that has long been a source of complaints. FBR expects the NFC to make tax proceedings faster, fairer and more transparent for taxpayers across Pakistan,” the statement said.

World.title: 'Tremendous things will be happening': Trump hails 'very productive' meeting with China's Xi
World.content:
US President Donald Trump on Friday concluded his “productive” meeting with Chinese President XI Jinping, noting in a post on Truth Social that “tremendous things will be happening”.

“Like almost everyone else, he seemed to like calling the poorly and inaccurately named artificial intelligence to a far more accurate and important name: super intelligence. That would be ‘super!’ Everyone last night agreed, also,” he wrote.

The lavish state summit at the White House appeared heavy on symbolism but light on substance, with no sign of major breakthroughs between the world’s biggest economies.

Still, Trump highlighted progress under a bilateral trade mechanism, citing what he described as increased market access for US farmers and ranchers, while both leaders identified artificial intelligence as an area for cooperation.

Trump would follow up his summit with Xi by taking the Chinese leader to the US National Archives, where they were expected to stress views about the history and direction of ties between their countries.

A newspaper featuring a front page photo of China’s President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump, at a White House welcome ceremony, is seen at a news stand in Beijing on September 25, 2026. —AFP

Trump said in remarks welcoming Xi that they would see some of the greatest treasures of US history at the National Archives, including the Declaration of Independence, the US Constitution and the Bill of Rights.

They would also see “artifacts testifying to the long and cherished relationship” between China and the United States and their “cultural exchanges”, he said.

“Just as our ancestors reached across the ocean centuries ago to trade, to learn, and to build a better world, our two countries do really the same thing, and we’re very proud of it and the relationship,” Trump said.

China has not commented on the visit to the archives, but analysts say Xi may be keen to see records relating to the US switch of recognition to communist China from Taiwan in 1979.

China presses on Taiwan

Xi has long sought to persuade Trump to state publicly that the United States opposes Taiwan’s independence, rather than saying only that it does not support independence, which has been Washington’s formulation for decades.

He is also keen to get the US to halt arms sales to the island.

As expected, Xi pressed Trump on Taiwan on Thursday, saying he hoped the United States would “handle the Taiwan question with prudence.” China’s state news agency also reported that Xi “hopes the US side will adhere to the correct position of opposing ‘Taiwan independence’.”

While the United States, like most countries, has no formal diplomatic relations with Taipei, Washington is its most important international backer and is bound by US law to provide it with the means to defend itself.

America’s Asian allies will watch closely to see how Trump talks about Taiwan following Xi’s visit.

After his May summit with Xi, Trump, whose administration in December approved an $11 billion arms sale package to Taiwan, said he was holding a second package, worth some $14bn, in abeyance and described it as a “very good negotiating chip.” Craig Singleton of the Foundation for Defence of Democracies think tank said Beijing may believe it has established a new baseline on Taiwan with Trump.

(L-R) China’s First Lady Peng Liyuan, China’s President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump and US First Lady Melania Trump look on during a military review in the Rose Garden of the White House in Washington, DC, on September 24, 2026. —AFP

He said Xi’s use of the word “adhere” was revealing because “it implies Beijing believes Washington is already behaving in ways it wants.”

“In the context of the current stand-down on Taiwan arms sales, China may increasingly view that restraint as a new baseline rather than a temporary pause,” he said.

“Beijing’s objective is to get Trump to absorb Chinese red lines into his own definition of a stable relationship.”

On Thursday, Senate Democrats criticised the summit, saying Trump had failed to secure meaningful concessions from Beijing on trade, security, artificial intelligence or human rights.

They also criticised Trump for failing to publicly address China’s military pressure on Taiwan and called for the immediate delivery of approved military aid and arms sales to the island.

World.title: Delegate walkout, protests greet Netanyahu as he addresses UN General Assembly
World.content:
NEW YORK: Dozens of delegates walked out of the UN General Assembly hall on Thursday as hundreds of protesters gathered outside the building while Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu defended Tel Aviv’s actions amid growing international isolation, with elections looming that could threaten his political future.

The walkout undersco­red the competing pressu­res facing Netanyahu, who is battling mounting criticism abroad over the Gaza conflict while campaigning for re-election at home ahead of an October 27 vote.

On Thursday, Netanyahu delivered a combative address inside the General Assembly, where dozens of delegations walked out as he began speaking.

The departing diplomats left large sections of the hall empty, creating a striking contrast with Netanyahu’s attempt to use the podium to present Israel’s case before the international community.

Netanyahu responded by accusing his critics of hypocrisy and calling them “moral cowards.”

He rejected allegations that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza, saying Israel had prevented rather than committed genocide. He defended the country’s military actions in Gaza and elsewhere in the region.

Delegates walk out of the General Assembly hall as Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu arrives to address the 81st United Nations General Assembly at UN headquarters in New York City, US, September 24. — Reuters

He also devoted a significant part of his speech to New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, calling him “the antisemitic mayor of New York” and accusing him of spreading what Netanyahu described as lies about Israel.

Mamdani, who had declined to join the street protests, responded after the speech.

“Prime Minister Netanyahu used his speech to repeat baseless lies meant to sanitise his genocide of Palestinians,” Mamdani said.

“No lie can change the fact that he remains the subject of an International Criminal Court arrest warrant alleging war crimes and crimes against humanity.”

Mamdani previously said New York City lacked the authority to enforce the ICC warrant against Netanyahu, arguing that the appropriate authorities should carry it out.

On Wednesday night, the mayor had hosted Palestinian families from Gaza at Gracie Mansion and planted an olive tree with them, saying: “May peace be our future.”

The two scenes — protesters confronting his government’s policies on the streets and diplomats leaving the hall during his address — turned Netanyahu’s brief visit to New York into a day of parallel confrontation.

Netanyahu’s stay had already been sharply shortened amid security concerns and expectations of protests. He arrived on Thursday morning, addressed the General Assembly and was scheduled to return to Israel the same evening rather than remain in New York overnight.

Outside the UN, Jewish and Muslim activists, Palestinian supporters, human-rights campaigners, progressive Jewish groups, politicians, artists and musicians took part in separate demonstrations across Manhattan. Their messages varied, but opposition to Netanyahu’s government and Israel’s conduct of the Gaza conflict brought many of them into the streets at the same time.

Demonstrators protest after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s address to the United Nations 81st General Assembly in New York City, U.S., September 24. — Reuters

The protests also offered a visible glimpse of a generational shift in American attitudes toward Israel and Netanyahu. While support for Israel remains stronger among older Americans, younger Americans have become substantially more critical of the Israeli government.

A Pew Research Centre survey conducted in May found that only 18 per cent of Americans aged 18 to 29 had a favourable view of the Israeli government, compared with 47pc among those aged 65 and older. Among the youngest Americans, 58pc expressed a favourable view of Palestinians, compared with 47pc among those 65 and older.

That generational divide was visible on the streets of New York, where many of the demonstrators were young people, including students, activists, artists and younger politicians.

The largest direct action outside the UN was organised by Jewish Voice for Peace, whose New York chapter brought hundreds of protesters to First Avenue and 39th Street. Demonstrators wearing matching white T-shirts sat in the roadway, chanting against Netanyahu and calling for an end to US support for Israel.

For a while, protesters stood and sat in the street, linking arms and blocking traffic as police moved in to clear the roadway. The chants continued as officers began making arrests.

At least 30 people, including actors and politicians, were arrested in the initial action. Police later said more than 100 protesters had been taken into custody.
